news.abstract: After 50 years as a stalwart U.S. ally, South Korea is now one of the administration's biggest foreign policy problems.
news.title: U.S. Ties With Seoul Strained by Troop Presence and North Korea

news.abstract: Zapatista rebels are stirring on eve of ninth anniversary of their armed uprising against Mexican government and its free-trade accord with United States; North American Free Trade Agreement eliminates tariffs on most agricultural goods on Jan 1; across Mexico, people fear that flood of cheaper, government-subsidized American exports will ruin hundreds of Mexican farmers (M)
news.title: Mexican Officials Report Threats by Zapatista Rebels

news.abstract: Russia will shut down mission in Chechnya of Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe, ending any permanent international monitoring in republic after mission's mandate ends tonight (M)
news.title: Russia to Shut Monitoring By Europeans In Chechnya

news.abstract: TURKEY: Change Opens Door For Popular Politician; BOSNIA: U.N. Cedes Police Role To Europe; BRITAIN: Deal On London Tube Overhaul; ITALY: Volcano Aftermath On Isle; FRANCE: Effects Of Spanish Spill;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: US Army acts to send thousands more soldiers from Third Infantry Division in Georgia to Kuwait in largest single ground deployment to Persian Gulf since war there in 1991; one of division's three combat brigades, about 4,000 soldiers, has been training in Kuwaiti desert since September, but unit's headquarters at Fort Stewart, Ga, receives order within last day directing rest of more than 15,000 combat troops to join soldiers in Kuwait; photo (M)
news.title: ARMY ACTS TO ADD THOUSANDS OF G.I.'S TO ITS GULF FORCE

news.abstract: Chinese authorities intensify efforts to suppress protesters in country's restive northeast, just week after releasing Xu Wenli, country's most prominent political prisoner, and sending him to United States; police charge two leaders of worker demonstrations in city of Liaoyang with subversion, crime that carries death penalty, after they organize protests to focus attention on workers' interests; China's decision to release Xu, who has pushed for greter democracy in China since late 1970's and has spent 16 of past 21 years in prison, was greeted as significant concession to US and Western critics of its human rights record; but Western rights groups warned that releases of prominent dissidents are mixed blessing, often leading to fresh crackdowns on less-well-known protesters (M)
news.title: China Cracks Down on Protests After Sending Dissident to U.S.

news.abstract: The investigation into recent attacks in Yemen suggests a cell of Islamic militants has been planning to target other foreigners as well.
news.title: Inquiry Into Attacks in Yemen Suggests Wider Plot, Official Says

news.abstract: International Herald Tribune appears for first time under sole ownership and management of The New York Times Co; takeover ends 35-year partnership between The Times and The Washington Post that produced journalistic hybrid consisting mainly of articles and editorials from both papers compiled by editors in Paris; The Times bought The Post's 50 percent stake for $70 million; beginning Jan 2, contents of The Tribune will come increasingly from staff of The Times, with continued contributions by international paper's own small staff and dwindling number of articles from The Post and other newspapers in United States; international paper's name and appearance will stay same, and its headquarters will remain in Neuilly-sur-Seine, suburb of Paris; Howell Raines, executive editor of The Times, will oversee news operations of The Tribune (M)
news.title: International Herald Tribune Now Run Solely by The Times

news.abstract: China plans to launch a manned capsule into orbit around Earth by the end of the year, official media reported today.
news.title: China Planning a Manned Space Mission for 2003

news.abstract: The United States will permit Mexico to sell tuna under the "dolphin safe" label, ending a 12-year-old embargo.
news.title: U.S. to Let Mexico Sell 'Dolphin Safe' Tuna

news.abstract: North Korea's top diplomat in Beijing blamed the U.S. for his country's decision to re-start its nuclear program.
news.title: North Korea Defends Decision to Re-Start Nuclear Program

news.abstract: Israeli children get lessons at school on donning gas masks in case of Iraqi attack in response to US military action against Saddam Hussein; photo of instruction in fourth-grade classroom in Jerusalem; psychologist Dr Bilha Noy observes that children in Israel lose some of their innocence in having to prepare for such events (M)
news.title: For Israeli Schoolchildren, Lessons in Gas Masks as Well as Geography

news.abstract: North Korea's top diplomat in Beijing blamed the U.S. for his country's decision to restart its nuclear program.
news.title: North Korea Defends Decision to Restart Nuclear Program

news.abstract: Bashiqa Journal on Iraqi village of Yazidis, sect of ethnic Kurds who follow eclectic faith that mingles Islam, Christianity and Zoroastrianism, along with some obscure practices like fierce prohibition on eating lettuce; surrounding hills are dominated by spired conical tombs of sect that suffered ruthless persecution under Ottomans; photos; map; armies and empires have crisscrossed Iraq for thousands of years, leaving remnants of spectacular civilizations and people who seem to date from long forgotten time (M)
news.title: Bashiqa Journal; A Sect Shuns Lettuce and Gives the Devil His Due

news.abstract: Iraq says UN weapons inspectors who have visited some 230 sites have thus far failed to find any weapons of mass destruction or evidence of other prohibited programs (S)
news.title: Iraq Says U.N. Teams Have Found No Weapons

news.abstract: Local authorities in Wales plan to take Cardigan Castle and turn it into museum and tourist attraction now that its owner, Barbara Wood, who has jealously kept them at bay, is moved to retirement home; lawyer who claims to have power of attorney over her affairs refuses to hand property over and has offered it for sale for $1.28 million; photos (M)
news.title: The Poor Woman Is Gone And Her Castle's Besieged

news.abstract: Two British police officers are charged with possessing and distributing indecent images of children, and one is charged with indecent assault on two girls under 16 (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: Officers Face Child Sex Charges

news.abstract: Thousands of people in six Pakistani cities protest against possible American attack on Iraq at rallies organized by coalition of hard-line religious parties; rallies are relatively modest by Pakistani standards; photo (M)
news.title: Small Crowds Of Pakistanis Stage Protests Against U.S.

news.abstract: PARIS:—  The British Medical Journal touched off a major controversy Friday when it published an article charging that pharmaceutical companies had invented a new condition called female sexual dysfunction so they could create a vast new market for drugs to treat it.
news.title: Drug firms accused of devising women's malady

news.abstract: Pres-elect Roh Moo Hyun of South Korea is preparing compromise proposal that would require both North Korea and US to accept concessions to resolve standoff over North's nuclear program; North Korea renews its call for US to reopen talks with it, but US State Department says North Korea must first stop its two programs to build nuclear bombs; photo (M)
news.title: New Seoul Leader to Press U.S. and North to Yield a Bit

news.abstract: New debate about whether Cuba is threat to American national security is set off by recent discoveries by federal investigators of Cuban espionage activities, including operation that penetrated Pentagon's intelligence agency; since 1988, FBI has exposed network of at least 16 accused or convicted Cuban spies who succeeded in penetrating several exile groups and worked to get inside American military installations; success appears to have been mixed; debate pits administration officials who want to pressure Castro government against bipartisan Congressional leaders who are trying to ease restrictions on Cuba; recent spy cases cited; intelligence officials say Cuba might still have as many as several hundred officers and agents operating in US; contend they are among most aggressive intelligence agents; photo (M)
news.title: White House Wary of Cuba's Little Spy Engine That Could

news.abstract: Finland's Sibelius Academy has launched startling number of conductors who have gone on to prestigious podiums around world; country provides large subsidies for education for composers and performers; photos (M)
news.title: Finland's Bold Musical Ambitions Produce a Multitude of Maestros

news.abstract: Political factions in Kuwait are carefully monitoring looming possibility of war next door, and weighing what overthrow of Saddam Hussein and refashioning of Iraq would mean for competing reformist and Islamic trends at home; photo (M)
news.title: Kuwaiti Political Combatants Hold Breath for Iraq Outcome

news.abstract: Intensely devout, armed and nationalistic tribes of Iraq are under increased scrutiny as Bush administration casts about for some credible force that can help it oust Saddam Hussein; country is home to about 150 major tribes, with largest numbering more than million people and smallest a few thousand; question now is how deep their professed loyalty to Hussein runs; map; photo (M)
news.title: In Iraq's Tribes, U.S. Faces a Formidable Wild Card

news.abstract: Venezuelan Foreign Min Roy Chaderton accuses strike leaders of shutting down heart of nation's economy in effort to overthrow government, but regrets violence that erupted during recent march against Pres Hugo Chavez; news reports says two men were killed when protest turned into street fight that lasted most of day; Chaderton says Chavez is trying to prevent repeat of last April's coup attempt when he was forced by military to leave office after violent demonstrations; photo (M)
news.title: Venezuelan Minister Says Chávez Won't Give In to Strikers

news.abstract: Two suicide bombers commit deadliest attack against Israel in 10 months, blowing themselves up just seconds apart in downtown area of Tel Aviv; 23 are killed and 100 more injured; area is crowded with foreign laborers and Sunday evening shoppers; spokesman for Al Aksa Martyrs Brigades, Palestinian militant organization, claims responsibility; Israeli reprisals begin, with gunships entering skies over Gaza and rocketing Palestinian positions there; Prime Min Ariel Sharon's cabinet meets in emergency session; rescue teams encounter scene of horrific carnage; say two bombs appear to be unusually large and were packed with nails and ball bearings and hunks of metal to sharpen their effect; photos; map (M)
news.title: Pair of Bombers Kill 23 in Israel; Reprisals Begin

news.abstract: United Nations weapons inspectors in Iraq make dramatic use of their authority, closing exits and entrances to any site where they are working and confining thousands of people at sprawling government research complex, including Iraqi ambassador to UN, for almost six hours; Amb Mohammed Aldouri, fuming with anger, calls inspection team's action 'unjustified' and says they should have acted in more civilized way; events underscore way both sides are stepping up pressure in dwindling time before first official assessment in inspectors' work; photos (M)
news.title: Inspectors Close Exits At Research Site for Hours, Confining Thousands

news.abstract: Kenya's new government began revamping policies today, starting with public education and past human rights violations.
news.title: Kenya's New Government Begins Revamping Policies

news.abstract: Three men sought accused of plotting to trade drugs for antiaircraft missiles agreed today to their extradition.
news.title: 3 Terror Suspects Agree to Extradition to U.S.

news.abstract: Streets of Caracas become scene of mass funeral procession as thousands of supporters of Pres Hugo Chavez denounce violence stemming from monthlong strike aimed at forcing him from power; marchers escort coffins of two men killed in clashes between government opponents and pro-Chavez groups; Vice Pres Jose Vicente Rangel and several other high-level government officials lead procession; fear of civil war grows; photo (M)
news.title: Thousands March at Rites for 2 Slain in Clashes in Venezuela

news.abstract: Kenya's new Pres Mwai Kibaki immediately acts to fulfill campaign pledge to make primary schools free; students find overflowing classrooms in some parts of country as parents who could not afford to send their children to class under old policy take advantage of new rules; some schools are unable to enroll all who seek to register; authorities agree to take down names of those who are left out and to help them enroll next year; photo (M)
news.title: Primary Schools in Kenya, Fees Abolished, Are Filled to Overflowing

news.abstract: Three men sought by FBI for allegedly plotting to trade drugs for antiaircraft missiles agree to their extradition to United States from Hong Kong; men reportedly told FBI undercover agents in Hong Kong that they hoped to resell Stinger missiles to Al Qaeda; men, two Pakistanis and an American, do not say why they have dropped their opposition to extradition, but officials in Hong Kong have stessed they would have no tolerance for terrorism; men are Ilyas Ali, Syed Saadat Ali Faraz and Muhammad Abid Afridi (M)
news.title: 3 in Hong Kong Agree to Face Charges in U.S.

news.abstract: BRITAIN: Crackdown On Gun Possession; NORTHERN IRELAND: Bomb Found At School;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Shopping mall geared to older shoppers is big hit in Tokyo, Japan, doing booming business in otherwise flat economy; it defies practice of letting young set trends in retailing, offering displays of old-fashioned toys and catering to nostalgia for optimistic era when country was booming; photos (M)
news.title: Tokyo Journal; Hot New Marketing Concept: Mall as Memory Lane

news.abstract: Israel's leaders forbid Palestinian leaders to leave country for talks in London, as much of rest of Israel takes day to mourn its dead following pair of deadly suicide attacks; talks in London, being sponsored by Prime Min Tony Blair, are intended to encourage Palestinian leadership to become more democratic and less corrupt; Israeli officials also order closing of three Palestinian universities; Israeli tanks and helicopters continue military operations in Gaza Strip, where they say they killed one Palestinian gunman; photos; map (M)
news.title: Israel Won't Let Palestinian Leaders Attend London Talks

news.abstract: PAKISTAN: Religious Coalition Seeks Islamic Law; CHINA: Amusement At U.S. Charges; JAPAN: Premier Vows To Press Reforms;.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: Number of Jews in France who moved to Israel more than doubled last year to 2,566, highest number since 1972; most are between 16 and 35 and have college degrees; anti-Semitic attacks in France cited, such as recent stabbing of Rabbi Gabriel Farhi (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: France: More Jews Leaving For Israel

news.abstract: Danish scientific panel concludes that Prof Bjorn Lomborg displayed 'scientific dishonesty' in popular book The Skeptical Environmentalist, which offers upbeat analysis of environmental trends; Lomborg says book is unbiased refutation of dire pronouncements by environmental groups; many experts say conditions are not as good as Lomborg says, but also not as bad as some environmentalists claim (M)
news.title: Environment And Science: Danes Rebuke A 'Skeptic'

news.abstract: Britain calls up 1,500 reservists to join active troops for possible military action against Iraq; Sec Geoff Hoon also announces reinforcing of naval task force in Persian Gulf; Prime Min Tony Blair tells gathering of British diplomats that standing by US is 'massively' in British self-interest; photo; says price of influence is not leaving US to face 'tricky issues alone' and denounces anti-Americanism as 'foolish indulgence'; pledges at same time to urge Bush administration to broaden agenda, saying active pursuit of Mideast peace is essential to winning Arab support against Saddam Hussein; Pres Jacques Chirac tells French troops to stand by, saying UN weapons resolutions must be enforced, but also warns US against precipitate action; more US war planners leave US Central Command in Tampa for Qatar; Blair urges Israeli Prime Min Ariel Sharon to reconsider barring Palestinians from traveling to London meeting; ban was ordered after suicide bombings killed 22 people in Tel Aviv (M)
news.title: Britain Calls Up 1,500 Reservists For Possible Action Against Iraq

news.abstract: Thousands of Iraqi men and women who have just completed basic military training march through provincial capital of Baquba to show support for Saddam Hussein; map; parade follows bellicose Hussein speech denouncing UN arms inspectors as spies (M)
news.title: A Spiffy Army of Volunteers Parades in Praise of Hussein

news.abstract: Chilean judge orders detention of former minister Carlos Cruz, longtime associate of Pres Ricardo Lagos, and two other officials on bribery charges (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Chile: Ex-Aide To President Faces Bribe Charge

news.abstract: INDIA-PAKISTAN NUCLEAR COMPETITION; SRI LANKA: Some Progress In Talks;.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: LONDON, Jan. 9 — Britain said today that Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon had rebuffed Prime Minister Tony Blair's personal appeal to reconsider Israel's decision to keep Palestinian negotiators from attending a British-sponsored conference in London next week. A spokesman for Mr. Blair vowed that some form of talks would go ahead as scheduled despite the Israeli ban.
news.title: Sharon Rebuffed Appeal on Palestinian Talks, Britain Says

news.abstract: Hans Blix said today that Iraq's report was "devoid of any new evidence" that the country had no banned weapons.
news.title: Iraq Gave No New Evidence in Arms Report, Inspector Says

news.abstract: Some 10,000 people took the streets in the eastern city of Hefei this week to protest problems with traffic safety.
news.title: Huge Demonstration in China, but Subject Is Traffic Safety

news.abstract: President Bush conferred with President Jiang Zemin today on North Korea's decision to withdraw from an arms treaty.
news.title: U.S. and China Agree to Work Together on North Korea

news.abstract: Rwanda plans to release up to 40,000 detainees who have been held for years for reported involvement in 1994 mass killings (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Rwanda: Detainees To Be Freed

news.abstract: Spanish Prime Min Jose Maria Aznar's wife, Ana Botella, announces her candidacy in Madrid's municipal election on ticket of governing Popular Party; she was offered No. 3 slot by mayoral candidate for Madrid, Alberto Ruiz-Gallardon, who has been mentioned as possible successor to Aznar when his term is up in 2004 (S)
news.title: Spanish Premier's Wife Becomes Candidate

news.abstract: Chief United Nations weapons inspectors sharply criticize Iraq for failing to come forward with new information to clarify its weapons program, but say they have 'not found any smoking gun' indicating that Baghdad is concealing illegal weapons; American officials seize on inspectors' report as new proof that Iraq is not cooperating with inspections as required by Security Council resolutions; American diplomats suggest they will step up pressure at UN for military action if Iraq does not change by end of month; Hans Blix, one of two chief inspectors, says declaration Iraq presented in December is lengthy but lacks much new information; says Baghdad has given 'inadequate response' to demand for complete list of Iraqi weapons experts; Dr Mohamed ElBaradei, director general of International Atomic Energy Agency, says aluminum tubes Baghdad tried to import were intended to build rockets and not centrifuges to enrich uranium; Bush administration has cited tubes as central piece of evidence for its claim that Pres Saddam Hussein is trying to restart nuclear arms program; inspections chiefs cast serious doubt on Iraq's cooperation so far; photo (M)
news.title: U.N. Inspectors Criticize Iraqis Over Arms List

news.abstract: Indian Prime Min Atal Bihar Vajpayee says government plans legislation to permit dual citizenship for Indians in United States, Britain, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Singapore (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: India: Plans For Dual Citizenship

news.abstract: Bill Richardson, newly sworn in as New Mexico governor, takes on unexpected role in effort to defuse nuclear confrontation involving North Korea at request of Han Song Ryol, one of North Korea's United Nations envoys; two have known each other for years; Richardson, who has visited North Korea in past as negotiator, stresses he acts unofficially, passing along data to State Sec Colin L Powell; makes clear that he does not ignore state problems; photo (M)
news.title: Unexpected Appointment in Gov. Richardson's Datebook

news.abstract: Republican congressional leaders say Congress will eliminate three special-interest provisions that caused furor when they were introduced anonymously into domestic security law last year; one limits liability of vaccine makers, idea that Sen Bill Frist says he still supports; second allows contracts with US companies that move overseas to avoid taxes; third creates domestic security research center in way that gives preference to Texas institutions (M)
news.title: G.O.P. Leaders Promise Repeal Of Provisions Hidden in Bill

news.abstract: United States Trade Rep Robert B Zoellick is expected to face street protests and officials concerned about American policies on generic versions of patented AIDS drugs and farm subsidies when he visits southern Africa to discuss free trade accords; African officials are upset that Pres Bush scrapped plans to attend Africa Trade and Economic Cooperation Forum, Mauritius, and is instead sending junior cabinet member (M)
news.title: U.S. Official to Discuss Trade; Africa Hopes to Discuss AIDS

news.abstract: United States officials and industry experts say strike that has virtually shut down Venezuela's oil industry is creating major complications for Bush administration's drive to oust Iraqi Pres Saddam Hussein, causing oil shortages that would probably make war in Iraq more costly to economy than expected; officials say distrust of American diplomats hampers efforts to end stalemate between Pres Hugo Chavez and his opponents; crisis could be compounded if Chavez follows through on proposal to split government-owned oil company, Petroleos de Venezuela SA, into two parts and restructure its central offices; US sees him seeking to replace managers and union leaders with political loyalists, making company less efficient, cutting output and making US even more dependent on Middle Eastern oil; graph of US petroleum imports; photos (M)
news.title: Venezuela Crisis Complicates Iraq Situation, Experts Say

news.abstract: North Korea's nuclear arms crisis echoes nation's 1993-94 threat to pull out of Nuclear Nonproliferation Treaty; United States response to threat recalled (S)
news.title: Korea Crisis: Same Song, Second Verse

news.abstract: The Israeli leader clearly implied today that Yasir Arafat's recent cease-fire call was an attempt to influence Israel's Jan. 28 elections.
news.title: Sharon Sees Political Motives in Arafat's Appeal

news.abstract: India welcomes nearly 2,000 Indians who emigrated or whose forebears emigrated for conference intended determine how resources and achievements of Indian diaspora might be used to uplift India; legislation is being introduced to grant dual citizenship to people of Indian origin living in US, Britain, Australia, New Zealand, Canada and Singapore; participants voice concerns ranging from Hindu-Muslim violence to Indian government's silence when rights of Indians abroad are violated; map shows world distribution of nonresident Indians; photos (M)
news.title: India Harvests Fruits of a Diaspora

news.abstract: German authorities arrest two Yemeni men in Frankfurt at US request; main suspect is identified as Sheik Muhammad Ali Hassan al-Mouyad, imam at mosque in Sana, whom American officials describe as significant Qaeda figure and fund-raiser for Osama bin Laden; Yemeni officials react with surprise; photos; map (M)
news.title: Germans Arrest 2 Yemenis at U.S. Request

news.abstract: Editors and journalists in Afghanistan face risks if they push boundaries of political satire even though Pres Hamid Karzai has announced that press is free; Abdul Ghafoor Iteqad, editor of Kabul weekly Farda, was jailed for two nights on order of defense minister, Marshal Muhammad Fahim, on ground that one of its cartoons insulted Karzai; Karzai, who was out of country at time, ordered Iteqad's release upon his return; cartoon (M)
news.title: Afghan Editors Test Freedom's Boundaries With Cartoons

news.abstract: Joy Lee Sadler, American nurse who went to Indonesia as sort of freelance Florence Nightingale, is released from prison after having been convicted by Indonesian authorities of contacting separatist rebels in Aceh province; will return to home in Waterloo, Iowa, but wants to continue her one-person health mission; her companion, Lesley McCulloch, British academic, is due to be released in February; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Woman Is Released From Prison In Indonesia

news.abstract: Asst Sec of State James A Kelly begins consultations with South Korean Pres-elect Roh Moo Hyun and other officials in Seoul about nuclear threat from North Korea; some developments in US and Russia indicate diplomatic solution might be bit closer, even as North Korean government issues barrage of bellicose statements; Gov Bill Richardson of New Mexico, who talked with North Korean representatives, says he expects low-level talks to begin between US and North Korea at United Nations; Russian Foreign Ministry expresses some optimism about possible settlement of crisis; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Envoy Starts Discussions in Seoul on North Korea

news.abstract: The White House said today that the U.S. was "not putting any artificial timetable" on U.N. arms inspectors in Iraq.
news.title: U.S. and Britain Assert No Deadline on Iraq Inspections

news.abstract: Prime Min Ariel Sharon of Israel speaks dismissively of Yasir Arafat's appeal for pre-election halt to Palestinian attacks on Israeli civilians; implies that Arafat is trying to help his dovish opponent; Palestinian officials, who view Sharon as implacable enemy, have openly voiced their preference for his opponent Haifa Mayor Amram Mitzna, former general who has said he would dismantle Jewish settlements in West Bank and Gaza Strip and reopen direct negotiations with Palestinians (M)
news.title: Sharon Says Arafat's Truce Call Aims at Influencing Israeli Voters

news.abstract: First graduating class of Russia's New Economics School gathers for its 10th reunion in Moscow; Western-style graduate school was established in first year of new Russia; its students were first to receive Western-style graduate education in economics after Soviet Union fell; its graduates have grown into some of country's most promising young leaders; 34 graduates of first class are now in jobs in business, education and government; they have brought fresh ideas and outlooks to Russia, and now are powerful force for change; photo (M)
news.title: At a Reunion in Moscow, Tales of Economic Change

news.abstract: Pope John Paul II expressed his strongest opposition yet to a potential war in Iraq today, describing it as a "defeat for humanity."
news.title: Pope Expresses Opposition to Potential War in Iraq

news.abstract: President Jacques Chirac rewarded those Muslim leaders who chose to join a council to represent an official Islam for France.
news.title: Another Step in France's Official Recognition of Muslim Leaders

news.abstract: Bush administration expects international inspectors will try to bring Iraqi scientists and engineers out of country starting next week to interview them about weapons programs; officials say interviews may be conducted on Cyprus or at United Nations facilities in Europe; talks are being timed to get information from scientists before reports to UN by chief weapons inspectors Hans Blix and Mohamed ElBaradei (M)
news.title: U.S. Expects Iraqi Experts Will Be Taken Abroad for Questioning

news.abstract: Pope John Paul II will travel to Croatia in early June (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Vatican: Pope Plans Croatia Trip

news.abstract: Reaction around world is almost unanimous in support of decision of departing Gov George Ryan of Illinois to pardon 4 death row inmates and commute sentences of 167 others; International Commission of Jurists, representing judges and senior lawyers in 60 nations, says it 'emphatically' supports decision (M)
news.title: Clearing of Illinois Death Row Is Greeted by Cheers Overseas

news.abstract: Four Algerians accused of plotting attacks using lethal toxin ricin are formally charged with terror and chemical-weapons offenses in London court, as antiterror police arrest six more people in Bournemouth on English Channel; six are charged under Terrorism Act of 2000, aimed at those suspected of possessing 'articles of value to a terrorist'; Prime Min Tony Blair says arrests show there is very real threat to people of Britain (M)
news.title: British Court Charges 4 Men As Terrorists; Arrests Spread

news.abstract: British police officer is stabbed to death during arrests of three terrorist suspects in Manchester; four other officers are wounded in raid linked to discovery of deadly poison ricin in London flat occupied by Algerians; six people arrested in Bournemouth are found to have been involved in terrorism hoax and possible immigration violations (M)
news.title: British Officer Slain, 4 Hurt As Terror Suspects Are Seized

news.abstract: Vladimir Kravchenko, Chief Prosecutor of Chechen administration, accuses guerrillas of kidnapping and then blowing up 10 civilians; dismembered bodies have reportedly been found across several acres near Grozny; victims have not been publicly identified and officials offer no proof as of yet to support their assertions (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Rebels Accused Of Killing Civilians

news.abstract: US and Afghan officials warn of continuing threat from Osama bin Laden, Taliban leader Mullah Muhammad Omar and warlord Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, who have frustrated more than year of efforts to find them; photos; they are believed hiding in remote mountains and lawless tribal areas straddling Pakistan border; UN officials report former Taliban members crossing back into Afghanistan (M)
news.title: Lost in Afghanistan (Maybe): Bin Laden (Still) and 2 Others

news.abstract: More than 1,300 people have been arrested in Britain in last ten months as part of Operation Ore, nationwide hunt for users of child pornography; list includes police officers, judges and politicians, teachers and social workers, as well as Who guitarist Pete Townshend, whose computers were seized in London; Townshend says he suspects he was abused as child and was researching subject; detainees are all accused of downloading explicit photos from pay-per-view Web sites that contained hard-core pornography and would have been impossible to access by chance; case stems from US Postal Service probe of ring run by Janice and Thomas Reedy (M)
news.title: Britain's Hunt for Child Pornography Users Nets Hundreds Besides Pete Townshend

news.abstract: Paul D. Wolfowitz, the deputy defense secretary, outlined a new plan for using American forces to improve security.
news.title: Pentagon Official Wants to Speed Rebuilding of Afghanistan

news.abstract: Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash and Greek Cypriot leader Glafcos Clerides have face-to-face meeting and plan additional meetings to discuss UN plan to reunite island after thirty-year division; effort had failed in earlier UN-led talks at European Union summit, but pending union membership for Cyprus has fueled renewed efforts toward unity; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Cyprus: Leaders Hold Talks

news.abstract: Former Zambian Finance Minister Katele Kalumba is arrested in connection with disappearance of $33 million dollars while he was in office; police found him hiding in tree near his home; several other past officials have been charged in corruption investigation in which police anticipate arrest of former President Frederick Chiluba (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Zambia: A Shady Ex-Official

news.abstract: PARIS:—  Jacques Chirac says that France and Germany's approach and vision concerning Iraq are "identical and of the same nature" — an elastic, credulity-stretching description of unity across the Rhine. It turns a wish into a single will, a country that describes its armed forces as ready for action into the supposed psychic mirror of a neighbor that rules out any role in a military strike against Saddam Hussein.
news.title: For Berlin and Paris, a facade

news.abstract: Pres Bush says he will ask Congress to postpone expiration of trade law that gives 35 African nations duty-free access to American markets (M)
news.title: Bush Says He Will Ask Congress To Extend Africa Trade Benefits

news.abstract: Rudolph W Giuliani ends his first working tour of Mexico City, for which his firm is acting as crime-fighting consultant; many citizens and police officers do not expect him to come up with great ideas, but they are impressed at his $4.3-million fee, which could pay starting salaries of 1,400 police officers for a year; fee was paid by businessmen; photos (M)
news.title: Mexico City Journal; Enter Consultant Giuliani, His Fee Preceding Him

news.abstract: Chicago City Council votes 41 to 1 for resolution opposing unilateral, pre-emptive strike on Iraq, joining more than two dozen cities nationwide that have taken similar action (S)
news.title: WAR DISSENT IN CHICAGO

news.abstract: Pres-elect Roh Moo Hyun of South Korea insists on peaceful approach toward North Korea, which he says wants to escape its status as rogue state, interview; will not contemplate military strike from South Korean territory against North Korean nuclear complex on Yongbyon, even if North Korea were found to be reprocessing nuclear fuel for bomb production there; tries to play down recent wave of anti-Americanism in South Korea and denies his candidacy rode such a wave; vows to keep his country's relationship with US strong while trying to usher North Korea out of international isolation; photo (M)
news.title: South Korea's President-Elect Rejects Use of Force Against North Korea

news.abstract: European Parliament approves law banning use of most animal tests to develop cosmetic products in European Union by 2009; also banned would be imports of cosmetics that have been tested on animals (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Europe: Ban On Animal Tests For Cosmetics

news.abstract: Top US military officers draw up comprehensive plan to combat terror that includes confronting countries that sponsor terrorism, even if that would not necessarily mean direct attack; experts say applying pressure on Syria and Iran, Hezbollah's patrons, would likely be more effective than trying to attack Hezbollah itself; document, approved by Gen Richard B Myers, chairman of Joint Chiefs of Staff, represents shift to pre-emptive action against hostile states and terrorist groups; also addresses military's heightened role in homeland security (M)
news.title: Pentagon Draws Up a 20-to-30-Year Antiterror Plan

news.abstract: Announcement that Emperor Akihito has prostate cancer and will undergo surgery is significant development in Japan, where imperial family lives closely guarded existence; Akihito has been eager to put more mortal face on often-distant family; photo of people lining up at Imperial Place in Tokyo to add their prayers for Emperor Akihito; photo (M)
news.title: Japan's Monarchy, Once Godlike, Shows Its Frailty

news.abstract: Senate Governmental Affairs Committee unanimously approves nomination of Tom Ridge to be nation's first secretary of homeland security; some lawmakers are skeptical of his assertion that nation is 'far safer' now than it was before Sept 11, 2001, terrorist attacks; new department under his leadership will draw together 22 federal agencies with nearly 170,000 employees; photo (M)
news.title: Senate Panel Quickly Backs Ridge for New Antiterror Post

news.abstract: Mexican army raids offices of drug enforcement officers in 11 states to seize evidence of enforcers' wrongdoing (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Mexico: Army Raids Drug Agents' Office

news.abstract: BUSH VISITS WOUNDED SOLDIERS President Bush visited five soldiers who had been wounded in Afghanistan, thanking them for their service and pledging to provide the military with the best possible care. Mr. Bush traveled to Walter Reed Army Medical Center in Washington for a 40-minute visit with the soldiers, all of whom suffered blast or shrapnel wounds. Afterward, he described the five, who were not identified, as
news.title: Briefly Noted

news.abstract: Federal health officials say that government's smallpox vaccination program will proceed as planned despite concerns about lack of safeguards raised in expert advisory group's report and calls for delay by unions representing health care workers; Institute of Medicine report, written as confidential draft at request of federal Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, contains 23 recommendations and was obtained and first described by New York Times on Jan 16; federal program calls for vaccination of up to 500,000 health care workers in coming weeks; second phase calls for innoculating 10 million more people; eleven states are ready to begin vaccinations which are part of biodefense program, not public health program, and, unlike other innoculations, offer risk but no benefits to recipients in absence of attack, since smallpox has been eradicated (M)
news.title: Officials Press Ahead With Smallpox Shots

news.abstract: Icelandic Prime Minister David Oddsson visits Japan; says he wants his country to follow Japan's lead and start hunting whales for scientific research; Iceland announced plans to resume commercial whaling in 2006 (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Iceland: Sharpening The Harpoons

news.abstract: Padsha Khan Zadran, powerful Afghan warlord who is pro-American and anti-Taliban but who opposes American-backed government of Pres Hamid Karzai, may be softening his opposition after months of deadlock and bloodshed; negotiations between Zadran and Karzai, through mediator, may be close to ending standoff; United Nations officials are seeking to negotiate face-saving way for Zadran to change in his position; he has railed against Karzai's 'illegitimate government,' but he is losing support as backing for Karzai grows; photo; map (M)
news.title: Warlord Is Said to Be Ready to End Standoff With Kabul

news.abstract: Less than two months after voters narrowly rejected an initiative that would have given Switzerland the most restrictive asylum laws in Europe, the Swiss government has signed an agreement aimed at curbing frivolous applications for political asylum.     The agreement with Senegal, signed last week in Dakar, Senegal's capital, allows Switzerland to deport to Senegal any West African whose asylum application has been rejected and whose country of origin is not clear.
news.title: Swiss Sign Pact to Curb the Rise Of Political Asylum Requests

news.abstract: Pres Hugo Chavez of Venezuela fails to win backing from Pres Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva of Brazil to include Russia, France and other 'friendly' nations in United States-sponsored mediation effort to restore peace to Venezuela; Chavez is facing growing demands from opponents at home to resignas economy buckles under sevn-week-long strike; he insists that mediation group be broadened; it currently includes US, Brazil Mexico, Spain, Portugal and Chile (M)
news.title: Chávez Set Back on Expanding Mediation Group

news.abstract: Polio virus--almost vanquished worldwide thanks to cheap and widely available vaccine--makes defiant comeback in India, borne along by rumor and fear; India had 1,509 newly diagnosed cases last year; vast majority are in Uttar Pradesh, country's most populous state, and one of its poorest; government officials and community leaders attribute this to widely believed rumor that oral vaccine is part of government population control scheme; mothers are refusing doses for their children, even when vaccinators come to their homes, fearing it will make their children sterile; polio outbreak has exposed religious health divide; majority of polio cases last year in Uttar Pradesh were among Muslims, although rumor was repeated in Hindu communities too; health officials note that Muslims in Uttar Pradesh tend to be landless laborers with lower literacy rates and greater mistrust of Hindu-dominated government; resurgence of polio in India alarms international health experts, who had aimed for global eradication by 2002; polio is now found in seven countries and has increased only in two: Nigeria and India; photos; map; chart (L)
news.title: Distrust Reopens the Door for Polio in India

news.abstract: Saudi Arabian leadership seeks Saddam Hussein's removal as leader of Iraq as part of war-avoidance strategy, even as it signals Washington that it will cooperate extensively with American military buildup in Persian Gulf, including offering use of crucial bases and airspace; other Arab and Muslim states could join effort as Turkey seeks to assemble Iraq's neighbors for urgent discussions in Ankara, with explicit agenda of averting military conflict; Prime Min Abdullah Gul of Turkey says he has encouraged Hussein to step down, while senior Saudi intelligence officer is said to be in talks with Hussein's son Qusay on proposal to offer amnesty to Saddam Hussein along with exile home for members of his extended family; Iraqi officials deny that such talks are under way; many Arab leaders appear to believe that any option that removes Hussein without resorting to war is far superior to destructive military campaign (M)
news.title: Fearful Saudis Seek a Way to Budge Hussein

news.abstract: Study by consortium of 15 influential private research centers concludes that US, Russia and Europe should do far more to reduce urgent and 'grave proliferation risks' from their remaining stockpiles of nuclear, biological and chemical weapons; says US and Europe must begin treating Russia as partner in such efforts rather than as strategic charity case; says Russia must become more open and remove obstacles to cooperation to prevent world's most lethal arms and technology from spreading to rogue states andterrorist groups; was financed by Carnegie Corp of New York and Nuclear Threat Initiative (M)
news.title: Study Urges More Action to Cut Risks From Weapons Stockpiles

news.abstract: Rallies against US-led war against Iraq are held across Europe; world religious leaders meeting at Vatican appeal to believers in all faiths to work to avert conflict in Iraq; photo (M)
news.title: In the Street, Across Europe, a Weekend of Antiwar Rallies

news.abstract: Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld, Sec of State Colin L Powell and Condoleezza Rice, Pres Bush's national security adviser, hint that they would consider allowing Saddam Hussein to find safe haven from Iraq if that would avoid war, but they reject calls for delay before confronting him militarily; say moment of decision is fast approaching on whether Hussein's government has complied with disarmament demands from United Nations (M)
news.title: EXILE FOR HUSSEIN MAY BE AN OPTION, U.S. OFFICIALS HINT

news.abstract: World Social Forum, antiglobalization alternative to World Economic Forum, is set to open in Porto Alegre, capital of Brazilian state of Rio Grande do Sul, where voters have thrown out state's Workers Party government and elected one that embraces globalization and will try to attract multinational corporations that Workers Party shunned; map (M)
news.title: Antiglobalization Forum to Return to a Changed Brazil

news.abstract: US and North Korea move slightly closer toward resolution of crisis over nuclear weapons development with American offers of economic cooperation and North Korean calls for dialogue; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Expands Aid Offer, and North Korea Wants to Talk

news.abstract: The government of Mexico asked the International Court of Justice today to block the executions of 51 Mexicans on death row in the U.S.
news.title: Mexico Challenges U.S. on Its Citizens on Death Row

news.abstract: Macedonian government requests European Union take over peace-keeping mission run by NATO since Yugoslav-Albanian uprising in 2001; action represents first use of European Union's new foreign and security policy; union anticipates replacement of NATO in Bosnia in next year (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Macedonia: Peace Role For Europeans

news.abstract: Eight backpacking American sky mountaineers on helicopters tours of Selkirk Mountains of western Canada are buried and killed by avalanche (S)
news.title: Avalanche Kills 8 U.S. Skiers Touring Canada

news.abstract: Prime Minister Tony Blair told members of Parliament today that the escalation of armed forces is shaking Saddam Hussein.
news.title: Blair Says Military Forces in Gulf Are Undermining Hussein

news.abstract: UN Human Rights Commision, meeting in Geneva, elects Libya to chairmanship after US demands and loses vote (S)
news.title: Libya to Head Rights Panel Despite U.S. Opposition

news.abstract: NATO postponed a decision on an American request for military assistance, mostly defensive in nature, that Washington said would be needed in the event of war with Iraq.
news.title: NATO Rebuffs U.S. in Debate Over Aid for a War With Iraq

news.abstract: Japan, second largest contributor to UN, will cut support by one-quarter in coming years; country accounts for 14.4 percent of global economy and pays 19.5 percent of UN budget, whereas US accounts for 30 percent of world gross domestic product and pays 22 percent of UN costs; Japanese are also angered at not getting permanent seat on Security Council(M)
news.title: Japan to Cut Contribution To the Budget Of the U.N.

news.abstract: The Labor government proposed that universities should be allowed to charge students higher tuition fees, and that students, in turn, should be able to delay paying until after graduation.
news.title: Labor Government Unveils Finance Plans for Higher Education

news.abstract: Iraqi citizens express anger mixed with hope towards the new U.N. mission to find weapons of mass destruction.
news.title: Iraqis Ambivalent on Inspections

news.abstract: Russian Foreign Intelligence Service denies The New York Times report that Russian agents worked with CIA in early 1990's to monitor North Korean nuclear program (S)
news.title: Russians Say Times Report Is Untrue

news.abstract: Preliminary returns give 44 of 150 seats in Dutch Parliament to Christian Democratic Party of Prime Min Jan Peter Balkenende, but Labor recovers from drubbing it received in May 2002 by winning 42 seats; big loser is Pim Fortuyn List, down to 8 seats from 26 in May; formation of coalition may take weeks; mood of nation has clearly shifted to right (M)
news.title: Dutch Appear to Re-elect Conservative Leader in Mixed Outcome

news.abstract: Pierre-Richard Prosper, United States primary diplomat for war crimes, meets with high ranking officials, including President Vojislav Kostunica, to levy ultimatum that Serbia arrest and hand over Ratko Mladic and Veselin Sljivancanin by March 31 or face possible suspension of US aid; Mladic stands accused of genocide in Bosnia and Sljivancanin of crimes in Croatia (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Yugoslavia: Pressure From U.S. On War Crimes

news.abstract: Iraqis complain of disruption and damage caused by international arms inspectors, even while they hope that war may be averted if inspectors complete their work without turning up chemical, biological or atomic weapons; inspectors are accepted in Iraq as wedge against any American attack, and they are also used to attack Bush administration; photo (M)
news.title: Many Iraqis, Like Their Government, Complain About Arms Inspections

news.abstract: Lord Robertson says he will step down as NATO secretary general in December, resisting requests by many members to stay on for another year (M)
news.title: NATO Secretary General to Leave His Post in December After 4 Years

news.abstract: Possible chaos from breakdown of existing order in Iraq has become overarching fear among ruling members of Saudi royal family, who realize success in ousting Pres Saddam Hussein could send uncertain winds of change sweeping through region; has motivated day-to-day ruler Crown Prince Abdullah to press efforts to motivate Pres Bush to acquiesce in 11th-hour strategy in which decision to attack Iraq would be followed by pause for intensive diplomacy, even coup-making, to remove Pres Saddam Hussein; Saudi Arabia's failed efforts of past 40 years to unite disparate tribes of peninsula and create sense of nationhood discussed; country has existed in state of arrested political development, under monarchy anchored in deeply conservative Islamic ideology that represses women's rights and excoriates foreign 'infidels;' suffers from extensive corruption, arising from enormous oil wealth (M)
news.title: Chaos, or Democracy, in Iraq Could Be Unsettling to Saudis

news.abstract: Bush administration officials have concluded that international inspectors are unlikely to find tangible and irrefutable evidence that Iraq is hiding weapons of mass destruction, so administration is preparing its own assessment that will rely heavily on evidence from Iraqi defectors; former Iraqi scientists, military officers and contractors have provided American intelligence agencies with portrait of Saddam Hussein's secret programs to develop and conceal chemical, biological and nuclear weapons that is starkly at odds with findings so far of UN weapons inspectors; but there are deep divisions in Washington over value of information from defectors; administration says three or four thought to have most valuable firsthand information have been placed in witness protection program and offered asylum (M)
news.title: Defectors Bolster U.S. Case Against Iraq, Officials Say

news.abstract: Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld's dismissal of France and Germany as 'old Europe' because they are trying to avert war with Iraq outrages both European politicians and ordinary citizens, who take remark as example of America's growing arrogance (S)
news.title: Europeans Try to Stem Anti-U.S. Anger

news.abstract: Two new cases of mad cow disease are diagnosed in Japan, bringing total infected to seven; suspiciously, six of those were weaned on formula imported from Western Europe in 1996; Japan supressed June 2001 report stating herds were at risk (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Japan: More Mad Cow Cases

news.abstract: Wealthy Chinese businessman Li Haicang is found dead in his Yuncheng office, apparently shot in head by old friend Feng Yinliang, who then shot himself; according to New China News Agency, motive appears to be tied to Feng's failed business and Li's refusal to help (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: China: Magnate Gunned Down

news.abstract: Twenty-five educators from traditional Islamic schools in Indonesia spend month in United States as part of program sponsored by State Dept to help Muslims overseas learn about United States; goal is to show skeptical Indonesian Muslims that America is land of tolerance and diversity; Indonesians visited schools and universities, learned about democracy and met with State Dept's senior officials; they also visited Statue of Liberty and Empire State Building and went shopping; one of participants says he found Americans to be friendly, but he is distrustful of policies of American government; in Feb, television studio audience in Jakarta will talk with audience in US, and results will be shown later in both countries; photo; map (M)
news.title: Indonesian Educators Ponder Lessons After U.S. Visit

news.abstract: Prime Min Jose Maria Aznar says Spanish police officials have arrested 16 militants suspected of links to Al Qaeda, breaking up two cells and confiscating electronic material and containers of unidentified chemicals; antiterrorist experts say that Spain, with its historic and geographical ties to North Africa, has been used as logistic and financial base by groups linked to Al Qaeda; photo (M)
news.title: Spain Arrests 16 Suspected of Ties to Al Qaeda

news.abstract: Palestinian factions opened talks here today that their Egyptian hosts hoped would result in a cease-fire halting attacks against Israeli civilians.    But few, if any, in the Arab world or in Israel think there is much likelihood that the dozen rival groups can reach a joint position on the conduct of the increasingly bitter 28-month intifada, let alone on stopping suicide bombers inside Israel.
news.title: Rival Palestinian Groups Meet in Cairo to Discuss Ending Attacks on Israeli Civilians

news.abstract: Department of Homeland Security opens for business with swearing in of Tom Ridge as its first secretary; skeleton staff will take control of 22 existing federal agencies over next several months, redirecting their mission to focus on defense of American soil from possibility of new terrorist attacks; Ridge declares 'we have a long way to go' in meeting goal of pre-empting new wave of terrorist strikes; Vice Pres Dick Cheney conducts swearing-in ceremonies with Pres Bush; photo (M)
news.title: Ridge Is Sworn In as a New Cabinet Secretary

news.abstract: Angelina Atyam has faced an awful trauma, and an awful choice.     Her fourth child, Charlotte, was one of 139 girls snatched in the early morning of Oct. 10, 1996, from St. Mary's College, a Catholic boarding school in the northern Ugandan town of Aboke.
news.title: A Mother's Bitter Choice: Telling Kidnappers No

news.abstract: The Chinese authorities are investigating the deaths of two men who dropped from the undercarriage of an Air France Boeing 777 as the plane approached Shanghai airport after a flight from Paris.    One of the men smashed through the roof of a house, leaving a large gash in the roof.
news.title: 2 Frozen Bodies Fall From Jet in Shanghai

news.abstract: Many Israeli Arabs, who represent about 1.2 million of 6.8 million people in Israel, say they have never before felt like such scorned outsiders; their sentiments could well manifest themselves on election day; there seems to be new peak in frustration and sense of alienation among Israeli Arabs; many Israeli Arabs say that while Arab parties in Parliament do not have enough votes to help them that much, they do not believe that predominantly Jewish parties with more power had any interest in addressing wide economic gaps between Arab and Israeli Jews; photo (M)
news.title: Israeli Arabs Lose Political Faith as Election Nears

news.abstract: New passages in South Korean textbooks have fed a debate about changing relations with North Korea and about the politicization of history during the cold war.
news.title: Making History, South Korea Gives Archenemy a Little Credit

news.abstract: Antonio Giuffre, Mafia turncoat, repeatedly testifies that mob has its grip on Italian government, including connections to Prime Min Silvio Berlusconi; forum for accusations is trial of Marcello Dell'Utri, senator in Berlusconi's political party, Forza Italia, as well as prime minister's old friend and business partner; prosectors contend that Dell'Utri was connection between mob and Milan business world; photo (M)
news.title: Mafia Trials Show Italy's Mix Of Myth and Mob in Politics

news.abstract: On the eve of a crucial report by U.N. inspectors, the secretary of state said the U.S. would go to war alone if European allies did not sign on.
news.title: U.S. Is Willing to Stand Alone Against Iraq, Powell Says

news.abstract: United States plans to enforce strict new security rules on Feb 2 for imports by sea in containers, despite complaints from many shippers that they are not ready; rules, drafted in response to Sept 11 attacks, are aimed at reducing risk that nuclear bomb or other bulky weapon of mass destruction could be shipped to United States; but exporters in Hong Kong in particular have been warning of delays and possible chaos at docks and warehouses because of rules (M)
news.title: Hong Kong Shippers Scramble to Meet New U.S. Cargo Rules

news.abstract: Taiwan's China Airlines breaks half-century freeze on commercial aviation across Taiwan Strait, picking up passengers at international airport in Shanghai and returning to Taiwan; flight is first of 16 charter flights to help Taiwanese living in mainland China to return home for Lunar New Year holiday; it is billed as important step toward restoring transportation links between political rivals; China has pushed for direct transport links for several years, but Taiwan has moved slowly to allow people and goods to flow freely to and from mainland, citing security concerns (M)
news.title: Taiwan Ends a Half-Century Freeze on Flights to China With a Trip to Shanghai

news.abstract: United States offers at least $4 billion to Turkey to compensate for economic damage it might suffer as result of playing active role in American-led coalition in war against Iraq; Recep Tayyip Erdogan, leader of Turkey's governing Justice and Development Party, says $4 billion figure is inadequate to solve Turkey's problems; offer of aid is part of carrot-and-stick approach by Washington to guarantee Turkish participation; Washington wants use of military bases and other facilities that would allow US to use Turkey as staging point for possible attack into northern Iraq; Turkish leadership is worried about domestic political fallout that could result from being seen as too pro-American by largely antiwar Muslim population; Washington has told Prime Min Abdullah Gul that Turkey must within next few days push through critical economic reforms, including radical cuts in public spending, to persuade International Monetary Fund to disburse $1.7 billion installment of fund's package for Turkey; photo (M)
news.title: In One Hand, U.S. Offers Turkey $4 Billion for War Aid; in Other, a Demand for Reform

news.abstract: Baghdad's foreign minister launched a scathing verbal attack on the United States hours before the report was delivered in New York.
news.title: Not Waiting for U.N. Report, Baghdad Assails the U.S.

news.abstract: Prime Minister Tony Blair's moralizing diplomacy, his tough talk on Iraq and his steadfast loyalty to President Bush have gained him acceptance in the United States, but they have cost him popularity at home, opinion polls indicate, and hard-won influence in Europe.
news.title: Tough Talk on Iraq Carries Cost for Blair

news.abstract: Excerpts from Secretary of State Colin L Powell's speech on Iraq at World Economic Forum; photo (M)
news.title: Powell on Iraq: 'We Reserve Our Sovereign Right to Take Military Action'

news.abstract: The Israeli prime minister's big win in elections amounted to an endorsement of his tough approach to the conflict with Palestinians.
news.title: Sharon Leads Likud to Decisive Victory

news.abstract: Authorities in Zimbabwe question five foreign aid workers, including one American, and accuse them of working as journalists without accreditation; workers are from Lutheran World Federation and write for in-house publication; country's strict media laws require all foreign journalists to be invited before working there (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Zimbabwe: Aid Workers Questioned

news.abstract: Vatican upholds excommunication of seven women who were 'ordained' in Austria in June 2002 (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Vatican: Women's Excommunication Upheld

news.abstract: Two trains collide head-on in Alpine tunnel near Italian border in southeast France, killing two people and injuring four seriously (S)
news.title: Crash in Tunnel Kills Two

news.abstract: Lower house of Japanese Parliament approves extra $25 billion in new spending on public works projects and job creation (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Japan: $25 Billion In Extra Spending

news.abstract: Some 350 American, European and Afghan forces fought a fierce battle through the night against a large group of rebel fighters in a mountainous region of southeastern Afghanistan, in the heaviest fighting they have encountered in nine months, the American military spokesman said here today.    As many as 80 fighters aligned with the former mujahedeen commander Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, a warlord who once battled Soviet occupation but has now joined forces with the remnants of the Taliban to oust the Americans, were thought to be lodged in caves and mountain hideouts near the border with Pakistan, said the spokesman, Col. Roger King. Those forces fired on Apache helicopters that went to investigate their presence in the Adi Ghar, a mountain range just north of Spinbaldak, the border crossing between the southern Afghan town of Kandahar and the Pakistani city of Quetta.
news.title: U.S. AND ITS ALLIES FIGHT REBEL FORCE ON AFGHAN PEAKS

news.abstract: A French-brokered peace accord aimed at ending a brutal four-month-long civil war in this country seemed to teeter this evening, as the army rejected key elements of a power-sharing deal with rebel groups and aligned itself with supporters of Ivory Coast's elected government.    The military made its position clear in a letter to Ivory Coast's president, Laurent Gbagbo, rejecting calls for demobilization.
news.title: Ivory Coast Army Rejects Power-Sharing Deal With Rebels

news.abstract: A top adviser to Saddam Hussein pledged tonight to make the ''extra effort'' to cooperate with United Nations weapons inspectors, but offered no dramatic initiative for doing so a day after the inspection team delivered a largely negative report on Iraq's cooperation so far.     ''We have for sure provided complete cooperation in every aspect,'' the adviser, Lt. Gen. Amir Rasheed, a former oil minister, told reporters. ''But as they have said, there is an opportunity for what they call pro-active cooperation. We said, 'O.K., welcome.' Proactive means we are ready as Iraq to facilitate.''
news.title: Iraqi Aide Pledges 'Extra Effort' to Cooperate With Inspectors

news.abstract: VENEZUELA: Trying To Stop Flight Of Dollars;.
news.title: World Briefing: Americas

news.abstract: The trains arrive with a whisper, speak with a computerized voice and at times are driven by women. Passengers board quickly and quietly at stations that are clean and airy, with graceful 30-foot arched ceilings and computerized entryways.    In a city of 14 million people that otherwise tends toward controlled anarchy, it is a pride-inspiring marvel.
news.title: New Delhi Journal; Clean, Modern Subway, Efficiently Built. In India?

news.abstract: Prime Minister Atal Behari Vajpayee expanded and shuffled his cabinet today in a move seen as intended to aid India's faltering economic reforms ahead of elections late next year.
news.title: India Cabinet Shakeup as Economic Reforms Falter

news.abstract: arafat offers direct talks with sharon, who declines**Yasir Arafat reacts to Prime Min Ariel Sharon's overwhelming victory in Israel's parliamentary elections by offering to begin face-to-face talks immediately; Sharon, who has sought to isolate and oust Arafat as Palestinian leader, rebuffs offer, saying he would speak only to Palestinians 'not involved in terror in any way'; rare, albeit indirect, exchange between old rivals comes as Israel's political factions sort through results of elections, and violence flares again in West Bank and Gaza Strip; photo (M)
news.title: Arafat Offers Direct Talks With Sharon, Who Declines

news.abstract: The verdict could give renewed vigor to Islamic radicals who have been on the defensive in Indonesia since the terrorist blast in Bali last October, analysts said.
news.title: Indonesia Clears Top Islamic Militant in Attacks on Christians

news.abstract: Chairman of Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen Richard B Myers says small numbers of American military forces are now operating in northern Iraq; says Special Operations Forces are in Kurdish areas to work with teams of Central Intelligence Agency operatives who are organizing Kurdish opposition groups; this is first time American military officials have commented publicly on periodic reports of American troops slipping in and out of area; photo (M)
news.title: Some U.S. Forces in Northern Iraq, Military Chief Says

news.abstract: Edward M Korry, United States ambassador to Chile from 1967 to 1971 who was wrongly suspected of helping to plot military coup to prevent Salvador Allende from becoming president, dies at age 81; photo (M)
news.title: Edward Korry, 81, Is Dead; Falsely Tied to Chile Coup

news.abstract: Ireland will ban smoking in all workplaces, including pubs and restaurants, starting in 2004; Health Min Michael Martin's announcement angers tobacco manufacturers and publicans alike, who call ban unenforceable and an infringement of personal liberties (M)
news.title: Ireland to Ban Smoking in Workplace (That Means Pubs, Too)

news.abstract: German Chancellor Gerhard Schroder used his opposition to war in Iraq to win narrow election in Sept, but opinion polls and commentators say his peace appeal is not working in local election campaign in Lower Saxony that is being seen as referendum on national government; state has one of highest unemployment rates in Germany, and that, not Iraq, is big issue for voters; broad expectation is that Schroder and his party are going to do very poorly in elections there and in Hesse; election losses would seriously erode his authority and prestige only four months after he began his second term (M)
news.title: Elections in 2 German States May Be Setback to Schröder

news.abstract: American spy satellites detect what appear to be trucks moving North Korea's stockpile of 8,000 nuclear fuel rods out of storage, prompting fears within Bush administration that North Korea is preparing to produce roughly half dozen nuclear weapons; intelligence analysts have seen extensive activity throughout Jan at Yongbyon nuclear complex; satellites cannot see exactly what is being put into trucks, but analysts conclude that it is likely that workers are transporting rods to another site, either to get them out of sight or to move them to reprocessing plant to convert them into bomb-grade plutonium; analysts suspect that North Korea could begin producing bomb-grade plutonium by end of Mar; Bush administration has said nothing publicly about activity, and not shared information widely with allies; some administration officials believe North Korean leader Kim Jong Il hopes to set off crisis to extract concessions from Washington, while others say Pres Bush does not want to distract international attention from Iraq; photos; map (M)
news.title: Satellites Said to See Activity At North Korean Nuclear Site

news.abstract: United Nations' top development official Mark Malloch Brown concludes costs of rebuilding Iraq after war will run to at least $30 billin in first three years (M)
news.title: U.N. Estimates Rebuilding Iraq Will Cost $30 Billion

news.abstract: BELGIUM: Parliament Approves Gay Marriages; BRITAIN: 2 London Subway Lines Closed For Weeks; IRELAND: The Perils Of Power; RUSSIA: Putin Reaches Out To Vatican; SERBIA: Ex-Intelligence Chief Jailed In Attack Plot;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Iran's Grand Ayatollah Hossein Ali Montazeri, freed from shackles of house arrest after five years, speaks to visitors, including delegation of Parliament deputies and hundreds of men and women who rotate in and out of warehouse-like auditorium, Qum; Montazeri, 80, learned cleric and reformist, is overtly hostile to Iran's conservative clerical establishment, scoring them for their repression and for trying to silence him, interview; calls harsh sentences given political prisoners by two special courts 'baseless;' urges courts be disbanned and all political prisoners freed; holds Ayatollah Ali Khamenei is not infallible and could be challenged by Parliament; continues to oppose United States foreign policy; map (M)
news.title: Freed Ayatollah Again Makes Voice Heard

news.abstract: Indian scientists ask Iranian officials to lend them pair of Asian cheetahs, which have been extinct in India for 50 years, for cloning; Asiatic cheetahs are critically endangered subspecies (S)
news.title: India, Out of Cheetahs, Seeks to Clone

news.abstract: At least 16 people, including women and children, are killed when their minibus explodes on bridge just outside Kandahar, Afghanistan, in blast probably caused by antitank mine; Gen Akram Khakrezwal, city's police chief, blamse Taliban or other rebel forces, phone interview; sees act of terror aimed at local people; United States forces, waging fierce battle against rebel fighters 90 miles from city, near Pakistan border, search mountain caves without incident; main group of some 80 rebels seems to have melted away; map; photo (M)
news.title: Afghan Women and Children Among 16 Dead in Bus Blast

news.abstract: RUSSIA: Arrests In Downing Of Helicopter; FRANCE: Former Oil Chief Turns Himself In; BRITAIN: Chechen Faces Extradition; BRITAIN: Police In Court On Child Sex Charges; SPAIN: Ending Diplomatic Crisis With Morocco; BRITAIN: Snow Paralyzes Country;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Loik LeFloch-Prigent, former president of old French state-owned oil company Elf Aquitaine, surrenders to authorities after appeals court upholds his conviction and 30-month jail term for corruption; was in hiding when he was convicted on charges rising out of vast scandal at Elf, which was privatized in 1994 and now forms part of TotalFinaElf; court overturned conviction of ex-Min Roland Dumas; photo (M)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: France: Former Oil Chief Turns Himself In

news.abstract: ABIDJAN, Ivory Coast, Feb. 2 — An explosion ripped through a dense city block in Lagos, Nigeria, this morning, killing roughly 30 people, injuring many more and setting off scenes of chaotic looting that impeded rescue efforts.
news.title: Explosion in Nigeria Kills Approximately 30

news.abstract: Large number of businesses across Venezuela are opening to offset huge financial losses from general strike, and opposition leaders say they will scale back walkout so that factories, shops, malls and schools can reopen; strike, which has failed in its originally stated mission to force Pres Hugo Chavez to resign or to call early elections, will continue only in all-important oil industry; decision is major victory for Chavez (M)
news.title: Chávez Foes Scale Back Strike for Businesses

news.abstract: Pentagon's war plan for Iraq calls for unleashing 3,000 precision-guided bombs and missiles in first 48 hours of opening air campaign in order to stagger and isolate Iraqi military and quickly pave way for ground attack to topple government in shock; campaign will be carried out by about 500 Air Force attack, radar-jamming and support planes; will seek to limit damage to Iraqi infrastructure and to minimize civilian casualties; ground offensive will use strategy called vertical envelopment, with Special Operations forces and airborne troops seizing airfields and other targets deep within Iraq, relying on planes flying high-risk missions to ferry American armored vehicles to runways seized behind enemy lines of Iraqi regular troops; huge tanker trucks are being massed in Kuwait to ensure that fighting forces do not outrun their fuel supplies; photo; map (L)
news.title: War Plan Calls for Precision Bombing Wave to Break Iraqi Army Early in Attack

news.abstract: Your average café denizen concluded that God was sending the U.S. a message that its entire Mideast policy is misguided.
news.title: Arabs Hope Shuttle Disaster Prompts U.S. Reflection

news.abstract: Veterans of the Battle of Stalingrad are pressing for the restoration of the name that came to symbolize the Soviet Union's stunning reversal of fortune.
news.title: Russian Veterans Push to Restore Name of City They Fought For

global_music.title: All I Have

news.abstract: Military wings of several main Palestinian factions are drawn together by their desire for revenge against Israel, but divisions in their ideology endure; more than two years of conflict and shared nationalist impulse have blurred their distinctions, but even in Nablus, which Israel calls center for terrorism in West Bank, members of Aksa Martyrs Brigades have little interest in meeting with members of Palestinian Authority or Hamas; Hamas representatives have no interest in meeting with Fatah leader; Israel has offered to ease retrictions and withdraw its forces from areas where Palestinians achieve calm, but Hamas and other groups scoff at idea that proposal should limit Palestinian uprising; some Fatah leaders argue that Palestinian attacks should be confined to soldiers and settlers in territories, believing such violence would be supported abroad as legitimate resistance to occupation; Hamas does not distinguish between boundaries, claiming all of Israel and territories belong to Palestinians; photo; map (L)

news.abstract: Tens of thousands of protesters around world take to streets to condemn United States-led war in Iraq; express anger at television images of Baghdad ablaze; protests in Europe draw in church leaders and politicians, schoolchildren and labor leaders; Pope John Paul II urges peace; in Spain, protesters denounce war and their government's unwavering support for military operation in Iraq; in Tokyo, demonstrators hold up photos of wounded Iraqi children in 1991 Persian Gulf war; photos (M)
news.title: Thousands Denounce War and the United States in Cities Around the World

news.abstract: In both countries the source of all new cases continues to be close contact with health care workers who themselves had close contact with earlier cases.
news.title: Respiratory Illness Spreads to Singapore and Vietnam

news.abstract: Taliban supporters launch two more attacks on Afghan government troops, continuing new wave of violence against American military presence in Afghanistan and American allies in Afghan government; three Afghan guards are killed in fighting 20 miles from border crossing to Pakistan; local district chief says attackers probably came across border from Pakistan (M)
news.title: Taliban Allies Kill 3 Guards Near Pakistan

news.abstract: It was the first large group of detainees suspected of membership in the Taliban or Al Qaeda to be released since the center opened more than a year ago.
news.title: U.S. Returns 18 Guantánamo Detainees to Afghanistan

news.abstract: Moscow denied that Russian companies have been selling night-vision goggles, anti-tank missiles and other hardware to Iraq.
news.title: White House Upset Over Russian Sale of Weapons to Iraq

news.abstract: Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld condemns Iraq's use of 'human shields' at various targets; says tactic prevents American-led air war from cutting off ability of Pres Saddam Hussein's regime to broadcast over state-run television and radio; says senior American commanders have avoided bombing as many as three dozen high-priority targets for fear of civilian casualties; map (M)
news.title: Rumsfeld Says Dozens of Important Targets Have Been Avoided

news.abstract: American and British ground forces suffer worst casualties so far in war against Iraq in sharpest engagements of conflict; at least 20 American soldiers die or are missing and 50 are wounded in day of ambushes, accidents and tank and artillery engagements; most of losses occur at Nasiriya, along Euphrates River about 100 miles north of Kuwaiti border where Army maintenance convoy is ambushed, resulting in death or capture of dozen soldiers; as many as 10 soldiers die during fierce battle after troop carrier is struck by rocket-propelled grenade; Pres Bush expresses grief to parents of soldiers lost in battle, but says he is confident campaign will succeed; main force of allied army races toward Bahgdad; skirts Najaf and other centers of population; Iraqi tactics show little coherent military organization, but expose potential weakness in dash by American forces to Baghdad; by skipping over cities, coalition forces appear to leave flanks and rear areas exposed to counterattacks by irregulars under command of Republican Guard; diagrams (M)
news.title: ALLIES AND IRAQIS BATTLE ON 2 FRONTS; 20 AMERICANS DEAD OR MISSING, 50 HURT

news.abstract: Turkish and American officials say series of misunderstandings and miscalculations have created profound tensions that are likely to endure between two countries; political analysts cast these tensions as clear example of collateral damage from war in Iraq; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Ties to Turkey May Face Enduring Strain, Officials Say

news.abstract: Eight gunmen dressed in Indian Army uniforms enter Kashmiri village of Nadimarg, open fire and kill 24 of 52 Pandits, or Hindus, still living there; Muslims from area sit by bodies of their Hindu neighbors, wailing and cursing killers; no one has claimed responsibility for attack, but Islamic militants fighting for Kashmir's independence or accession to Pakistan have stepped up attacks on Hindus in recent years; latest attack heightens fears that with spring approaching and American attention elsewhere, violence could rise again in Jammu and Kashmir; photos; map (M)

news.title: British Troops Plan to Use Force in Basra

news.title: 3rd Infantry Seizes 3 Bridges in Fiercest Fighting So Far

news.abstract: Treatment of 3,500 Iraqi prisoners of war becomes matter of attention after Iraqi national television shows graphic pictures of dead and captured American soldiers, prompting protests from Bush administration; allied military officials in Iraq say they take their duty to respect rights of POW's very seriously; photo (M)
news.title: Hot Disputes Over Images of P.O.W.'s Held on Each Side

news.abstract: World's longest-running Communist insurgency is reviving in Philippines, with attacks, ambushes and assassinations increasing sharply in last three years; photos; map; insurgency was founded in mountains near San Agustin, north of Manilla, 34 years ago and reached peak in mid-1980's as main outlet for opposition to Ferdinand Marcos regime; it withered after his fall, with many of leading figures returning to mainstream, but draws new life from persistent poverty and corruption (M)

news.abstract: About 4,330 Iraqis have returned from Jordan to Iraq to fight for Saddam Hussein, whom they once hated as oppressor; Iraqis staying in Jordan say many of those going home merely want to help their families; either way, war churns complex emotions among 380,000 Iraqis who live in Jordan; photo (M)

news.abstract: Gale-force winds and intense dust clouds hampering allied drive across southern Iraq to Baghdad is expected to clear within day; weather map (M)
news.title: Front That Brought Winds and Dust Is Due to Lift

news.title: Wounded Americans Say Iraqi Soldiers Fought in Disguise
