news.title: Hong Kong closes its schools to curb outbreak

news.abstract: Turkish Airlines flight on its way to Ankara from Istanbul is hijacked and forced to fly to Athens, where it sits on tarmac for three hours before the more than 190 passengers on board are released; Turkish officials say there was just one hijacker, 22-year-old Turkish man identified as Ozgur Gencarslan, and he does not have known ties to any terrorist group; passengers say he appeared to be emotionally unstable (M)

news.title: WHITE HOUSE SAYS WAR IS 'ON TRACK'; SHOW OF SUPPORT

news.title: U.S. Finds Buried Bodies of 4 G.I.'s

news.title: U.S. Convoy Is Ambushed; 2 Americans Are Killed

news.abstract: American Marine and Army infantry units arrayed along broad front south of Baghdad make first probing attacks against Republican Guard division at Karbala, 65 miles from capital; this follows week of heavy aerial bombardment on Iraqi forces that guard approaches to Saddam Hussein's stronghold; in Baghdad, another round of airstrikes begins; bombing continues on city's southern outskirts, where at last two Republican Guard divisions are deployed; probing attacks are intended to keep pressure on Hussein and to re-establish allied momentum that has been stalled in recent days by fierce attacks on allied supply lines; Gen Tommy R Franks, American commander in region, disputes charge that allied commanders misjudged willingness of Hussein's loyalists to resist and underestimated size of armed force needed to sudue them; defends his war plan, as do Gen Richard B Myers, chairman of Joint Chiefs of Staff, and Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld; despite Franks's confidence, situation in Iraq appears tense; war continues to unfold as far more complex tapestry than expected, with dispersed engagements, political and psychological warfare against Hussein's government, mobilization to deliver aid to south, frenetic diplomacy and shifting explanations at home about war's duration and cost; photos; map (L)

news.abstract: The U.S., through its past acts, is largely to blame for the failure of Iraq's Shiite majority to rise in revolt against Saddam Hussein, a senior military commander said.

news.abstract: Zahra Eshraghi, granddaughter of Ayatollah Khomeini, sister-in-law of Pres Mohammad Khatami and wife of head of reformist wing of Iran's parliament, has enormous standing in Iranian society, and uses it to state frankly her hatred of chador, black veil forced on women since her grandfather's revolution; interview; photo; Eshraghi, 39, is herself government official who has fought colleagues at Interior Ministry, where she promotes women's issues; her candor also reflects changes in Iran, where revolution's values have given way to intense, even dangerous debate about religion's place in politics and society (M)
news.title: Daughter of the Revolution Fights the Veil

news.abstract: EGYPT TO EXPEL IRAQI ENVOY Egypt has decided to expel a senior Iraqi diplomat, giving him a week to leave the country. An Arab diplomat who monitors Iraqi affairs in Cairo said the order was served Tuesday morning.
news.title: Briefly Noted

news.abstract: There is one in the back row of every classroom, in every nest of office cubicles, at the end of the bar at every happy hour. And, as it turns out, there is one in a tent of men exhausted by the preparations for war, their aching feet sliding into cool sleeping bags.    ''Aw, look at all the girls going to sleep,'' came the voice from a makeshift table in a corner of the tent, the small patch of hair on the big head dulled with dust. ''It's like a slumber party.'' He shuffled a deck of cards between his thick fingers and continued, in a lilting falsetto: ''Hey, did that guy ever call you? Really? Wow! In just two days?'' The men tried to ignore him.    It was mid-March in Kuwait, and the war had not yet begun. Unlike most of the other marines in the tent, the Deuce was not tired. The Deuce was playing cards, and it was the Deuce's deal.
news.title: An Outfit's Wise Guy Sees the Lighter Side of Even the Somber Moments

news.abstract: Army's Third Infantry Division clears last geographic obstacle to Baghdad, 20 miles away, after it seizes damaged bridge over Euphrates River following intense three-hour battle against more than company of dug-in Iraqi soldiers; thousands of American soldiers surge across bridge in tanks, Bradleys, mobile artillery batteries and array of other armored vehicles; there are no immediate reports of American casualties; battle for bridge described; Iraqi tactics that proved efective against forces encircling Najaf, Nasiriya and Samawa--sniping, ambushes, taxi bomb--could do little to slow division's armored forces; photo (M)
news.title: G.I.'s Pry Iraqis Loose And Surge Over River

news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: New Commons Leader

news.abstract: Southern African Development Community forms task force to probe intensifying political tensions that threaten to push Zimbabwe toward further unrest and economic ruin; at issue is dispute between Pres Robert Mugabe and political opponents who charge his authoritarian rule has undermined democracy and devastated economy; Zimbabweans fleeing hunger and unemployment are becoming drain on South Africa; Western governments are pressing South African Pres Thabo Mbeki to take stronger stand against Mugabe's human-rights violations (M)

news.abstract: Almost until the last minute the border post in Trbeel functioned with the efficiency and graft of Saddam Hussein's Iraq.
news.title: Iraq's Border With Jordan Remains Chaotic

news.abstract: Red Cross official Vatche Arslanian is killed in crossfire in Baghdad, forcing it and other agencies to suspend relief program; full relief effort will be carried out by United States civilian agencies led by US Agency for International Development and will include agencies from UN and other international and private relief groups; by charter, these agencies are unable to work under authority of any military force, including Pentagon's civilian team headed by retired Gen Jay Garner, which will initially form administration; agencies will coordinate with Garner to ensure programs are as effective as possible; are stockpiling supplies but say they have little idea what they will find when they are able to inspect sanitation and water systems, size of food stocks and medical system; effort will require 480,000 tons of food every month and will cost nearly $2 billion; photo (M)
news.title: Relief Agencies Are Forced to Wait as Chaos Reigns

news.abstract: Several hundred Kurdish fighters under the command of 100 American special force fighters took control of the oil town of Kirkuk today as the focus of the American campaign switched to the northern part of Iraq.
news.title: Focus Shifts to Northern Iraq; A Message for Iraqis; U.S. Says Baghdad 'Still an Ugly Place'

news.abstract: Hopes of breakthrough in deadlocked Northern Ireland peace process are dashed when Prime Mins Tony Blair of Britain and Bertie Ahern of Ireland are forced to cancel joint appearance because of last-minute objections by Sinn Fein, political party of Irish Republican Army; new plan drawn up in London and Dublin is aimed at producing long-awaited decision by IRA to disarm and renounce violence for good (S)
news.title: Northern Irish Peace Hopes Are Set Back

news.abstract: Summary of major developments in Iraq war (M)
news.title: Fall of a Northern City, Suicide Bombing on Marines, Killing of a Cleric

news.abstract: Pres George Bush and Prime Min Tony Blair use newly seized Iraqi state television facilities to send message to Iraqi people promising to help build 'government that protects the rights of all citizens'; message is opening salvo in Pentagon-devised media campaign intended to shape messages sent to Iraqi people and speed end of war; it is unclear how many people received broadcast because of widespread power failures; both governments also intend to publish newspapers; details of other information dissemination campaigns noted, including broadcast of American nightly news programs; photos (M)
news.title: A Media Campaign Is Intended to Speed End of War

news.abstract: American forces entered Mosul today after it fell without a fight as the last of Saddam Hussein's loyalists vanished during the night.
news.title: Mosul Falls as Iraqis Surrender, Leaving Tikrit as Last Holdout

news.abstract: LONDON, April 11 — President Bush's special envoy to Northern Ireland, Richard N. Haass, said tonight that it was up to the Irish Republican Army to make a
news.title: U.S. Envoy Urges I.R.A. to Rescue Northern Ireland Peace Plan

news.abstract: American Special Forces troops enter Mosul, Iraq, after organized Iraqi resistance flees, finding city engulfed by anarchy; quickly retreat; incursion followed talks with tribal and Baath Party leaders intended to bring about peaceful surrender of city, homeland of Sunni Arab nationalism; armed Kurds in civilian clothes drive around city flying flag of Kurdish Democratic Party; thousands of Kurdish troops remain outside city; Kurds in city stage small-scale uprising; city's Arabs begin attacking Americans; Arabs and Kurds blame US for not moving soldiers into Mosul quickly enough to stop looting; photo (M)
news.title: Sniper Fire Greets G.I.'s in Big City in North

news.abstract: Officials at military hospital in Germany say Pfc Jessica D Lynch has recovered enough from her injuries to return to United States, where she will undergo further medical treatment; she was rescued from Iraqi captivity on Apr 1 (S)
news.title: Freed G.I. to Return To U.S. to Undergo Further Treatment

news.abstract: Two Marine sentries charged with protecting Camp Fenway in Iraq sit in foxhole in desert on cold night; their physical discomfort described; away from camaraderie of camp, wind becomes their friend, but silence is not to be trusted (M)
news.title: Marines in Nowhere Land: Sentry Duty in the Desert

news.abstract: Cambodia and Thailand agree to reinstate diplomatic relations, which have been suspended since Thai embassy and businesses were destroyed and vandalized in last January Phnom Penh rioting; riots were brought on by rumors that well-known Thai actress Suwanan Khongying had claimed Angkor temples belong to Thailand; Cambodian government has paid Thailand $5.9 million for damages done to embassy (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Cambodia: Relations With Thailand Resume

news.abstract: HONG KONG:—  Asian nations battling the spread of a killer disease across land, sea and air borders imposed dramatic new restrictions Friday on all travelers suspected of infection.
news.title: Battling the spread of SARS, Asian nations escalate travel restrictions

news.abstract: Table shows casualties in Iraq war: 110 US troops, 31 British, 16 US troops captured or missing
news.title: Casualties

news.abstract: Syrian Foreign Min Farouk al-Sharaa denies series of accusations leveled by United State about covert Syrian assistance to Iraq and criticizes American military for failing to establish order there; photo of Sharaa with French Foreign Min Dominique de Villepin (M)
news.title: Syrian Foreign Minister Denies Covert Aid to Iraq

news.abstract: President Bush also accused Syria of possessing chemical weapons, but he was careful not to threaten military force.
news.title: Bush Accuses Syria of Harboring Senior Iraqis

news.abstract: Almost as soon as Kurdish forces streamed into the northern Iraqi city of Kirkuk this week, American diplomats were on the phone to Turkish government officials to assure them that allied forces would take control of the situation.    That pledge had an immediate practical goal: to keep Turkish troops from entering the region, thus preventing the possibility of clashes between Turkish soldiers and Iraqi Kurds.
news.title: Turks and Kurds Maintain a Mutual Suspicion

news.abstract: All roads now lead to Tikrit for United States forces in Iraq; Tikrit is once-bleak farming town that Saddam Hussein imprinted with his opulent style of mosques and palaces; it may be last place that his loyalists could mount fierce battle against allied forces, a concern among American officials (M)
news.title: For Allies, the Next Target Is Hussein's Hometown

news.abstract: Pres Bush accuses Syria of harboring senior Iraqi military and government officials; demands 'cooperation' in punishing some of them, but stops short of threatening to use military force against Syria; asserts there are chemical weapons in Syria but does not clarify whether they were shipped there during or before war in Iraq; Syrian officials deny allegations that they are taking in Iraqi leaders and accuse Washington of waging 'disinformation campaign' to divert attention from lawlessness in Iraq; Bush also says efforts to get North Korea to bargaining table to discuss nuclear arms may be successful; question remains whether US march to Baghdad will drive North Korea to disarm or to build nuclear arsenal; Gen Tommy Franks says military has samples of Saddam Hussein's DNA and will use them to determine whether he has been killed in airstrikes (M)
news.title: Bush Demands 'Cooperation' From Syrians

news.abstract: Adversaries in Israeli-Palestinian conflict work to strengthen their diplomatic footing, anticipating renewed push by Bush administration for Middle East peace as war in Iraq winds down; Prime Min Ariel Sharon of Israel seeks substantial revisions in peace plan that Pres Bush pledges to publish soon; says plan should include requirement that Palestinians give up their claim of right of return to what is now Israel for refugees of 1948 war that created state; new Palestinian Prime Min Mahmaud Abbas struggles to form government, Bush's condition for moving ahead with plan; his proposed list of ministers would take crucial posts out of hands of men tied to Yasir Arafat; Arafat and his Fatah movement object, and are delaying scheduled presentation of list to Al Fatah's central committee; Abbas's list also comes under criticism from Palestinian reformers, who say too many old faces remain; photo (M)
news.title: Mideast Sides Maneuver, Expecting New Peace Effort

news.abstract: Canada's federalist Liberal Party jumps to lead in polls and appears poised to wrest Quebec provincial government from separatist Parti Quebecois in Apr 14 elections; victory could portend big change in Canadian politics; shift appears to reflect emerging consensus on reducing local taxes, tackling long lines for publicly financed health care and, most importantly, ending Parti Quebecois dream of separating from Canada; polls that show Liberals surging rapidly also suggest that Parti Quebecois could possibly make last-minute comeback and retain control of provincial assembly it has held since 1994; photo (M)
news.title: Liberal Party Leads Separatists in Quebec Election Poll

news.abstract: Federal health officials warn consumers to be wary of advertisements on Internet for products claiming to prevent SARS; Food and Drug Administration Comr Mark B McClellen says risk of contracting disease in United States is 'very, very low,' and there is no evidence that any specific drug is effective against it; photos (M)
news.title: The Internet Is Awash in Ads for Products Promising Cures or Protection

news.abstract: American marines move into edges of Tikrit, ancestral home of Saddam Hussein, and meet significant resistance; report getting 'foothold' in city; bombardment by jets and helicopter gunships is intense; objective is to wipe out what is believed to be one of last large concentrations of forces loyal to government of Hussein, and do it in two or three days; size of Iraqi force inside Tikrit is estimated to be about 2,500 men; Tikrit is thought to be where several high-ranking military leaders and possibly members of Hussein's inner circle have taken refuge; city is near village of Awja, Hussein's birthplace; southeast of Baghdad, marines enter town of Kut unopposed; British forces relieve First Marine Division in Amara, and now control area between Amara and Basra; no casualty figures are available for either side (M)
news.title: U.S. TROOPS POISED TO OUST LOYALISTS IN NORTHERN CITY

news.abstract: Any member of President Saddam Hussein's family can be positively identified, whether dead or alive, through scientific matching techniques.
news.title: Science Aids Hussein Hunt, General Says

news.abstract: The toll in Hong Kong from severe acute respiratory syndrome set a new single-day record.
news.title: One-Day Death Rate From New Virus Hits 9 in Hong Kong

news.abstract: Tally of reported casualties, missing and captured in Iraq war as of April 14
news.title: Casualties

news.abstract: Margaret Tutwiler leaves post as ambasador to Morocco to assume temporary position overseeing all public relations and information operations in postwar Iraq; was State Department spokeswoman during Persian Gulf war in 1991; photo (S)
news.title: Spokeswoman in '91 War To Help U.S. Leader in Iraq

news.abstract: INDONESIA: Mediators Seek Talks On Restive Province; JAPAN: Masked In The Halls Of Power;.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: Italian courts already handed down a conviction of multiple life terms to Abu Abbas for masterminding the 1985 hijacking of the Achille Lauro cruise liner.
news.title: Italy Seeks Extradition of Captured Cruise Ship Hijacker

news.abstract: Gathering of European Union leaders in Athens for signing of treaties that will enlarge group by 10 member was meant to showcase European unity, but that message is being overshadowed by rifts among members, particularly over war in Iraq, which Britain and Spain supported and France, Greece and Germany opposed; photo (M)
news.title: European Union's Expansion Is Overshadowed by Disarray

news.abstract: Pres Thabo Mbeki of South Africa says his government will pay reparations totaling $85 million to more than 19,000 victims of apartheid crimes who testified about their suffering before Truth and Reconciliation Commission; family of each victim will receive about $3,900, which compares with average annual salary in South Africa of about $3,000 (M)
news.title: South Africa to Pay $3,900 to Each Family of Apartheid Victims

news.abstract: Plunder of National Museum of Iraq, one of Middle East's most important archaeological repositories, occurred despite repeated pleas to Defense Department by experts and scholars that it be protected when American troops entered Baghdad; senior Pentagon officials say military agreed not to target site, but never guaranteed it would be able to guard it from looters (M)
news.title: Experts' Pleas to Pentagon Didn't Save Museum

news.abstract: South Korea abstained from voting on a resolution adopted by a U.N. commission that condemns North Korea for "widespread and grave" abuses of human rights.
news.title: South Korea Abstains From Vote Assailing North on Rights

news.abstract: Marines in Mosul, believing they are being fired upon, open fire in city's main square, killing four Iraqis and wounding 10; is second such incident in as many days; residents say shootings must stop and warn Americans not to squander whatever good will remains; photos (M)
news.title: Marines Again Kill Iraqis In Exchange of Fire in Mosul

news.abstract: Baghdad's cultural elite rage about destruction of city's art treasures, first by American bombs and then by looters; Amal al-Khedairy, whose home is in one of Baghdad's wealthier enclaves, walks amid rubble and shattered windows and ransacked remains of her home and cultural center she ran; war has dragged her from comfortable way of life under Saddam Hussein; she does not speak of compromises involved in running Baghdad's most luminous artistic center that flourished during Hussein's reign; her rage seems emblematic of whole class of people who might be expected to be more sympathetic to American cause; all they can see now is ruins; photo (M)
news.title: An Art Center Left in Ashes

news.abstract: Map of Iraq shows locations of military skirmishes
news.title: Strikes in the East

news.abstract: Gen Tommy R Franks seals his victory in war on Iraq by convening top allied officers in one of Saddam Hussein's proudest palaces; commanders gathering at Abu Ghraib palace in Baghdad discuss how to maintain security and rebuild Iraq now that Hussein is gone; decide to meet again in Franks's headquarters in Qatar in several days to complete plans; agree that Army will take responsibility for Baghdad and territory to north, while Marines deploy in south, where British control Basra, most important city; two-hour session concludes with video conference with Pres Bush; meeting is laden with symbolism, making clear that Americans now dominate Iraq; American troops strive to re-establish order, but Baghdad remains shattered city still groping for normal life, still in thrall of looters and arsonists and full of wary and confused people with hostility toward Americans; Franks acknowledges that much remains to be done; photos; map (M)
news.title: U.S. Generals Meet in Palace, Sealing Victory

news.abstract: Bush administration is considering series of steps to punish Cuban government for its recent crackdown on dissidents; Pres Bush is likely to make public statement soon about crackdown, which could involve cutting off cash payments to relatives in Cuba or halting direct flights to island; he is expected to issue stern warning to Havana government that US will not tolerate another exodus of rafters; Fidel Castro has relieved internal tensions several times during his 44-year tenure by allowing mass migrations to Florida; officials and Cuba specialists speculate about why Castro has unleashed most sweeping crackdown on dissidents in years; some say Castro was unnerved by American-led ouster of his ally Saddam Hussein in Iraq; others note that dissident community has made some strides in recent months (M)
news.title: U.S. May Punish Cuba for Imprisoning Critics

news.abstract: Aneesa Mirza elected mayor of Ahmadabad, commercial capital of Gujarat State; becomes first Muslim woman mayor in India (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: India: A First

news.abstract: Northwest Airlines' effort since March 15 to keep on top of rapidly emerging respiratory disease SARS reviewed; airline has crisis team that gets updates on spread of SARS and has ordered preventive measures such as wiping down ticket counters and allowing employees to wear masks and gloves; Northwest is particularly vulnerable as one of two major US airlines serving Asia; United declines to discuss procedures (M)
news.title: One Airline's 5 Weeks With a Medical Threat

news.abstract: US Army Special Forces soldiers in Diwaniya, who came to Iraq trained to fight war, find themselves wading into angry crowds, mediating between rival tribes and trying to hold together thin threads of social order; photo; 12-man team has become de facto center of government, hearing daily from tribal leaders, businesses and ordinary citizens who stream into compound to complain about spotty electricity, rampant looting and lack of jobs and commerce; Green Berets, several of whom speak Arabic, have in last week started police force, recruited English-speaking professor as city manager, located offices for municipal government and begun holding meetings where community leaders discuss problems (M)
news.title: Trained for War, 12 Green Berets Keep the Peace in an Iraqi Town

news.abstract: Unidentified gunman kills Sergei N Yushenkov, legislator and co-chairman of Western-style Liberal Russia Party, in front of Yushenkov's Moscow home; photo; second assassination of Liberal Russia leader in eight months occurs just after Yushenkov announces that new party will run candidates in parliamentary elections this December (M)
news.title: Moscow Gunman Kills Leader Of New Western-Style Party

news.abstract: Remotely piloted aircraft like Predator and Global Hawk have played crucial role in Iraq war, providing bird's-eye view of battlefield and giving military planners ability to take out targets, all without risking American lives; about 15 are in use in skies above Iraq; diagram shows how aircraft gathers and transmits data (M)
news.title: In the Skies Over Iraq, Silent Observers Become Futuristic Weapons

news.abstract: Cuba issues defiant statement in face of Bush administration threats to penalize Cuba for jailing nonviolent dissidents; experts say economy is especially vulnerable and would suffer if United States stops family remittances, which amount to up to $1 billion a year (M)
news.title: Facing U.S. Threat of Penalties, Cuba Issues a Defiant Statement

news.abstract: Their eyes widened when one of their jailers entered the room in Mahkmoor, Iraq, with a stack of fresh bread. Then, shamelessly, they devoured it, wolfing down chunk after chunk.
news.title: Young and Hungry Captives

news.abstract: Montgomery Malaami, Assyrian Christian teacher in Basra, offers positive recollections of life in Saddam Hussein's Iraq, as long as one kept on good side of Baathists; photo (M)
news.title: Teacher, a Survivor, Fondly Recalls Life in Hussein's Iraq

news.abstract: Photos and diagrams explaining how US military in Iraq is shifting tactics from large-scale hostilities to establishing street-level security and containing civil disorder
news.title: The Military in Transition: From Combat to Containment

news.abstract: Foreign ministers of six countries that share border with Iraq, including Syria, hold first postwar meeting in Saudi Arabia and sharply criticize US for mounting pressure on Syria; ministers urge 'occupying powers' to quickly stabilize Iraq and withdraw; photo (M)
news.title: Iraq's Neighbors Issue Declaration Criticizing U.S. Over Syria

news.abstract: Overview of news coverage of war in Iraq by New York Times correspondents and photographers; photos (L)
news.title: Scenes That Linger: An Iraq Chronicle by the Witnesses to a War

news.abstract: Question of who should write new Iraqi constitution and how it should be adopted is being discussed in aftermath of war; conference intended as first step toward creation of interim authority is held in Ur and is attended by Kanan Makiya, exile who has relationship with Bush administration, and other prominent expatriots; photo (M)
news.title: Questions Arise on Drafting Blueprint for Governing Iraq

news.abstract: Excerpts of diary of photographer Ozier Muhammad, who witnessed war in Iraq firsthand; recalls experience with Marine Division when explosions shook area where they were sleeping; photos (M)
news.title: Young Fighters on a Mature Mission

news.abstract: News analysis: war in Iraq was neither as painful as opponents predicted nor as painless as proponents suggested; consequences for world and regional political stability are still unknowable; new flexibility in fighting and intelligence gave allied forces edge, but there were also some nasty surprises and speed of operation contributed to plethora of loose ends, not least of which are questions about fate of Saddam Hussein and existence of weapons of mass destruction; how exile Ahmad Chalabi will be received in effort to form government and impact of destruction of historical relics and libraries also remain to be seen; in all, American triumph is not as clear-cut as was hoped; photo (M)
news.title: A New Way of Warfare Leaves Behind an Abundance of Loose Ends

news.abstract: DAVID ROHDEYoung and Hungry Captives Their eyes widened when one of their jailers entered the room in Mahkmoor, Iraq, with a stack of fresh bread. Then, shamelessly, they devoured it, wolfing down chunk after chunk.
news.title: The War Through the Eyes of Times Reporters

news.abstract: President Bush said that he was encouraged by signs that Syria was heeding his call not to harbor former Iraqi leaders.
news.title: Bush More Hopeful on Syria

news.abstract: The 79-year-old president of Azerbaijan collapsed twice during a nationally televised speech there today, prompting fresh questions about the health of a leader considered integral to the stability of his oil-rich country.
news.title: Leader's Collapse Raises Concern for Azerbaijan's Health

news.abstract: Pres Bush says he believes Syria is willing to cooperate with US, primarily about providing harbor to senior members of Saddam Hussein's administration; also appears to address broader concerns of Syria's links to terrorist organizations and development of chemical weapons; comments come amid debate over how long US will have to occupy Iraq and how it can retain control over Iraq's political and economic development; photo (M)
news.title: Bush Now Says He Believes Syria Wants to Cooperate

news.abstract: Selma Dawood, aunt of Tariq Aziz, disavows him and says relationship was cursory at best; Aziz, who has been missing since invasion of Baghdad, was prime minister under Saddam Hussein and well known worldwide as Iraq's voice; Dawood praises American action in Iraq; map; photo (M)
news.title: 'Let Them Arrest Him,' Tariq Aziz's Aunt Says

news.abstract: Serbian government is cracking down on gangsters and criminals under state of emergency imposed after assassination of reformist Prime Min Zoran Djindjic on March 12; police have questioned more than 7,000 people and imprisoned more than 2,000 suspected members of what Serbs like to call the mafia; dragnet is also sweeping up some of most notorious figures from Slobodan Milosevic era, including top army and security officials and others accused of war crimes (M)
news.title: Serbia Cracks Down on Mobsters and War-Crime Suspects

news.abstract: The leaders of Taiwan's two main opposition parties, which together have outpolled the current party in power in recent elections, have agreed to run together on a single ticket in next year's presidential election.    The agreement, between Lien Chan of the Nationalist Party and James Soong of the People First Party, comes after years of personal rivalry. The decision by Mr. Soong to seek the vice presidency as Mr. Lien's running mate, instead of running again for the presidency, gives the two men a strong chance of beating President Chen Shui-bian when he seeks re-election in March, political analysts here said.
news.title: Opposition Figures Team Up To Take On Taiwan President

news.abstract: Reported cases in Beijing of SARS climbed by 249 to 588 as the government continued its belated campaign to give honest figures.
news.title: Reported SARS Cases in Beijing Take Sharp 2-Day Jump

news.abstract: Argentine attorney Luis Moreno Ocampo is elected chief prosecutor of newly established permanent Hague war crimes court, which is expected to begin hearing cases next year; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | United Nations: Argentine Is Elected To New Court

news.abstract: The 79-year-old president of Azerbaijan, Heydar A. Aliyev, collapsed twice during a nationally televised speech there today, prompting fresh questions about the health of a leader considered integral to the stability of his oil-producing country.    Mr. Aliyev, who has a history of heart and other health problems, was addressing a military audience in Baku, the capital of Azerbaijan, when he gasped, clutched his heart, complained of pain and fell. The live television broadcast of his remarks was interrupted while bodyguards rushed over to support him.
news.title: Azerbaijan's Leader Collapses While Delivering TV Speech

news.abstract: In an extraordinary display of the raw power of Iraq's Shiites, the country's long repressed yet dominant Islamic sect, hundreds of thousands converged on this holy city today to perform one of the most important rituals in the Shiite calendar for the first time in a quarter of a century.    The mass pilgrimage, banned under Saddam Hussein, carries as much political as religious significance for the Shiites, who, though they make up the majority of Iraqis, have long lived as second-class citizens under the rule of a Sunni Muslim minority. The procession has a history of turning into a political rally and many who gathered here for the festival that culminates on Wednesday were eager to express their desire to choose their own government without the interference of the United States.
news.title: Elated Shiites, On Pilgrimage, Want U.S. Out

news.abstract: Pentagon raises $1.7 billion in financial assistance, food, medicine and other relief products for Iraq from various countries, including Jordan, United Arab Emirates, Britain, Japan, Australia, Netherlands, Canada, Switzerland and Romania (M)
news.title: Pentagon Reports Raising $1.7 Billion to Assist Relief Effort

news.abstract: Newt Gingrich delivers scathing attack on Bush administration in speech to American Enterprises Institute, charging that State Department under Sec of State Colin L Powell is guilty of pattern of diplomatic failure that weakened America's standing in world and threatens to weaken effects of military victory in Iraq; scores department for enlisting Russia, European Union and United Nations to write plan to establish Palestinian state (S)
news.title: Gingrich Denounces State Department

news.abstract: Health officials report number of people infected with severe acute respiratory syndrom has leveled off in Hong Kong in last week, although disease is unlikely to be eradicated soon, if ever; Hong Kong still has two to three dozen new cases a day and almost as many people hospitalized with SARS as rest of world; area's number of hospitalized probable SARS cases peaked at 960 and has since fallen 9 percent; 34 SARS patients have died, most of them elderly; tentative signs are emerging that residents are accepting SARS as manageable risk and moving on with daily lives; graph of hospitalized patients; photo (M)
news.title: SARS Cases In Hong Kong Have Begun To Level Off

news.abstract: The plan calls for government spending and tax cuts concentrated in the next four months that will equal 1 percent of the territory's entire annual economic output.
news.title: Hong Kong Earmarks $1.5 Billion to Deal With Effects of SARS

news.abstract: European Union spokesman holds that Cuba's recent crackdown on opposition, evidenced by execution of 3 men for hijacking and imprisonment of 75 dissidents, jeopardizes potential trade relations with European Union; holds that damaged relationship is not irreparable as union foreign ministers will not vote on deal with Cuba until June (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Cuba: Trade Pact Threatened

news.abstract: Canada's National Microbiology Laboratory finds virus for severe acute respiratory syndrome in only 40 percent of probable and suspected cases, suprisingly low rate; additionally, portion of recent cases testing positive for virus is declining, and a number of people who are not suspected of having SARS are testing positive; director Dr Frank Plummer says findings have potential to weaken link in Canada between SARS and the previously unknown member of coronavirus family that World Health Organization has said is cause of SARS; stresses he is not challenging WHO's conclusion, but finds results 'weird'; WHO says it continues to believe that new coronavirus is cause of SARS, but is following research developments (M)
news.title: Virus Proves Baffling, Turning Up in Only 40% of a Lab's Test Cases

news.abstract: American envoys complete first day of talks to persuade North Korea to abandon its nuclear weapons program, and China appears to be playing unusually assertive role in keeping lines of communication open; officials and analysts describe China as determined to keep talks going, to soften entrenched positions and to force both sides to focus on how to bring about diplomatic outcome; photo (M)
news.title: China Offers Its Help in U.S.-North Korea Nuclear Talks

news.abstract: Afghani Pres Hamid Karzai asks Pakistan to hand over Taliban members that Afghanistan accuses of being terrorists and says Pakistan is sheltering; names specific Taliban commanders who he says are guilty of atrocities and also behind continuing campaign of violent attacks against Afghan government; Karzai is on two-day state visit to Pakistan; map (M)
news.title: Afghan President Shows Cards In Pakistan's Taliban Deck

news.abstract: WASHINGTON (CNN) -- After an initial search of several sites in Iraq, U.S. investigators have found a clue indicating a U.S. Navy pilot who was shot down in the Gulf War may have been alive years after the fact, Pentagon officials told CNN Wednesday.
news.title: Clue on Missing Gulf War Pilot Is Said to Be Found

news.abstract: Tariq Aziz, the Iraqi deputy prime minister who often served as the public face of Saddam Hussein's government, surrendered to American forces.
news.title: Tariq Aziz Surrenders; Interim Government Near

news.abstract: THE PHILIPPINES: Counterattack Against Rebels; INDONESIA: Peace Talks Collapse; JAPAN: Death Sought For Cult Leader; CAMBODIA: Neighbors Reconcile;.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: Annual Great Spring Festival of Yasukuni Shrine is held to dwindling group of aging relatives of Japan's war dead; it is most hotly disputed shrine of Japan's oldest religion, because mixed in with heroes, celebrated and unknown, are 14 Class A war criminals associated with atrocities committed during World War II; visits to shrine by prime ministers and lesser politicians regularly cause diplomatic crises with Japan's most important neighbors, China and Koreas (M)
news.title: Japan's Shrine to War Dead Worries About Its Generation Gap

news.abstract: ETHIOPIA: Food Shortages Worsen; SUDAN: Tribal Violence;.
news.title: World Briefing: Africa

news.abstract: Government of Hong Kong is assigning broad and expanding role to police in effort to fight spread of infectious disease SARS; officers are taking computer software designed for major criminal investigations and instead entering information on family members and other close contacts of people with SARS; other officers pay three visits daily to homes of people ordered not to go out because someone in their household has confirmed case of disease; new confinement orders are issued for household members of suspected SARS patients as well; tougher measures appear to have broad support in populace terrified of disease that is still infecting 200 more people and killing two dozen each week; photo (M)
news.title: To Broad Support, Hong Kong Police Take On an Expanded Role in Fighting SARS

news.abstract: Palestinian suicide bomber blows himself up when confronted by Israeli security guard at train station in Kfar Saba, Israel, killing guard and wounding 13 Israelis; bombing drives home challenge facing new Palestinian prime minister, Mahmoud Abbas, who will be expected to rein in militants as part of peace initiative; his new government is likely to be formally approved within week, move that will likely bring on peace initiative sponsored by United States, United Nations, European Union and Russia; Israel says any diplomatic progress is contingent on Palestinians' subduing militants; still, Israeli response to attack in Kfar Saba is relatively restrained; Prime Min Ariel Sharon, who shunned Yasir Arafat, is prepared to meet Abbas, opening channel for dialogue that has been largely absent for last two years; militant groups say they will continue their attacks; they claim new government is being forced on Palestinians by US and other foreign govenrments; photo; map (M)
news.title: Suicide Bomber Kills a Guard and Wounds 13 Israelis

news.abstract: PAKISTAN: 13 Are Killed In Crash; THAILAND: A Dream Flight ;.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: Thai Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra is passenger in F-16 fighter jet enroute to air show (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Thailand: A Dream Flight

news.abstract: Winnie Madikizela-Mandela, former wife of Nelson Mandela, is sentenced to four years in prison on dozens of counts of theft and fraud; Addy Moolman, broker and business associate, is sentenced to seven years in prison; Judge Peet Johnson acknowledges Madikizela-Mandela's contributions to building of South Africa's first democracy (M)
news.title: Winnie Mandela Is Sentenced to Four Years for Theft and Fraud

news.abstract: At least six Iraqis were killed today after an attack on an ammunition dump on the outskirts of the city set off powerful explosions in a residential area, the U.S. military said.
news.title: Iraqi Civilians Killed in Blast at Ammunition Storage Site

news.abstract: Profile of Paulo Lins, whose book City of God, and movie of same name, portray extreme violence and poverty of Rio's slums, where Lins grew up in public housing project in 1960's; interview; photo (M)
news.title: Out of the Slums of Rio, an Author Finds Fame

news.abstract: Argentines are set to vote to elect new president, their 6th in little more than year; polls indicate race, among nearly 20 candidates, is too close to call; ex-Pres Carlos Saul Menem narrowly leads field, with Ricardo Lopez Murphy and Nestor Kirchner in dead heat for right to take part in runoff; photos (M)
news.title: A Muddled Electoral Field for Weary Argentines to Cross

news.abstract: Singapore has designated 1,000-bed hospital for SARS, disease that spreads so readily in closed spaces that patients are evaluated outside, in tent; hospital got its first case Mar 1, before disease was known, and many doctors fell ill; hospital now uses four specially ventilated rooms for each patient to insure isolation; medical staff wears special protective garb; photos (M)
news.title: Focusing One Hospital's Resources on One Disease

news.abstract: Flood of Greek and Turk Cypriots are crossing to see each other's side of island divided for almost 30 years, rushing as if uncertain sudden opening will last; respond to abrupt lifting of travel restrictions and opening of two checkpoints by Turkish Cypriot leaders, move that surprised United Nations peacekeepers, police, diplomats and others; menacing buffer zone is still in place, but island is already seeming less divided in people's minds; map; photos (M)
news.title: Greeks and Turks Mingle Peacefully on Cyprus

news.abstract: Baghdad's police force is being slowly reorganized after disbanding in face of US advance, but neighborhood police stations and their officers, who once provided reliable local presence, are still mostly unarmed and waiting for orders; photo (S)
news.title: Dressed Up Amid Disorder, Unarmed Officers Stand Idle

news.abstract: Marine Le Pen is softer, younger side of France's National Front, led by her father, Jean-Marie Le Pen, who has named her vice president; photo; 34-year-old lawyer is most visible spokesperson for far right-wing party, pushing hard in interviews to 'de-demonize' its hard-line image; interview (M)
news.title: The New Face of France's Far Right

news.abstract: Two of Iraq's prominent television news anchors turn up at their war-ruined studios in Baghdad, dressed up and ready for cameras to roll again; they worked for Shabab Television, pet project of Saddam Hussein's son Uday; two portray themselves merely as employees; photo (M)
news.title: Veteran TV Anchors Push to Become the Voices of a New Iraq

news.abstract: The defense secretary told troops at Central Command that they had proved doubters wrong by carrying out a war plan that quickly toppled Saddam Hussein's regime.
news.title: Rumsfeld Visits Troops in Qatar

news.abstract: Outbreak of new respiratory disease SARS inflicts greatest blow to Chinese economy since Tiananmen Square killings in 1989, causing plunge in retail sales, slump in demand for some Chinese exports and near-collapse in domestic and foreign tourism; Chinese economy has gone from expanding at annual rate of 9.9 percent in first quarter to shrinking at annual rate of 2 percent in second quarter, according to estimates from J P Morgan Chase; economic damage is being increased by some government policies adopted to slow spread of SARS, such as ordering closing of all movie theaters, Internet cafes and other places of entertainment in Beijing, or refusing entry to tour groups in Guangdong Province; if current economic downturn proves prolonged, it could damage Communist Party's claim to be best way to offer greater prosperity to 1.3 billion Chinese; photos; graph (L)
news.title: Outbreak of Disease Brings Big Drop-Off In China's Economy

news.abstract: Paraguayan voters appear to be putting their country back in hands of Colorado Party, whose rule has been unbroken since 1947; opposition parties had viewed this election as their best chance of unseating Colorados, with government corruption rife and economy sliding deeper into crisis; Colorado presidential candidate Nicanor Duarte Frutos, apparent winner, campaigned cleverly, playing on people's fears of rising crime and on nostalgia for old days; also called on Colorados' political machine, which prevades nearly all sectors of society, controlling state sector jobs and supplying rural communities with many of their needs; Duarte Frutos, in his victory speech, promises to crack down on corruption (M)
news.title: Paraguay's Voters Appear to Extend Party's 5-Decade Rule

news.abstract: Saddam Hussein's dying government continued to execute suspected spies even as American troops neared huge prison at Abu Ghraib; Iraqis have almost never learned fate of loved ones executed in Hussein's 24 years as president; with Hussein gone, relatives descend on pit just outside prison, unearthing 14 bodies of recently killed prisoners; neighbors say they found 10 more corpses on prison grounds, also recently killed; personal stories told in two weeks since Hussein's fall reveal scale of torture and killing that may surpass predictions of even his worst critics; former inmates say last prisoners at Abu Ghraib were held as spies; thousands of other prisoners there were released in Oct in amnesty declared by Hussein as tensions between Iraq and US grew; photos of Iraqis, with faces covered against stench, digging up shallow graves of executed prisoners (M)
news.title: As Hussein Faded, Prisoners Were Executed

news.abstract: Politicians begin campaigns for May 29 elections for Northern Ireland Assembly despite continuing suspension of legislative body and talks to suspend elections as well; assembly was suspended last October after allegations of IRA paramilitary activity (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Northern Ireland: Elections In Doubt

news.abstract: World Health Orgn is relying on time-tested rule of thumb used by epidemiologists in declaring Vietnam first country to stop its outbreak of SARS; rule says epidemic is over if no new cases occur in time span that is double longest known incubation period of the disease; SARS has 10-day incubation period and no new cases have been detected in Vietnam in 20 days; Vietnam had total of 63 cases and 5 deaths; WHO spokesman gives credit for Vietnam's success to old-fashioned infection-control measures; says there was high level of political commitment there from beginning (M)
news.title: Health Group Relies on a Time-Tested Rule to Determine Last New Case

news.abstract: Following is a full transcript from a speech about Iraq by President Bush yesterday in Dearborn, Mich., as transcribed by Federal News Service Inc.
news.title: Full Text: In Bush's Words

news.abstract: Political gathering of 300 Iraqis from most parts of country and most religious and ethnic factions, sponsored by United States and Britain, decides to call national conference in month's time to select postwar transitional government for Iraq; national conference is to decide whether Iraq wil adopt leadership council or single head of state; Zalmay Khalilzad, Bush administration envoy, is co-chairman of meeting, held in Baghdad; members of Shiite clerical groups are present, as are members of Supreme Council for the Islamic Revolution in Iraq, group with strong ties to Iran that boycotted earlier meeting in Nasiriya; several miles from conference hall, several thousand protesters affiliated with Shiite theological college in Najaf denounce meeting as unrepresentative of religious Shiism; security for Baghdad gathering is extraordinarily tight, partly because large-scale demonstrations are expected to mark Saddam Hussein's 66th birthday; in Tikrit and nearby Awja, Hussein's hometown, demonstrations that members of his family called for are thwarted by stepped-up presence of American troops; two nights earlier, pro-Hussein demonstration in Tikrit left one Iraq man injured and three Iraqi cars crushed by American tanks (M)
news.title: Iraqis Set to Meet to Pick Transitional Government

news.abstract: Judge Leonie M Brinkema orders Justice Dept to provide Zacarias Moussaoui with details to support its theory that he was meant to participate in terrorist hijacking separate from four hijackings that occurred on Sept 11, 2001, in plane that was to crash into White House; he is only person charged in American court with conspiring in Sept 11 attacks; was not allowed to attend hearing in which prosecutors outlined their theory because it involved classified information; Moussaoui acknowledges he was member of Qaeda network and loyal to Osama bin Laden, but he denies any involvement in Sept 11 attacks (M)
news.title: Moussaoui Should Get Details In '5th Plane' Theory, Judge Says

news.abstract: Stock markets rise sharply across East Asia amid hopes that SARS outbreak can be controlled; photo of Hong Kong traders wearing face masks, which are becoming less common on floor of exchange and in streets in city hardest hit by disease; 12 more deaths reported there, bringing total to 150, but there are just 15 new cases (M)
news.title: Stocks Rise in Asia on Hopes That Worst of SARS Is Over

news.abstract: Pentagon sent two of its new 21,500-pound bombs to Persian Gulf but they arrived too late to be used in Iraq war (S)
news.title: Just Too Late: Huge U.S. Bomb

news.abstract: US will withdraw all combat forces from Saudi Arabia by this summer, ending military presence that began as joint operation to contain Saddam Hussein after 1991 Persian Gulf war but has become dangerous for US troops because of terrorism stoked by Osama bin Laden; US anger has also swelled since Sept 11 terrorist attacks in which 15 of 19 hijackers were Saudi; Sec Donald Rumsfeld and Prince Sultan bin Abdul Aziz say in news conference in Riyadh that ouster of Hussein creates 'safer region' that allows pullout; photos; only small longstanding training program will continue; US is already pulling out of sprawling air base for new base in Qatar; prince denies asking US to withdraw, but announcement is broadcast on television; Saudis have suggested departure will help them institute political reforms (M)
news.title: U.S. TO WITHDRAW ALL COMBAT UNITS FROM SAUDI ARABIA

news.abstract: Alan Cowell Letter from Europe on fiftieth anniversary of conquest of Mount Everest by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay; photo; triumph, coming as London prepared for Queen Elizabeth II's coronation, brought flush of pride to Britain, recapturing glory of empire for moment and brightening dreary years after World War II (M)
news.title: To the Top of the World, and Down Again

news.abstract: US will send up to 4,000 soldiers into Baghdad in next few weeks, bringing in more military police and light forces to carry out patrols and improve security; Army units now there often have only tanks and generally sparse US presence makes it difficult to restore order (M)
news.title: U.S. Planning to Regroup Armed Forces in Baghdad, Adding to Military Police

news.abstract: After two suicide bombers in Israel were found to be British citizens, Britain faced suggestions today that young British Muslims had shifted their focus to terrorism in the Middle East.
news.title: British Muslims Are Seen Moving Into Mideast Terrorism

news.abstract: The faltering five-year-old peace effort in Northern Ireland stumbled yet again today when Prime Minister Tony Blair postponed a critical election, blaming the Irish Republican Army for avoiding a "very clear" commitment to end violence.
news.title: Ulster Peace Effort Stumbles Again as Blair Postpones Vote

news.abstract: United States asks officials from 191 countries to reopen negotiations on treaty meant to control sale and use of tobacco; it is scheduled to be adopted month from now at World Health Assembly in Geneva; American negotiators object to treaty's 'no-reservations' clause, which would prevent countries from disregarding any provision they find unacceptable; proposed treaty would place comprehensive ban on advertising and promoting tobacco products, except where prohibition conficts with national constitutions; it would also impose high taxes on tobacco products and expose companies to liability for their products; it would require tobacco companies to divulge all ingredients in their products and print warning labels that cover at least 30 percent of package; it would ban companies from using misleading terms, like ultralight or light; US objection is that certain provisions would override state laws; Democrats in Washington accuse Bush administration of protecting tobacco companies (M)
news.title: U.S. Wants to Reopen Talks On Global Anti-Tobacco Pact

news.abstract: Experts say more than 2,000 objects were stolen from museums in Iraq in wake of Persian Gulf war in 1991, and not more than half dozen of those pieces have been tracked down; many others are presumed to have been traded away through thriving international market in antiquities; poor record of returning artifacts lost after gulf war suggests daunting obstacles that museum officials and police investigators face as they commit to finding items recently sacked from National Museum of Iraq in Baghdad and other sites; photo; map (M)
news.title: Of 2,000 Treasures Stolen in Gulf War of 1991, Only 12 Have Been Recovered

news.abstract: Al Quds al Arabi, London-based Arabic newspaper, prints handwritten letter said to be signed by Saddam Hussein that calls on Iraqis to rise up against American forces, referred to as 'cowardly occupier'; letter was faxed to newspaper's offices and dated Apr 28, Hussein's 66th birthday; newspaper editor Abdel Bari Atwan says letter proves Hussein is still alive and determined to fight back; says he has seen Hussein's signature before and believes letter is 'definitely' his; newspaper describes itself as pan-Arab and independent; it is published in London and New York six times weekly; photo (M)
news.title: A Letter Said to Be From Saddam Hussein Urges Iraqis to Rebel Against the Americans

news.abstract: Pres Bush helps to fly Navy S-3B Viking plane that lands on deck of aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln; emerges from plane, decked out in flight suit, and is swarmed by cheering members of Lincoln's crew; photo (M)
news.title: In Full Flight Regalia, the President Enjoys a 'Top Gun' Moment

news.abstract: Greek Cypriots rush to visit Kyrenia after Turkish Cypriots ease travel across buffer zone that had divided island since 1974; many come to celebrate in little port, eating, drinking and shopping; Turks are joining them as though there never was war that tore them apart; photo; map (M)
news.title: Kyrenia Journal; Beware These Greeks? No, They're Bearing Cash

news.abstract: Mob violence in Babylon, where Saddam Hussein had built vast palace, is particularly forceful; Babylon once existed as powerful myth, reminder that civilization as we know it was born in region; when Hussein began building there, he reduced its remarkable history to kitsch expression of his ego; photos (M)
news.title: Monuments Recall Another Empire That Ignored Writing on the Wall

news.abstract: United States government is being given high marks for its aggressive handling of SARS, even by critics who had accused senior health officials of bungling response to last major health emergency, anthrax attacks of Oct 2001; Health and Human Services Sec Tommy G Thompson speaks of 'whole new feeling of responsiveness'; most experts say SARS has been less of challenge than anthrax, which came without warning; SARS first emerged in China, giving American health officials time to prepare; unlike Canada, where single SARS patient infected dozens of others, US has apparently had no such 'super spreaders'; Thompson is leaving nothing to chance; gets daily briefings and has met twice with Pres Bush to discuss epidemic; shares concerns of some experts that SARS could wane in warm months, then come roaring back in fall; drawing (M)
news.title: Lessons of Anthrax Attacks Help U.S. Respond to SARS

news.abstract: Swiss court denies appeal and makes available former Nigerian dictator Gen Sani Abacha's financial documents; Nigeria is searching for national assets allegedly stolen during Abacha's rule and plans to investigate his Swiss accounts totaling estimated $618 million, which have been frozen since his death; relatives and associates also have interest in ownership of funds and Swiss authorities have demanded assurance from Nigeria that Abacha's widow and sons be treated fairly (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Switzerland: Court Allows Access To Ex-Leader's Files

news.abstract: American troops, having won war in Iraq, are straining to manage anger, frustration and competing ambitions of nation long suppressed by Saddam Hussein; new politicial parties, Kurds and Shiite religious groups are asserting virtual governmental authority in cities and villages across nation, sometimes under noses of American soldiers; educated Iraqis eager for American-led transformation fear Americans may be losing initiative; anti-American sentiment remains palpable; photos (M
news.title: U.S. Is Now in Battle for Peace After Winning the War in Iraq

news.abstract: The six people were arrested in connection with Wednesday's suicide bombing in Tel Aviv that was carried out by a Briton.
news.title: Britain Arrests 6 Linked to Bombing in Israel

news.abstract: Former Shell Oil executive Philip J Carroll and two senior Iraqi oil officials are expected to be appointed as top leaders of struggling Iraqi oil sector by American and Iraqi officials; Carroll is expected to be appointed chairman of advisory committee that will have oversight of Iraqi Oil Ministry (M)
news.title: An American and 2 Iraqis To Assume Key Oil Posts

news.abstract: SARS appears to be spreading in Taiwan as fast or faster than anywhere except mainland China, prompting World Health Organization to prepare to send team there despite risk of creating diplomatic tensions with Beijing; Taiwan announces that it has 11 more confirmed cases, number that has more than tripled in last 10 days; five people die of SARS in Taiwan, raising its death toll to eight; chart shows outbreak in Taiwan; photo (M)
news.title: SARS Spreads in Taiwan; W.H.O. Plans Trip There

news.abstract: Structure of American administration of postwar Iraq remains unresolved, as Defense Sec Donald Rumsfeld issues strong endorsement of Jay Garner, retired lieutenant general whose job seemed about to be eclipsed by L Paul Bremer (M)
news.title: Iraq's U.S. Overseer Is Praised by Rumsfeld

news.abstract: Sec of State Colin L Powell meets with Pres Bashar al-Assad in Damascus and says Syria has begun closing offices of at least some militant anti-Israeli groups in Damascus as demanded by US; groups are identified as Hamas, Popular Front for Liberation of Palestine-General Command and Palestinian Islamic Jihad; closings appear to be breakthrough in dealing with Syria, which has had an up-and-down relationship with US over years and more recently has been labeled by some American officials as junior member of 'axis of evil' because of its tolerance of groups' presence; Powell also demands that Syria turn over any Iraqi leaders hiding in Syria and ensure that no weapons are flowing from Syria into Iraq now that American occupation is encountering some attacks in parts of country; also expresses concern about Syrian support for Hezbollah, Shiite group that is active in Lebanon and has lobbed missiles into Israel; photo (M)
news.title: POWELL SAYS SYRIA IS TAKING ACTION ON TERROR GROUPS

news.abstract: Pres Bush says weapons of mass destruction will be found in Iraq but it will take time because Saddam Hussein spent so many years hiding his stockpile; remarks reflect growing concern in administration that opponents of war will claim that US exaggerated evidence against Iraq in order to justify attack that was intended to depose Hussein; Bush's senior aides have begun backing away from prewar claims that Hussein had arsenal that was loaded and ready to fire, saying that instead he developed 'just in time' production strategy for his weapons, hiding chemical precursors that could be quickly loaded into empty artillery shells or short-range missiles; no evidence has been found that he did so; photo of Bush in Crawford, Tex, with Prime Min John Howard of Australia (M)
news.title: Bush Says It Will Take Time to Find Iraq's Banned Arms

news.abstract: Amram Mitzna's resignation is a sign of the disarray hobbling Israel's left, but it seems unlikely to affect the new peace process immediately.
news.title: Leader of Israel's Labor Party Resigns

news.abstract: David Hicks, 27-year-old Australian who converted to Islam, fought with Taliban in Afghanistan and was captured by Northern Alliance forces in Kandahar in December 2001, is now being held at US naval base in Guantanamo, Cuba, and has become thorny issue in US-Australian relations; US, seeking to reduce number of detainees, wants Australia to take custody of Hicks and prosecute him, but Australian authorities are not pressing US for his release and doubt if he can be prosecuted under Australian law; Hicks has only small support group in Australia, but government is criticized in some quarters for abandoning him; his family describes him as rebel searching for a cause; photo (M)
news.title: A Drifter's Oddysey From the Outback to Guantánamo

news.abstract: The Chinese submarine accident that killed 70 crew members occurred more than two weeks before it was officially revealed, a naval officer has been reported as saying.
news.title: Engine Trouble Suspected in China Submarine Disaster, Newspaper Says

news.abstract: Bush administration officials said today that they would soon release an additional group of prisoners, about a dozen, from the detention center in Guantánamo Bay, Cuba.
news.title: U.S. to Free More Afghan War Prisoners From Guantánamo

news.abstract: Iraqis turned their attention to sports and entertainment Sunday, leisure activities that had all but disappeared during the war.
news.title: Some Fun Returns to Baghdad

news.abstract: Kanan Makiya, author and architect who has been among Saddam Hussein's most prominent critics, finally visits infamous monument he wrote about but never saw, called 'crossed swords,' gargantuan archway in Baghada erected as tribute to Hussein and his army in late 1980's; Mikiya says it stands as monument to vulgarization of Iraqi culture under Hussein; photo (M)
news.title: Exile Sees Lessons in Iraqi Grandiosity

news.abstract: Militant Palestinian groups in Damascus challenge American statements that Syria has cracked down on them; Syria's government sidesteps issue, refusing to confirm one of few Syrian concessions that seems to emerge during weekend visit by Secretary of State Colin L Powell (M)
news.title: Militant Palestinian Groups Dispute Powell's Report of a Crackdown by Damascus

news.abstract: Iraqi women view newfound religious freedoms nervously; Iraq does not have history of religious fundamentalism; fear among some women is that conservative Muslim religious leaders will fill power vacuum that has ensued since war ended; Iraq's women enjoyed near parity with men for several decades through 1970's; when Saddam Hussein took power, their rights were curtailed; restrictions he imposed, as well as recent social conservatism, come as blow to older, educated women, who fought against head scarves, arranged marriages and other constraints; their hope is that United States will not allow religious leader to run government; photo (M)
news.title: IRAQI WOMEN WARY OF NEW UPHEAVALS

news.abstract: Hague war crimes tribunal indicts Jovica Stanisic, Slobodan Milosevic's former secret police chief, and Franko Simatovic, founder of paramilitary group accused of assassinating Serbian Prime Minister Zoran Djindjic (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Serbia: Hague Tribunal Indicts 2

news.abstract: Sales of antiviral drug Zadaxin surge because doctors in China are using it in attempt to contain widening outbreak of SARS; drug is produced by small American biotechnology company SciClone Pharmaceuticals; it is not yet approved for use in United States, Europe or Japan; SciClone president Donald R Sellers says Chinese are probably trying many drugs; Zadaxin is currently being tested by US government scientists, who are screening thousands of compounds in hopes of finding some that may work against SARS (M)
news.title: Sales of U.S. Company's Drug Rise as Chinese Try It Against SARS

news.abstract: L. Paul Bremer will outrank Jay Garner, the retired Army lieutenant general who has been in charge of postwar administration in Iraq.
news.title: In Victory for Powell, Bush Names Civilian Overseer for Iraq

news.abstract: Monument dedicated to Nobel Peace prize winner Andrei D Sakharov is unveiled in St Petersburg; Yelena Bonner, his widow, has opposed tribute stating display is inappropriate given current condition of human rights in Russia; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Monument Honors Sakharov

news.abstract: Colombia's Marxist guerrillas execute provincial governor, former minister of justice and eight others they had been holding hostage in mountains of northern Colombia; victims bodies are found by elite combat troops dropped into heavily forested areas; three soldiers who had also been held captive survive the ordeal; rebels, members of Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), blame soldiers for touching off violence; rebels continue to hold three American defense contractors as well as dozens of Colombian politicians and soldiers (M)
news.title: Rebels Execute 10 Hostages In Colombia

news.abstract: Statistical analysis of 1,425 patients suspected of having SARS who were admitted to Hong Kong hospitals from Feb 20 to Apr 15 suggests death rate from SARS could be up to 55 percent in people 60 and older and 13.2 percent in younger people, for overall rate of 19.9 percent, far higher than health officials had thought; unless numbers fall drastically, SARS would be among infectious diseases with highest death rates; difficulty of calculating mortality rates for newly emerging diseases noted; photo (M)
news.title: Study Suggests A Higher Rate Of SARS Death

news.abstract: British authorities arrest 18-year-old man for murder of American artist Margaret Muller; Muller was living in London when she was stabbed to death in busy East London park while on her morning jog; more than 100 witnesses participated in crime reconstruction (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: Arrest In American's Killing

news.abstract: The findings were not conclusive as of today, and may not be for some time, but they were nevertheless important, for the White House and the Pentagon.
news.title: U.S. Tests Iraqi Vehicle Suspected as Mobile Weapons Lab

news.abstract: SPAIN: Work To Resume On Sunken Tanker; BRITAIN: Lawmaker Suspended Over Iraq Remarks; BRITAIN: Arrest In American'S Killing; BRITAIN: Fat Cat;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: American soldiers from special mobile exploitation team work with members of opposition Iraqi National Congress to search secret police headquarters, Baghdad, for seventh century copy of Jewish Talmud, one of most ancient copies in existence; fail to unearth text, but instead find trove of Iraqi intelligence documents and maps relating to Israel and data on offer by 'holy warrior' to sell uranium and other nuclear materials to Iraq; photo (M)
news.title: Iraqi Documents on Israel Surface on a Cultural Hunt

news.abstract: Senior Bush administration officials say joint British-American team of experts concluded that tractor-trailer truck found in northern Iraq several weeks ago could be mobile biological weapons lab; say it closely fits description given by defector but cannot say whether it has ever produced biological agents for weapons; van was seized Apr 19 at checkpoint controlled by Kurdish allies in northern Iraq; when Secretary of State Colin L Powell addressed United Nations in Feb, he cited defector's report on mobile labs that could develop unconventional weapons and be moved around Iraq to avoid detection and attack; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Aides Say Iraqi Truck Could Be a Germ-War Lab

news.abstract: Deputy Secretary of State Richard L. Armitage said he was "cautiously optimistic" about the renewal of diplomatic relations between India and Pakistan.
news.title: Armitage 'Optimistic' About Renewed India-Pakistan Dialogue

news.abstract: Pete Townshend, rock guitarist and co-founder of Who, is given formal police caution and placed on official register of sex offenders for having gained access to pedophile Web site in Jan; court in London clears him of more serious charge of being in possession of indecent pictures downloaded from Internet; police say his name will be removed from register after five years, barring any new incident; he admits using credit card to enter Web site advertising child pornography; claims he was doing research for autobiography that would chronicle his suspected abuse as child; spokesman for group representing child-abuse victims voices outrage at what it considers leniency of Townshend's punishment (M)
news.title: British Rock Star Receives Lesser Punishment in Internet Case

news.abstract: Israeli attack helicopters fired three missiles that killed a senior Hamas militant driving in Gaza City today, and Israeli troops also shot dead two Palestinians in separate confrontations.
news.title: Israeli Missile Strike Kills Hamas Militant

news.abstract: President Bush met with the foreign ministers of the seven East European countries and thanked them for their support of American policy on Iraq.
news.title: Senate Votes Unanimously to Approve Expansion of NATO

news.abstract: President Bush, continuing to wield diplomatic leverage gained from a decisive victory in Iraq, proposed a new free trade zone for the Middle East.
news.title: Bush Proposes Free Trade Zone for Middle East

news.abstract: Groups of tourists from Europe have been seized in Algerian desert region of Illizi in last few months; their fate, and who took them, are unknown; region is known for drug and gun-smuggling, but it might also provide hideaways for Islamic militant group which has long waged war against Algeria's secular government; in all, 31 tourists are missing: 15 Germans, 10 Austrians, 4 Swiss, a Swede and a Dutchman; no ransom demands have been reported; most of missing people are said to be experienced adventure travelers, equipped with global positioning satellite navigation equipment and satellite telephones; governments involved refuse almost all but most cursory comment; Algeria has reportedly sent 5,000 troops, aided by 300 local guides, to desert to look for missing tourists; Algerian tourism official has been quoted as saying they are alive and that negotiations are taking place to win their release; photo; map (L)
news.title: Tourists Seized In the Sahara, But by Whom?

news.abstract: Britons Paveen Akthor Sharif, Tahari Shad Tabassum and Zahid Hussain Sharif, detained by British police for possible connection with suicide bombing in Tel Aviv, are charged and will appear in court today; three others being held are released; Tel Aviv bombing was carried out by Asif Hanif, who is from London, and Omar Khan Sharif of Derbyshire; Sharif fled scene when his suicide bomb failed to detonate (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: 3 Charged In Tel Aviv Bombing

news.abstract: Deputy State Sec Richard L Armitage meets with Pres Pervez Musharraf and other Pakistani officials in Islamabad; then says he is 'cautiously optimistic' about prospect for renewed relations between India and Pakistan; says Musharraf has assured him that infiltration by Islamic militants from Pakistan into part of Kashmir controlled by India has stopped, and that any militant camps found in Pakistan will be closed; India and Pakistan have suprised many with their sudden overtures for peace in last two weeks; Armitage says he hopes to encourage dialogue between two countries over Kashmir (M)
news.title: U.S. Official Is 'Optimistic' On India-Pakistan Dispute

news.abstract: Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld says senior Baath Party members will not be allowed to hold positions of authority in postwar Iraq; says Iraqis installed in official jobs may be removed after their initial appointment if subsequent review by American authorities finds official had been senior Baath Party member; Rumsfeld's comments are important because some Iraqis are already complaining that former senior Baath Party officials are being given top jobs in new Iraqi government or in prominent Iraqi institutions; photo (M)
news.title: Top Baathist Officials to Be Barred From Government

news.abstract: SPAIN: Election Ban On Radical Basque Parties; BRITAIN: Israel Bombing Suspect'S Relatives In Court;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: UN sends first team of human rights investigators to Iraq for long-term missionto help distribute aid and handle rights complaints (S)
news.title: AFTEREFFECTS: Briefly Noted; U.N. SENDS TEAM TO IRAQ

news.abstract: Thiry health care workers at Mount Sinai Hospital in Toronto are quarantined after hospital administrator comes down with respiratory symptoms that could be SARS(S)
news.title: Colleague Ill, So 30 Toronto Hospital Workers Are in Quarantine

news.abstract: US sets aside latest Mideast peace plan for now to press both Israel and Palestinians to take immediate steps to ease tensions; progress doubted as Sec Colin Powell leaves for region (S)
news.title: U.S. Shifts Its Mideast Focus To Press for Easing of Tension

news.abstract: British police disclose identities of three people being held in connection with Tel Aviv (Israel) suicide bombing as sister, brother and wife of Omar Khan Sharif; Sharif is still at large and is wanted by Israeli security forces; bomb he was wearing failed to detonate and he fled scene (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: Israel Bombing Suspect's Relatives In Court

news.abstract: An Iranian opposition group in Iraq agreed to hand over its weapons to the U.S.-led coalition that toppled Saddam Hussein's regime.
news.title: Iranian Group Disarms

news.abstract: Editors' note on New York Times's investigation into reporting of Jayson Blair, who has resigned as reporter after discovery of instances of plagiarism and falsification
news.title: Editors' Note

news.abstract: Deputy State Sec Richard L Armitage concludes three-day visit to South Asia, hailing new peace initiative by Indian Prime Min Atal Bihari Vajpayee with neighboring Pakistan as 'far-reaching at of statesmanship' (M)
news.title: American Official Praises India's Move to Defuse Tensions With Pakistan

news.abstract: Iraqis tell of civilian casualties during weeks of war and allied bombing in Iraq; determining number of civilian casualties is proving difficult; photo (M)
news.title: For Family That Lost 10 to Allied Bomb, Only Memories and Grief Remain

news.abstract: Shiite leader Ayatollah Muhammad Bakr al-Hakim returns to Iraq from exile and immediately rejects liberal Western-style democracy as incompatible with country's Islamic culture; says Iraq must base its laws on Islamic strictures; says new Iraqi government must be elected and be representative of all ethnic and religous groups, not only majority Shiites; his emphasis on elected government and national unity reflects marked shift in tone for Shiite leaders after fervent calls for Islamic state in initial euphoria after collapse of Saddam Hussein's regime; Ayatollah Hakim has spent much of his life outside Iraq fighting to overthrow Hussein, who deported and killed thousands of Shiites in relentless campaign to silence dissident religious leaders; he is also one of few senior clerics who openly challenged Hussein and survived assassination, because Iran sheltered and financed him for 23 years; his views are expected to help shape Iraq's political future; photo (M)
news.title: Back in Iraq, A Cleric Urges Islamic Rules

news.abstract: It was the first visit to Beirut by an Iranian president since the 1979 Islamic revolution, and it is being closely watched by the U.S.
news.title: Khatami Arrives in Lebanon to Crowds, Chants and Cheers

news.abstract: Mass grave uncovered near Basra, Iraq, is thought to contain remains of those killed in Shiite Muslim uprisings in 1991 and 1999; family and friends come to site to dig up bones and grieve for dead; photo; map (M)
news.title: Mass Grave Is Unearthed Near Basra

news.abstract: Iraq's only hospital providing long-term care for chronic schizophrenia and other serious mental disorders was all but destroyed during war, leaving patients to wander off; some got shot and killed, others got raped by looters; of more than 1,400 Iraqis institutionalized at Al Rashad state hospital in Baghdad, 300 remain; Iraqi psychiatric staff accuses marines of standing by as looters carried away everything within hospital; staff says marines then broke door down on maximum security wing and patients fled, untethered from antipsychotic drugs that stabilized many of them; Red Cross has spent $1.5 million over last three years bringing facility almost to Western standards for compassionate care to mentally ill; Dr Olaf Rosset, Norwegian who has overseen project, says he asked US military commanders to send troops to provide security, but they did so only after hospital was all but destroyed; psychiatrists at hospital meet with desperate Iraqis who plead for help in handling disturbed family members who returned home after escaping from hospital; photo (L)
news.title: In Baghdad's Anarchy, the Insane Went Free

news.abstract: American intelligence officials conclude that North Korean leader Kim Jong Il went into seclusion during final buildup to war in Iraq because he feared he too might be target of attack; Pentagon is considering new ways to hold him and his inner circle at risk as way of bolstering deterrence on peninsula; military's ability to mount precision attacks on leadership targets in Iraq is being examined to see how it might apply in tense standoff with North Korea, perhaps influencing North Korea's behavior without ever firing shot; photo (M)
news.title: Lessons From Iraq Include How to Scare Korean Leader

news.abstract: Ayatollah Muhammad Bakr al-Hakim, longtime opponent of Saddam Hussein who spent last 32 years in exile in Iran, is expected to enter Najaf and assert his claim to speak for Iraq's long-suppressed Shiites in negotiations for postwar government; his return to Iraq has not generated much excitement so far; many Iraqis are especially suspicious of former exiles who spent years outside country and have now returned to help organize transitional goverment; photo (M)
news.title: Iraqis More Bemused Than Enthused by Cleric
