news.abstract: Truck loaded with explosives blows up near government complex in northern Chechnya, killing at least 41 people and wounding scores more; officials call it suicidal terrorist attack; region has until now escaped worst of Russia's war against Chechen separatists; none of Chechnya's known separatist groups claims responsibilty for attack; it is worst violence there since Russia held constitutional referendum in March as part of Kremlins's efforts to hasten peaceful end to war after 44 months of violence; Pres Vladimir V Putin says attack is intended to disrupt efforts to foster stability in Chechnya under loose political federation with Russia; photo; map (M)
news.title: 41 Die in Suicide Bombing in Chechnya

news.abstract: Four separate overnight bombing attacks strike Western targets in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on eve of Secretary of State Colin L Powell's visit there, causing undetermined number of deaths and dozens of injuries; United States Embassy in Riyadh says 44 Americans are injured, some seriously; local press reports deaths of one Saudi, one Lebanese and one Westerner; casualty figures are expected to rise; Powell says violence is likely work of Al Qaeda, saying it bears its hallmarks; says Al Qaeda has been weakened but not destroyed; live pictures from scene attest to power of blasts at apartment compounds that are home to American, British, Italian and other Westerners, as well as to Saudis and citizens of other Middle Eastern countries; Saudi Interior Min Prince Nayef says first three blasts were suicide bombings set off by cars stuffed with explosives driven into targeted compounds; attackers strike after State Dept's extraordinarily specific warning on May 1 that terrorists would soon attack American targets in Saudi Arabia; there was botched attempt by Saudi security services to seize cell that Interior Ministry accused of being linked to Al Qaeda terrorist network; 19 suspected militants escaped, but police seized huge arms cache; photos; map (L)
news.title: EXPLOSIONS ROCK WESTERN ENCLAVES IN SAUDI CAPITAL

news.abstract: The Israeli prime minister dismissed as not "on the horizon" any talk of changing settlement policy.
news.title: Sharon Sets Hard Line on Settlements Policy

news.abstract: Philip J Carroll, American official charged by Bush administration with broad oversight of Iraqi oil industry, says he understands that his appointment is viewed by many Iraqis and others in Arab world as American grab for country's vast oil wealth; says he will take initial approach of learning from Iraqis already working there and of keeping low profile; says he will try to calm concerns among members of Orgn of Petroleum Exporting Countries that Iraq, under American pressure, would abandon cartel; says Iraq's membership is not for US government to decide; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Official Treads Carefully In Overseeing Iraq Oil Industry

news.abstract: Security Council ambassadors discuss possibility of inviting foreign military force to help avert any increase in violence in Ituri province of Democratic Republic of Congo, where power vacuum has emerged since troops from neighboring Uganda withdrew (M)
news.title: U.N. Council May Request Foreign Force For Congo

news.abstract: Former Pres Carlos Menem reportedly withdraws from Argentine runoff election and then retracts resignation after aides convince him not to give up uphill battle for third term; withdrawal would give Nestor Kirchner victory by default (S)
news.title: Former Argentine Leader Still in Presidential Race

news.abstract: Prime Min Ariel Sharon dismisses idea of restraining Israeli settlements and rejects suggestions that US is pressuring him to do so to promote new peace plan (M)
news.title: Sharon Rules Out Dismantling Settlements

news.abstract: German researchers say that experimental Pfizer drug AG-7088, which was tested and shelved as common cold remedy, may, with some chemical tinkering, be used to fight SARS virus; Pfizer did not apply for FDA approval and modification would take several years; researcher Dr David Ho says in Hong Kong that he and colleages at Aaron Diamond AIDS Research Center in New York have synthesized several peptides that could prevent SARS from entering human cells, but that will also take years of testing (M)
news.title: Experimental Drug May Fight SARS, Researchers Say

news.abstract: President Vladimir V. Putin and Secretary of State Colin L. Powell met in the Kremlin and failed to resolve most of their differences involving the future of Iraq.
news.title: Powell Gets Warm Words in Moscow but No Deal on Iraq

news.abstract: GERMANY: Neo-Nazi Crime Up; GERMANY: Bird Flu Confirmed; ITALY: Berlusconi Says He Will Sue Over Insults; IRELAND: Landmark Saved;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Patriotic Union of Kurdistan, Kurdish political party working with United States to shape interim government in Iraq, pushes ahead quietly on three oil development projects, acting autonomously as local government; party has signed production-sharing contracts with two Turkish companies to develop and survey oilfields in northeast Iraq, and has agreed to allow Australian company to do surveying work in eastern Iraq; photo (M)
news.title: Kurdish Group Takes Autonomous Role in Iraq Oil Projects

news.abstract: United States Amb John D Negroponte says he expects Security Council to vote next week on new draft resolution lifting sanctions and recognizing forces that defeated and occupied Iraq as legal authority in country; photo (M)
news.title: U.N. Vote on Iraq Authority Is Due Next Week, U.S. Says

news.abstract: About 300 violent criminals have been arrested in the last 48 hours as part of a security clampdown, the new American administrator for Iraq said today.
news.title: Bremer Says U.S. Is Tackling Security Problem in Baghdad

news.abstract: Proposal by Bush administration to allow development of new kinds of small nuclear weapons is rejected by Republican-controlled House Armed Services Committee (S)
news.title: Panel Rejects Nuclear Arms Of Small Yield

news.abstract: Seventeeen European tourists held captive in Sahara in Algeria are released unharmed after Algerian armed forces raid camp said to be controlled by militant Islamic group; 15 other travelers missing since Mar are still unaccounted for; senior German official terms their situation 'precarious'; freed tourists--10 Austrians, 6 Germans and Swede--were held by members of Salafist Group for Preaching and Combat; group has been fighting guerrilla war against secular Algerian government and is beleived to have ties to Al Qaeda; freed captives appear healthy as they arrive home; it is unclear whether there is any connection between their release and recent visit to Algiers of German Foreign Min Joschka Fischer; photos; map (M)
news.title: 17 Tourists Abducted in Sahara Are Freed in Army Raid

news.abstract: Germany's top officials said today that they wanted to reach an agreement on the U.N. resolution on Iraq that is being pressed by Britain and the United States.
news.title: Germans Edge Toward U.S. Stance on U.N. Iraq Resolution

news.abstract: World Health Orgn officials say outbreak of SARS in Taiwan is being inaccurately counted and is probably much bigger than reported; official Taiwan tally is 264 cases with 34 deaths; Dr Lee Ming-liang, former health minister leading fight against epidemic, says Taiwan would conform to WHO standards in reporting outbreak, and that when it does, there may be many more probable cases; disease has spread to another major hospital in Taipei, infecting 7 doctors and nurses said to be wearing full infection gear, and ambulance drivers, one of whom dies (M)
news.title: Number of Cases in Taiwan May Be More Than Reported

news.abstract: Pres Vladimir V Putin of Russia offers to grant amnesty to Chechen separatists who agree to lay down their arms by Aug 1; offer excludes any accused of murder, rape, kidnapping or other crimes; proposal comes after two suicide attacks in Chechnya this week killed at least 77 people and shattered Kremlin's latest assertions that peace and stability in republic are at hand after 44 months of war; proposal, submitted to lower house of Parliament for vote, appears to be effort to regain political initiative that Putin administration hoped to sustain after voters approved new constitution for Chechnya in Mar; Putin calls amnesty proposal 'an act of humanism'; it remains to be seen whether offer will entice significant numbers of Chechen fighters to accept return to civilian life under Russian rule (M)
news.title: Putin Offers an Amnesty Plan Covering Most Chechen Rebels

news.abstract: Bush administration officials say that in month before bombings in Riyadh, United States asked Saudi Arabia on at least five separate occasions to deploy armed uniformed government guards around all Western targets of possible terrorist attack; say one request was made by Stephen J Hadley, deputy national security adviser, in May 5 meeting with Crown Prince Abdullah, kingdom's day-to-day leader; say Saudi authorities did nothing to augment security at any of sites; Saudi ambassador to US Prince Bandar bin Sultan says Saudi security agencies concluded that they had adequate measures in place; notes near impossibility of deterring 'determined, crazy, evil person'; other Saudi officials point out that there are hundreds of potential Western targets in kingdom; American officials acknowledge that at no time did US specify which sites it wanted guarded; say precise nature of attacks in Riyadh raises questions about their assumption that they had successfully reined in Al Qaeda (M)
news.title: Five Requests to Saudis Went Unheeded, U.S. Says

news.abstract: Lebanese government officials say Lebanese Army, helped by Syrian intelligence, arrested nine Islamic militants in northern Lebanon who were plotting attack on United States Embassy in Beirut; say men were also planning to take one or more government officials hostage as bargaining chip in efforts to free 30 militants of Sunni Muslim extremist movement arrested in government crackdown two years ago; Army spokesman says movement, Redemption and Dawn of Islam, adheres to strict Wahhabi branch dominant in Saudi Arabia; says 7 of men are Lebanese and two Palestinians, and that explosives and detonators were also seized during arrests (M)
news.title: Lebanon Says Arrests Foiled Attack on the U.S. Embassy

news.abstract: At least 14 people are killed in several explosions in Casablanca, Morocco, as attackers use car bombs and detonate another device to strike Jewish, Spanish and Belgian targets; Interior Min Mostafa Sahel tells reporters that attacks 'bear the hallmark of international terrorism'; says that 10 suicide bombers were also killed anddddthat 60 other people were injured (M)
news.title: Suicide Bombs Kill at Least 14 In Casablanca

news.abstract: It is called the Tour d'Afrique and, like the Tour de France, it is a grueling, multiple-stage bicycle race.
news.title: Bicyclists near end of Cairo-to-Cape Town race : 4 long months on 2 wheels

news.abstract: Some 70 more American law enforcement and intelligence officials leave for Saudi Arabia after Saudi government approves tripling size of team probing terrorist bombing attacks on three Western residential complexes in Riyadh; Saudi official Adel al-Jubeir calls bombings 'massive jolt,' news conference, Washington; says government will work with United States and do whatever is needed to halt internal terrorism; admits government had not responded in days before attacks to urgent American requests for tightening of security around Western compounds; details aggressive and determined Saudi effort against terrorism; holds nation is being unfairly tarred by critics, including anonymous Bush administration officials; Federal Bureau of Investigation Dir Robert Mueller and Atty Gen John Ashcroft laud initial Saudi probe; photo (M)
news.title: Saudis Triple Bomb Inquiry; Vow Joint Antiterror Effort

news.abstract: Nisha Sharma becomes overnight sensation in India by calling police to her wedding and having groom arrested after free-for-all between their families over his family's last-minute demand for larger dowry; dowries, illegal for many decades in India, are now often disguised by families as gifts to give newlyweds a start in life; more than a media creation, Sharma and her dowry defiance strike chord in nation, whose expanding middle class is rebelling against dowry tradition that is being overfed by new commercialism; photo (M)
news.title: Dowry Too High. Lose Bride and Go to Jail.

news.abstract: Spanish Deputy Prime Minister Mariano Rajoy expresses government's anger over video of ETA, Basque separatist group, in which three hooded members urge viewers to vote for outlawed candidates; video was aired on Basque public television station Euskal Irrati Telebista and is under investigation by state prosecutor (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Spain: Anger At Broadcast

news.abstract: Euro is growing into rival to dollar, making up all ground it lost after its introduction in 1999; more important, it has gained stature as safe haven for investors and governments; with US running up vast deficits, economists say euro has chance to consolidate gains; photo; charts show growth of euro against dollar and as percentage of world's foreign exchange reserves (M)
news.title: Euro Beginning to Flex Its Economic Muscles

news.abstract: Iraq's old currency, so-called Saddam dinar, skyrockets in value, soaring by about one-third against dollar, and is now at highest value since 1996; bill bears portrait of former dictator Saddam Hussein; dinar's surge along with dollar's plunge have wiped out purchasing power of $20 emergency payments being handed out to workers, who have been grumbling that it was poor substitute for pay, which they have not received since March; photo (M)
news.title: His Face Still Gives Fits As Saddam Dinar Soars

news.abstract: Suicide bomber attacks bus in Jerusalem, killing at least six people and wounding more than 20; attack comes hours after Israeli Prime Min Ariel Sharon and Palestinian Prime Min Mahmoud Abbas hold talks; Sharon cancels trip to US, during which he was scheduled to see Pres Bush; other violence, which is thought to be in response to peace efforts, described; second blast occurs on outskirts of city, but no once except bomber is killed; police say bus bomber was disguised as observant Jew; no claim is made for bombing; photo (M)
news.title: In Bus Attack, a Jerusalem Suicide Bomber Kills 6 and Wounds More Than 20

news.abstract: The group said the administrator, L. Paul Bremer III, has failed to support the rapid creation of an Iraqi-led interim government.
news.title: Iraqi Shiite Group Criticizes U.S. Civilian Administrator

news.abstract: AIDS is imperiling many Caribbean countries as it spreads into population; infection rate there is highest outside Africa; health experts and political leaders warn of potential for devastation in region of small, image-conscious countries that depend on limited pool of labor and resources, as well as tourism; 40,000 adults and children in Caribbean are believed to have died of disease in 2001 alone; it is leading cause of death among young men; epidemic's full extent is obscured by fear, denial, limited treatment and lack of public health resources; estimated 2.4 percent of Caribbean's adult population is thought to be infected with HIV; migration between islands--and United States--is common and helps spread disease; medications remain unavailable in many places, and on many islands hospitals and doctors lack will or resources to treat HIV-positive patients, bouncing them from clinic to clinic; photos; map; chart (L)
news.title: As AIDS Ravages Caribbean, Governments Confront Denial

news.abstract: Speculation grows that suicide bombing attacks in Casablanca at five separate sites that killed 41 people, including 13 bombers, might have blended order from abroad with homegrown organization; Moroccan authorities are calling attacks highly coordinated terrorist operation linked to sophisticated international terrorist network; but fact that suicide bombers' likely target, sprawling Jewish cemetery, escaped harm, and that three young Muslim men are among victims, lends amateur quality to events; King Mohammed VI arrives in Casablanca to show his direct involvement in aftermath of attacks; stops at several bombed sites, including hotel, Jewish cultural center and private Spanish club; says he has asked Interior Ministry and security services to investigate 'in full transparency' and to keep public informed of developments; photos (M)
news.title: In Casablanca Neighborhood, Ruptured Calm

news.abstract: Israeli officials and Palestinians say two Palestinian suicide bombers who killed themselves and nine other people in explosions 12 hours apart over weekend in Hebron and Jerusalem appear to have been working in concert; note bombers lived block apart in Hebron, belonged to militant Hamas movement and carried out their attacks disguised as religiously observant Jews; in Hebron, single mourning tent is set up for two bombers, and coffee and candy is handed out to friends and relatives who gather; Israeli troops surround street and order people to leave; Palestinian information min Nabil Amr condemns bombings (M)
news.title: Israelis Say 2 Bombers Appeared to Be a Team

news.abstract: The rally combined a religious event with a political protest against the American military presence and Washington's plans for a future Iraqi government.
news.title: Thousands of Iraqis Rally to Protest U.S. Moves in Baghdad

news.abstract: Louisiana crawfish, brought to Lake Massaciuccoli in Tuscany more than decade ago as culinary experiment, has multiplied greatly, wreaking havoc on native crawfish and throwing life in lake out of whack; biologists have deployed thousands of pike into lake to combat invader crawfish; photos; map (M)
news.title: Massaciuccoli Journal; The Killer From Louisiana, on the Loose in Italy

news.abstract: Cuba's leading dissident today faulted the Communist government on the island for manipulating fears of an American invasion to justify its harsh line on opposition.
news.title: Cuban Dissident Says Castro Uses Invasion Fear as Ploy

news.abstract: Pres Bush defends administration's peace plan for Middle East as aides scramble to revive Israeli-Palestinian discussions in face of five bomb attacks on Israelis in three days; says road to peace will be bumpy; despite his hopeful words, some administration officials concede that little can be done to sustain delicate momentum of peace effort if suicide bombings of last few days continue; say their first priority is to keep pressing Palestinian Prime Minister Mahmoud Abbas to take action against Hamas, Aksa Martyrs Brigades and other groups that have taken responsibility for bombing attacks against Israel; Prime Min Ariel Sharon of Israel is coming under pressure from conservatives in his cabinet to act against Yasir Arafat; State Dept says it is still American policy to discourage Israel from expelling Arafat from West Bank; photos (M)
news.title: Bush Insists Mideast Peace Plan Will Move Forward, Despite Bombings

news.abstract: Fifth Palestinian suicide bomber to strike against Israelis in less than 48 hours detonates shrapnel-packed bomb outside mall in northern town of Afula, killing security guard and two bystanders, wounding more than 50 others and delivering new blow to peace effort that is already reeling; blast so disfigures dead that hours later authorities are still trying to identify bomber among remains; police say they believe bomber was woman; latest attack is part of what Israeli police call 'wave of terror' that has greeted most intensive international effort to date to end 31-month conflict; Pres Bush says new international place plan 'still stands,' but Israeli officials say violence has strengthened their resolve to substantially change plan, which lays out reciprocal concessions to achieve peace and Palestinian state in three years; senior Israeli security official says new attacks are aimed both at Israel and at Mahmoud Abbas, first Palestinian prime minister, who has promised to disarm militant groups; photos (L)
news.title: 3 ISRAELIS KILLED AND 50 WOUNDED IN BLAST AT MALL

news.abstract: World Health Orgn reports no cases of SARS have been transmitted on airline flights since late Mar, after it recommended that countries and airlines screen passengers and crew members departing from affected areas; says most recent affected flight was on Mar 23, from Bangkok to Beijing, four days before it made its recommendations on air travel; Taiwan, which is battling epidemic of SARS, is unsuccessful in its effort to use disease as reason to gain observer status in WHO; photo (M)
news.title: No Cases of SARS Have Been Transmitted on Airlines Since March, W.H.O. Reports

news.abstract: Closing arguments begin in Detroit in trial of four Arabs arrested after Sept 11, 2001 attacks; prosecutors say four plotted terrorism; defense tries to cast doubt on government's case and its crucial witness Youssef Hmimssa, onetime associate of defendants; they are charged with document fraud, conspiracy and material support of terrorism; they are Farouk ali-Haimoud of Algeria and Abdel-Ilah Elmardoudi, Ahmed Hannan and Karim Koubriti of Morocco (M)
news.title: Final Arguments Start in Trial Of 4 Arabs in Terrorism Case

news.abstract: Dept of Defense releases latest list of confirmed deaths of Americans in Iraq (S)
news.title: Names of the Dead

news.abstract: American marines guarding the U.S. Embassy in Kabul shot and killed at least three Afghan soldiers from the Intelligence Service today and wounded two more.
news.title: U.S. Forces in Kabul Shoot Afghan Soldiers by Mistake

news.abstract: US intercepts communications strongly suggesting that small cell of Al Qaeda leaders in Iran directed recent terrorist attacks in Saudi Arabia, and US lodges strong protest with Iran; US is said to have hard intelligence that at least dozen Qaeda figures are in Iran, including Saif al-Adel and Osama bin Laden's son, Saad bin Laden; Sec Donald Rumsfeld comments; photos (M)
news.title: U.S. Suggests a Qaeda Cell in Iran Directed Saudi Bombings

news.abstract: US intelligence agencies conclude that two mysterious trailers found in Iraq were mobile units to produce germs for weapons, but have not found biological agents or evidence of such use; trailers were thoroughly decontaminated with unidentified caustic agent but experts can come up with no other plausible explanation; US reportedly will invite international experts to examine mobile units; photos; diagram; Iraqi scientists claim 2,000-liter vessel in each unit was used to mix chemicals to produce hydrogen gas, but evidence suggests vessels, made in 2002 and 2003, are fermenters used to multiply seed germs into deadly swarms (M)
news.title: U.S. Analysts Link Iraq Labs To Germ Arms

news.abstract: World Health Organization begins program to restore basic health services in Iraq, at estimated cost of up to $180 million; Dr David Nabarro explans plans (S)
news.title: U.N. Begins Effort in Iraq To Mend Health Services

news.abstract: ARGENTINA: DEPARTING LEADER PARDONS PLOTTERS. VENEZUELA: PAGEANT REPRIEVE.
news.title: World Briefing: Americas

news.abstract: Cemetery in Najaf, Iraq, expanded to eight times its previous size in one decade to accommodate casualties of war and repression during Saddam Hussein's rule; people of Najaf are only now able to recount events of those years to outsiders, about bloodshed they witnessed and bullet-torn bodies they helped bury in unmarked graves; one keeper of graveyard describes 'days of chaos' in 1991, when Shiite Muslims launched rebellion against Hussein and Iraqi soldiers pursued them into cemetery, taking 15 days to find them and shoot them to death; photos; map (M)
news.title: Tales of Iraqis' Silent Suffering Now Find Voices

news.abstract: The military is deploying one of its most highly regarded armored divisions in Baghdad in an effort to bring greater order.
news.title: U.S. Moving to Clamp Down on Crime in Baghdad

news.abstract: American marines guarding United States Embassy in Kabul shoot and kill at least three Afghan soldiers from Intelligence Service and wound two others, in what American officials call regrettable incident; Afghan soldiers and officers say more men were wounded as they rushed to help first colleagues who were hit; say their battalion commander was seriously wounded; there are no American casualties; shootings occur after American marines in Kabul are placed on high alert amid warnings of imminent terrorist attacks around world; photo (M)
news.title: Marines at U.S. Embassy Kill 3 Afghan Soldiers in Incident Called Error

news.abstract: Voters in Basque town of Tolosa prepare to vote for candidates of outlawed Batasuna party, which has been linked by Spanish government and United States to violent separatist group ETA; hope is that ballots, although void, will be counted unofficially and reveal strength of popular support for Batasuna; photos; map (M)
news.title: Tolosa Journal; Politics in a Perilous Place: The Basque Country

news.abstract: BRITAIN: CHILD KILLER GRANTED LIFELONG ANONYMITY. IRELAND: PARTY DEFENDS ITSELF.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: More than 1,600 were killed in the earthquake that struck Algeria, "and the victim figures are expected to rise," Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia said at a news conference today.
news.title: Algerians Begin Burying Dead From Quake; Death Toll Rises

news.abstract: Alejandro DeTomaso, whose company DeTomaso Automobili produced sports car that combined Italian flair with American horsepower, dies at age 74; photos (M)
news.title: Alejandro DeTomaso, 74, Maker of Sports Cars, Dies

news.abstract: Pentagon is having trouble recruiting civilian lawyers to represent terrorist suspects in its military tribunals at United States naval base in Guantanamo Bay, Cuba; Pres Bush has not singled out any prisoner from Afghanistan for tribunal yet, but Pentagon has been preparing for one; suspects will be provided military defense lawyers but can also ask for civilian lawyers; Col Will A Gunn, named as acting chief defense counsel, says he has had some inquiries from military lawyers but none from civilian lawyers (M)
news.title: U.S. Seeking Guantánamo Defense Staff

news.abstract: British military hands over major Iraqi port of Umm Qasr to local administrators in symbolic transfer of power intended to show that Iraqis are beginning to take control of major elements of their country; British military prepares to scale back its personnel at port, which is chief gateway for aid agencies bringing supplies into country; new Iraqi Port Authority for Umm Qasr will remain under oversight of American and British administrators now running country (M)
news.title: British Give Port Control To the Iraqis

news.abstract: China's Communist Party seeks to claim credit for defusing SARS crisis caused partly by official denial and deceit; some scholars and media commentators, disagree, saying SARS did more to expose weaknesses of China's political culture than its strengths; frank debate about government's handling of SARS comes as anxiety about disease has begun to ease (M)
news.title: Some Chinese Say Government's Response to Epidemic Has Been Too Heavy-Handed

news.abstract: CHINA: Missile Penalties Criticized; PAKISTAN: Billboards Torn Down; INDIA: Heat Wave Kills Scores;.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: End to United Nations trade sanctions will officially end 13 years of international isolation for Iraq; experts say move will bring little immediate relief to Iraq's battered economy; say biggest restraint on trade and investment has been fear about current lawlessness and instability, not sanctions (M)
news.title: Lifting of Iraq Sanctions Ends 13 Years of Isolation, but Immediate Relief Isn't Expected

news.abstract: Afghani Min Ashraf Ghani sets aggressive new drive to overhaul customs and finance departments countrywide and curb corruption in bid to draw in revenue for central treasury; outlines plan after 12 most powerful regional leaders agree to hand over their customs revenue and income from state enterprises in their areas; says he will visit Herat, where Gen Ismail Khan draws in estimated $400 million a year in customs; plan also puts spotlight on lucrative enterprises controlled by Gen Abdul Rashid Dostum in north (M)
news.title: Kabul Announces Push to Gain Revenue and Combat Corruption

news.abstract: Attacks by Islamic activists are wiping out liquor stores in Iraq, particularly in Basra and other southern cities where Shiite Muslims are in majority; clerics and Islamic political parties blame zealots beyond their control (M)
news.title: Iraq's Liquor Trade Becomes A Casualty of Postwar Chaos

news.abstract: Seven men and one woman go on trial in Netherlands for alleged involvement in Chinese smuggling operation; are believed to have been responsible for deaths of 58 Chinese immigrants found in truck in Dover (England) three years ago (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: The Netherlands: Smuggling Trial Begins

news.abstract: Rumors of evildoers dressed in black are latest wave of panic sweeping through largely Muslim provinces of southern Thailand, where central government in overwhelmingly Buddhist nation has failed to reduce widespread poverty and disaffection; mob of rural villagers attack and kill two plainclothes policemen after rumor spreads that they were black ninjas (M)
news.title: Tales of Black Ninjas Are Spreading Fear in Rural Thailand

news.abstract: Nestor Kirchner, who takes office as president of Argentina on May 25, faces economic and political crisis that has consumed five presidents in 18 months; demands for new direction are more insistent than ever; economy has begun to bounce back after hitting bottom, leaving a fifth of work force unemployed and thousands of businesses bankrupt; photos (M)
news.title: Argentina Looks to a New Leader

news.abstract: Art exhibit is held in damaged government building in Basra, Iraq, and artists show their first works created free from controls of Saddam Hussein; photo (M)
news.title: Raw Iraqi Art Breaks Free of Chokehold

news.abstract: Leading figures in Kirkuk, Iraq, gather to elect City Council; American authorities detain five delegates who were to take part in voting after receiving intelligence reports that men had been high-ranking members of Saddam Hussein's Baath Party; American authorities have begun organizing elections in northern Iraq--first in Mosul and now Kirkuk; Americans say elections, which are not popular ballots but are carried out by assembly of local leaders choosing interim administrations, are first step toward Iraqis governing themselves (M)
news.title: U.S. Detains 5 Suspected Baath Loyalists at Kirkuk Elections

news.abstract: Early release from prison of mobster convicted of murder touches off furious debate in Italy about policies that reward even worst killers if they provide information that helps put other members of Mafia behind bars; Enzo Brusca, whose prison sentence was commuted to house arrest, is one of more than 1,100 criminal informers, called pentiti, who are collaborating with Italian law enforcement officials, and they have become favorite weapons Italian police use against criminal organizations (M)
news.title: Mobster's Release Brings Criticism of Italian Policy on Informers

news.abstract: Afghan authorities arrest five men who allegedly planned to bomb busy area in Kandahar; Mullah Janan, Taliban member with close ties to Al Qaeda, is among those arrested (M)
news.title: Five Are Arrested in Reported Plan to Set Off Bomb in Kandahar

news.abstract: Interview with Sener Levent,l
news.title: Turkish Cypriot Publisher Goes to Press, and Court, Almost Daily

news.abstract: Nearly 200 cows belonging to the same Alberta herd as the cow infected with mad cow disease were found to be free of the disease, according to test results made public over the weekend.
news.title: No Mad Cow Disease in Herd That Had Infected Animal

news.abstract: Spanish Prime Min Jose Maria Aznar's governing party loses some ground in municipal and regional elections; manages to hold power in Madrid and many other cities; opposition Socialists win largest number of votes nationwide for first time in decade, taking control of Madrid's regional government; Aznar's wife, Ana Botella, is elected to Madrid town council (M)
news.title: Aznar's Party Keeps Hold on Madrid in Vote

news.abstract: Bush administration officials say US is pressing Iran to cooperate with investigation into recent bombings in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, and to hand over operatives of Al Qaeda believed to have been working in Iranian territory; administration has held series of secret meetings with Iranian officials, who continue to deny any involvement with Al Qaeda; UN Amb Javad Zarif says Tehran is cooperating in attempts to control Al Qaeda and has arrested members of network but would not respond to 'language of pressure'; dispute in intelligence community about Iran-Al Qaeda connection discussed; some in administration believe terrorists could be in Iran but not necessarily with sanction of government; there is also concern that Iran is supporting Shiite groups in Iraq seeking to destabilize American occupation; possible acceleration by Iran of its nuclear weapons program discussed; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Demands That Iran Turn Over Qaeda Agents And Join Saudi Inquiry

news.abstract: Unidentified gunmen fired machine guns and rocket-propelled grenades today at a column of military vehicles, killing two American soldiers.
news.title: Gunmen Kill 2 U.S. Soldiers in a Firefight in Central Iraq

news.abstract: Latest massacre in Congo reveals, with graphic and embarrassing detail, impotence of international reaction to horrors that have befallen that country; death toll in town of Bunia stands at 350 as militias belonging to rival Hema and Lendu tribes battle for control; machete's ghastly wreckage is evident on men, women and children inside what passes for hospital; there is no telling when next round of carnage will unfold, or whether United Nations Security Council will send troops to bring order; Secretary Gen Kofi Annan has appealed to member countries to send soldiers for multinational force; peacekeepers sent to Bunia were overrun and two of them were also massacred; American officials say only long-lasting solution for peace in Congo is to persuade outsiders, namely Uganda and Rwanda, to stop arming proxy fighters and to support peace deal recently negotiated between warring factions; photos; map (M)
news.title: Congo War Toll Soars as U.N. Pleads for Aid

news.abstract: World Health Orgn reports that blood tests of people who work with exotic animals in markets in southern China show that significant proportion apparently have been infected with SARS virus, suggesting that some people may become infected without becoming ill; findings are from two separate studies of workers in markets in Guangdong Province; they strengthen SARS link between animals and humans (M)
news.title: Tests in China Suggest Some With SARS Don't Become Ill

news.abstract: Amphibious assault ship Nassau sails into North Carolina waters after nine months at sea and begins to disembark 1,100 marines returning to Camp Lejeune, part of first contingent home from war in Iraq; arrival is delayed by searches for two missing sailors; one fell into ocean chasing football on deck and second did not show up for roll call (M)
news.title: A Return to North Carolina, Marred by Loss of 2 Sailors

news.abstract: Some analysts contend local Italian elections reflect mixed feelings about Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi's government as early results predict his party losing Province of Rome to center-left opposition; Berlusconi has been embroiled in corruption trial (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Italy: Berlusconi Party Lagging In Rome Race

news.abstract: The Saudi police made the arrests, which included the accused mastermind, in a series of raids in and around Medina.
news.title: Saudis Arrest at Least 8 Men Believed Tied to Bombings

news.abstract: China's battle against SARS virus takes on old unsanitary habit of spitting in street, with authorities and volunteers handing out little plastic spit bags in parks and malls; photos; Communist Party Central Committee gives imprimatur to campaign, issuing Directive on Launching Activities to Transform Vile Habits (M)
news.title: SARS Forces Beijing to Fight An Old but Unsanitary Habit

news.abstract: Canadian government introduces legislation to decriminalize possession of small amounts of marijuana but set stricter penalties for trafficking in drug (S)
news.title: Canada Introduces Measure Adjusting Penalties for Marijuana

news.abstract: Sec Donald H Rumsfeld, responding to questions after speech to Council on Foreign Relations, New York City, suggests publicly for first time that Iraq might have destroyed chemical and biological weapons before war; again holds it is just matter of time before military teams uncover illicit arms Pres Bush cited as major reason for war; seeks to counter critics who have accused administration of bungling post-war campaign in Iraq; appeals for patience for reconstruction effort that will be difficult and bumpy at times; photo (M)
news.title: Rumsfeld Echoes Notion That Iraq Destroyed Arms

news.abstract: Saudi Arabia, in first sign that it has already wearied of public debate that followed May 12 suicide bombings, orders removal of Jamal A Kashoggi as editor in chief of Al Watan, newspaper that has spoken out against Islamic militancy; move dismays those who believe religious institutions propagate extremist ideas; members of religious establishment feel vindicated; paper, partly owned by prominent descendants of late King Faisal, has been leading voice calling for openness and reform in kingdom; opened unprecedented petition on its Web site asking rulers to curb extremist religious discourse (M)
news.title: A Saudi Editor Who Offended Clerics Is Ousted From His Post

news.abstract: Japanese survivors of World War II atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki fear country is becoming increasingly blase about remembering bombings; Hiroshima's entire image and economy are linked to horrendous final days of war; city officials say visits by Japanese travelers are down, and commissions are formed to reverse trend; one survivor, who regularly tells her story to classrooms full of students, says each year students' stares grow blanker and their questions grow more stilted; photos; map (M)
news.title: Hiroshima Journal; Teaching Youth to Start Worrying About the Bomb

news.abstract: Pres Bush's scheduled stop in Poland is to thank country for supporting American policy in Iraq when bigger countries of NATO opposed it; visit signals that in Washington's eyes, Poland has become important ally, even special friend; it is strange and even improbable role for country whose tragic and tormented history has kept it in shadows for centuries; alongside any awkwardness Poland may feel at being caught between Europe and US goes unaccustomed security and pride at standing on same battlefields as Americans, particularly in Iraq, where Poland is to send 1,500 soldiers to keep peace and will command one of four occupation zones; photo (M)
news.title: Bush Visit Will Lift Poland to Status of Special Friend

news.abstract: Saudi Interior Min Prince Nayef announces capture of eight suspected militants wanted in connection with bombing attacks on residential compounds in Riyadh; says police raids around holy city of Medina led to total of 11 arrests, including foreign-born wives of three of suspects; American Amb Robert W Jordan says United States believes chances are high that another attack will take place despite arrests; Prince Nayef says those arrested include three radical clerics known for their support of militant causes; Saudi and American officials say Al Qaeda remains prime suspect (M)
news.title: Saudis Arrest 8 in Deadly Riyadh Bombing

news.abstract: Health authorities in Canada quarantine as many as 2,000 students, teachers and staff members of large parochial school on outskirts of Toronto that was closed after 11th-grade student attended classes for two days last week while showing symptoms of SARS; new quarantine underscores potential seriousness of new outbreak of SARS, only two weeks after local and international authorities declared it was no longer spreading in Toronto; second potential new case of SARS is being investigated in small Ontario community of Parry Sound after resident there develops SARS-type symptoms following visit to affected hospital in Tornoto; 70 residents of Parry Sound are in quarantine; possibility that disease has affected fifth hospital in metropolitan Toronto area is also under investigation after new wave of illness is reported; two elderly SARS patients die, bringing total to 29 deaths in Toronto area in three months; photo (M)
news.title: Quarantine Hits Toronto School In SARS Fight

news.abstract: Kurds in Kirkuk, city long dominated by Arabs from Baath Party of Saddam Hussein, celebrate election of Abdul Rahman Mustafa as mayor; vote for mayor follows city council elections that give Kurds largest block of votes on 30-seat council; American-organized elections in Kirkuk are significant because city is center of Iraq's vast northern oil resources, and because it has been focal point of ethnic tension between Arabs and Kurds; Arab delegates are subdued even though Arab, Ismail Ahmed Rajab, is elected deputy mayor; photos (M)
news.title: Kurds Celebrate Election of Mayor in Kirkuk

news.abstract: Pres Roh Moo Hyun of South Korea is fighting for his political life barely three months into his five-year term; faces daunting list of woes, including corruption investigations involving some longtime associates and his older brother; calls news conference to fend off accusations of corruption, but news media coverage is strongly skeptical, saying there are still many unanswered questions; his recent visit to Washington, during which he met with Pres Bush and strongly reaffirmed country's attachment to its 50-year alliance with US, was supposed to be victory for him; it turned into political debacle at home, after leftist student groups and others accused him of caving in to Washington after campaigning on theme of greater independence; photo (M)
news.title: Criticism Takes Toll on South Korean Leader

news.abstract: China has nearly tamed the SARS epidemic, with new cases dwindling and no evidence of the wildfire spread in the hinterlands that experts had feared.
news.title: Number of SARS Cases Falls Sharply in China

news.abstract: British government says it will grant refugee status to Abas Amini, Iranian poet and political dissident who sewed up his lips, eyelids and ears to protest what he says are injustices in way Britain treats asylum seekers; Amini, who will be allowed to remain in Britain, vows to leave stitches intact and to continue his hunger strike on behalf of other asylum seekers (S)
news.title: Britain to Grant Iranian Dissident Refugee Status

news.abstract: Sergei Larin, lone Russian climber, reaches summit of Mount Everest on 50th anniversary of first ascent by Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay; gale winds at base camp prevent several American expeditions from trying to reach summit to mark anniversary; they may not have another chance, because climbing season closes on June 1; Hillary, who favors restricting number of climbers on mountain, has inveighed against softening of Everest ethic; says many would-be climbers use base camp as place to drink; several veteran climbers also lament 'commercialism' and 'circus' atmosphere of Everest; photo; map (M)
news.title: 50 Years Later, a Lone Man Stands at Top of the World

news.abstract: Italian Parliament is expected to pass bill submitted by supporters of Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi that protects those serving in top five political posts from facing trial while in office; opposition leaders claim bill is written to allow Berlusconi, currently involved in corruption trial, to evade prosecution (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Italy: Berlusconi Immunity Plan

news.abstract: Pakistani officials report arrest of Qari Abdul Hayee, Islamic militant believed to have helped plan and carry out kidnapping and murder of American journalist Daniel Pearl; Hayee is member of banned sectarian group Lashkar-e-Jhangvi and among most wanted militants in Pakistan (S)
news.title: ARREST IN PEARL CASE

news.abstract: World Psychiatric Assn calls on China to fulfill its promise to let international experts examine charges that psychiatry has been misused; China has agreed to cooperate, but ground rules for visit have not been determined; China's psychatric practices have been criticized in recent years since hundreds of members of Falun Gong movement were declared delusional and were forcibly hospitalized (M)
news.title: Psychiatrists Rebuke China For Blocking Inspection Visit

news.abstract: British Prime Min Tony Blair angrily denies charges that in making case for war in Iraq, his government exaggerated intelligence reports showing that Saddam Hussein possessed weapons of mass destruction; refutes BBC, which said report asserting that Hussein had capacity to deploy chemical and biological weapons within 45 minutes had been made 'sexier' on Blair's orders and against judgment of intelligence service (M)
news.title: Blair Denies Britain Distorted Reports on Iraqi Weapons

news.abstract: Pres Bush arrives in Europe, where there is both hope that trans-Atlantic rift can be healed and skepticism about America's desire to rebuild Europe-American partnership; Bush's words will be dissected to see if administration intends to foster European unity or divide it into 'old' and 'new' Europe; some European newspapers are treating failure to find weapons of mass destruction in Iraq as blow to Bush's credibility that will harm prospects for future cooperation between Europe and US (M)
news.title: Europe Awaits, With Bated Breath

news.abstract: MONACO:—  Take a fabulous and unique diamond. Add a royal family, a black-tie ball, fashion models and movie stars, Ferraris, Jaguars and spacious yachts. Throw in an exclusive three-night party with star disk jockeys, dancers and circus acts.
news.title: In Monaco, glamour in the fast lane

news.abstract: Myanmar's military government takes Daw Aung San Suu Kyi and 19 of top members of her pro-democracy party into what it calls 'protective custody' after clash involving her supporters near town of Dipeyin that left 4 people dead and 50 injured; blames Aung San Suu Kyi for causing violence; also closes her party's headquarters in Yangon (M)
news.title: Burmese Opposition Leader Taken Into Custody After Clashes

news.abstract: BERLIN, June 1  Chancellor Gerhard Schröder's plan to enact economic reform by reducing Germany's vast network of social protections was approved today by 90 percent of the delegates at a politically crucial meeting of his Social Democratic Party.
news.title: German Chancellor's Economic Reform Plan Endorsed

news.abstract: Most merchants have locked up and retreated in anticipation of possible violence surrounding the Group of 8 summit meeting that is to open in Évian on Sunday.
news.title: With Protesters on the Move, Geneva Shops Board Up

news.abstract: Deputy Defense Secretary Paul D. Wolfowitz indicated he hoped to convince South Korean that American troops should withdraw to south of Seoul.
news.title: U.S. Pushing Realignment of Troops in South Korea

news.abstract: Nepal allows China to force 18 Tibetan refugees back to Tibet; has long winked at efforts by its ethnic neighbors in Tibet to separate from China, but is now bending more and more to pressure from Beijing, which is increasingly important aid and trade partner (M)
news.title: Over Protests, Nepal Lets Chinese Force Refugees Back to Tibet

news.abstract: Pres Bush arrives in France for meeting of Group of 8, encountering European leaders who opposed war in Iraq and trying to increase pressure on Iran and North Korea to give up their nuclear weapons programs; offers pro forma handshakes to Pres Jacques Chirac of France and Chancellor Gerhard Schroder of Germany; Bush believes they undercut his effort against Saddam Hussein, but he shows no desire to rehash their differences; instead he sticks to main issue on his agenda--nonproliferation; his aides work behind scenes to sign countries up for new White House initiative to create international legal basis for seizing missiles, chemical and biological agents and nuclear components on high seas or in air; proposal is intended to give countries broader authority to quarantine North Korea, and perhaps Iran as well; it is unclear how many of traditionally American allies at meeting would agree; concerns about American empire can be heard within meeting halls and in huge protests moving through streets of Geneva and villages in both Switzerland and France; Bush will use economic forum to argue, as he already has, that world must unify behind American vision of confronting tyrants and unconventional weapons; photo; map (L)
news.title: BUSH PRESSES CASE ON IRAN AND KOREA AT ECONOMIC TALKS

news.abstract: Yasir Arafat's trappings of power are almost all gone, but Palestinian officials and analysts are certain he will be most influential Palestinian figure in renewed peace negotiations with Israel, even if he is working behind scenes; although Arafat does retain considerable influence, dynamics of Middle East conflict have been changing in month since Mahmoud Abbas assumed office as prime minister; Abbas's cabinet meets weekly without Arafat, and Abbas says he hopes to reach cease-fire deal with Islamic militant group Hamas and perhaps other radical Palestinian organizations, something Arafat was never able to deliver; Arafat is not invited to attend regional summit meeting in Jordan, when Pres Bush will meet with Abbas and Israeli Prime Min Ariel Sharon; but he remains head of Palestinian Authority, leader of Palestine Liberation Orgn and of Fatah movement; photo (M)
news.title: Spotlight Leaves Arafat, but He's Still in the Show

news.abstract: Three young legal scholars in China send petition to national legislature, challenging system by which big-city police officers detain, fine and expel rural migrants at will, with no judicial oversight; their modest proposal is to enforce personal rights that are guaranteed in Constitution; petition has drawn unusual attention and praise in news media; it was submitted following unexplained beating death of man detained in Guangzhou, but drafters have larger goals in mind; they hope to advance cause of constitutional rights in general; in often paradoxical legal environment of China today, proposals that are tied to widely acknowledged social problems, that do not challenge one-party rule and that are couched in narrow terms of legal reform, can be debated more openly than ever before; photos (M)
news.title: Petitioners Urge China to Enforce Legal Rights

news.abstract: When President Bush opens a new Middle East peace quest on Tuesday in Egypt, he will confront a region still trying to absorb America's occupation of Iraq.
news.title: Arab Leaders Skeptical, but Hope for Results

news.abstract: Nepal's Maoist guerrillas come to Katmandu under cease-fire that has virtually stopped political violence since it took effect four months ago; civil war that had festered out of sight of Katmandu exploded tenfold last year, claiming 4,655 lives and prompting King Gyanendra to fire his prime minister and make secret feelers to Maoists; Krishna Bahadur Mahara, Maoist leader, says there is now strategic equilibrium of military power; Maoists say they control 80 percent of countryside, while king oversees 50 percent increase in Royal Nepal Army, with new military aid arriving from India, Britain and United States; major question is whether Maoists are serious about talking peace or merely using time to gain military strength for new phase of war; photo (M)
news.title: Nepal's Maoist Guerrillas Let the Revolution Rest, for Now

news.abstract: In their brief encounters in the French Alpine town of Évian-les-Bains over the past two days, George W. Bush and Jacques Chirac acted like grown-ups.    There were no testy exchanges, no biting one-liners, no disparaging comments by unidentified aides. On the contrary, when the American and French presidents met for the first time since their bitter split over the American-led war on Iraq, they were polite in public and, by all accounts, even nice to each other in private.
news.title: U.S.-French Détente: Leaders Lower Voices

news.abstract: The provincial assembly here, dominated by an alliance of religious parties, voted unanimously today to introduce Islamic law to the North-West Frontier Province, fulfilling an election promise that has worried the national government and its American allies.    The six-party religious alliance, the Muttahida Majlis-e-Amal, which holds a majority in the assembly, is opposed to the American presence in Afghanistan and is sympathetic to Taliban elements that are continuing to fight United States forces. It has campaigned to introduce Islamic law, or Shariah, to ensure better justice for the population, but critics accuse it of dragging the province back into the Taliban era.
news.title: Pakistani Legislators Approve Islamic Law for Province

news.abstract: INDIA: Dangerous Heat; PHILIPPINES: Pact With U.S. On Tribunals; SINGAPORE: Conjoined Adults To Be Separated;.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: With questions persisting about the failure to find unconventional weapons in Iraq, Senator John W. Warner, Republican of Virginia and chairman of the Armed Services Committee, said today that his panel would conduct hearings this month on the issue.    The House Intelligence Committee has already requested that the C.I.A. investigate whether prewar assessments of Iraq's weapons capacity were flawed.
news.title: Senate Panel Inquiry on Iraq Weapons

news.abstract: President Bush arrived in the Mideast tonight for the first time in his presidency, preparing to face Arab leaders skeptical of American intentions in Iraq and to mediate between the Israelis and the Palestinians, a role he has long avoided.    When Air Force One landed here tonight on the southern tip of the Sinai Peninsula, Mr. Bush was greeted with a hug by the Egyptian president, Hosni Mubarak. But the warm welcome masked undercurrents of wariness.
news.title: Bush, in Egypt, Finds Warmth And Wariness

news.abstract: Israeli and Palestinian prime ministers will appear together publicly for first time in Aqaba, Jordan, in company of Pres Bush; White House operatives get Jordanians to build bridge over pool at king's new palace to enable leaders to walk together toward massed cameras for literal image and metaphor; photo; Mahmoud Abbas is expected to make explicit call for end of armed intifada; Ariel Sharon to endorse vision of two states living in peace (M)
news.title: Hoping a Troubled Bridge Over Water Will Be a Pathway to Mideast Peace

news.abstract: The head of the U.S.-led administration in Iraq met Tuesday with the new United Nations representative to Iraq, and they vowed to work together "to create a democratic, independent and peaceful Iraq."
news.title: Ex-head of army warns of long stay and says Pentagon balks at admitting it : U.S. leader in Iraq sees role for the UN

news.abstract: Shores of broad lake that spreads across Africa's Rift Valley in Kenya, where British colonials once disported on emerald lawns and verandas, are now setting for booming industry in growing out-of-season vegetables and cut flowers that are shipped to distant markets in Europe; photo; enormous tracts of farmland have drawn thousands of workers, mostly women from distant villages who earn barely enough to survive; proponents of globalization say self-interest of business will lead to better wages and environment for workers (M)
news.title: Beside Blossoming Fields, Where Poverty Grows

news.abstract: Egyptian court upholds one-year sentence for libel against brothers Mustafa Bakri, editor in chief of weekly newspaper Al Osboa, and Mahmoud Bakri who works at paper; libel charges stem from articles published 3 years ago about personal life of opposition Social Justice Party leader Muhammad Abdel-Aal, who is currently serving 10-year sentence for accepting bribes (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Egypt: Journalists Jailed For Libel

news.abstract: Prime Minister Tony Blair said today a parliamentary committee would investigate the accusations and make public its findings.
news.title: Blair Denies Britain Distorted Intelligence Reports on Iraq

news.abstract: Authorities conduct raids in Altar, Mexico, shutting down dozens of rundown hostels that serve illegal migrants waiting to cross border into United States; raids are latest step in crackdown by Pres Vicente Fox against criminal groups, characterized as international mafias, that have made immigrant smuggling billion dollars a year industry; law enforcement officials estimate that in this region of border alone, 1,500 people attempt to cross desert each day, and scores die each year, most from exposure; map; photo (M)
news.title: In Border Town, Migrant Crackdown Rankles

news.abstract: VIETNAM: Crime Boss Convicted; NEPAL: New Prime Minister Appointed; TAIWAN: Crash Analysis Issued;.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: News analsysis: commitments secured by Pres Bush from Israeli Prime Min Ariel Sharon and Palestinian Prime Min Mahmoud Abbas to road map for peace will require both sides to face up to their internal conflicts; Sharon's promise to begin confronting settler movement he nurtured for decades means plunging nation into long-postponed national debate over what Israel wants from its occupation of West Bank and Gaza; Abbas's promise to end armed Palestinian uprising means stopping terrorists who have highacked Palestinian national dream and shifting internal Palestinian conversation away from empathy for suicide bombers; both leaders will face severe challenges, which are already beginning, as thousands of settlers stage angry protest and Hamas leaders reject Abbas's suggestion that they surrender their arms; photos (M)
news.title: Looking Beyond Words

news.abstract: European Union governments agree to send joint peacekeeping force to Congo to help contain ethnic violence; 1,400-member force, which was authorized by United Nations, marks first time European Union will carry out military operation without help from North Atlantic Treaty Organization and first European Union military operation outside of Europe (M)
news.title: European Peacekeepers to Go To Congo on Non-NATO Mission

news.abstract: The attack in Falluja, which also injured five U.S. troops, was the eighth death of an American soldier in the last 10 days.
news.title: Another G.I. Dies in Violence-Prone Iraqi Town

news.abstract: United States and South Korea agree to reposition American troops far away from demilitarized zone that separates North and South Korea to make them less vulnerable to attack by North; 14,000 American troops are considered strategic 'tripwire' on Korean peninsula, ensuring that American troops would be drawn into any war started by North; redeployment, which will occur over period of years, is negotiated at time of high tensions beetween US and North Korea over North's suspected development of nuclear weapons; it comes after months of strained relations between US and South Korea, where Pres Roh Moo Hyun won election in December amid large-scale protest movement against American military presence in country; most of 37,000 American troops in South Korea are based in northern tier of country, in and around Seoul; some South Korean officials feared that repositioning of troops would leave US free to make pre-emptive attack against North Korea's nuclear sites without fear of retaliation against American soldiers; their fears are eased when US pledges that some American troops will remain presence in northern part of country, near demilitarized zone; photo (M)
news.title: G.I.'s Will Gradually Leave Korea DMZ to Cut War Risk

news.abstract: Grand Ayatollah Ali al-Sestani, one of most senior Shiite clerics in Iraq and world, steps into political fray; meets with Kurdish leader Massoud Barzani, who has enjoyed close ties to Washington, and calls for elections to national assembly for Iraqis to produce new constitution; Sestani is reportedly critical of postwar conditions in Iraq; his visit with Barzani underscores fact that dissatisfaction with current state of planning in Washington and London for postwar government extends beyond former Iraqi opposition leaders to other major figures (M)
news.title: Leading Iraqi Shiite Cleric Emerges to Meet U.S. Ally

news.abstract: Hidden assailants in Falluja, Iraq, launch another attack on American soldiers, killing one American and wounding five; after series of almost weekly attacks on American forces, Falluja is emerging as center of anti-American resistance in Iraq; US commanders adopt get-tough approach in city; 4,000 soldiers will replace 1,200-member squadron; what occurs in Falluja in next several weeks could set precedent; American military might could either crush dissent in area--or fuel it; photo of one resident who says he was roughly searched by soldiers; map (M)
news.title: Another Attack in Central Iraq Kills Another U.S. Soldier

news.abstract: Pope John Paul II's visit to Croatia marks 100th time he has left Vatican City for foreign visit, reminder of extent to which travel has defined his papacy and he has used travel to redefine papacy itself; since beginning of his papacy in 1978, he has traveled to more than 125 countries, many of them more than once; his frequent trips, coupled with news coverage it generates, has given him enhanced stature on international stage; Vatican officials say he considers travel integral part of his mission; photo of Pope with Croation Pres Stjepan Mesic (M)
news.title: Vatican Traveler in Croatia, Reaching 100, Trips, That Is

news.abstract: GEORGIA: U.N. Observers Kidnapped; EUROPEAN UNION PENALIZES CUBA;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: A United Nations envoy arrived today in Myanmar and said he would press for the release of the pro-democracy leader Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, who is in detention after a violent clash that the United States said might have been instigated by the government.    Arriving on a previously scheduled visit, the envoy, Razali Ismail, said he hoped to be allowed to see Mrs. Aung San Suu Kyi as well as top government officials. She has been held at a secret location since the incident on Friday in which the government said 4 people were killed and 50 injured.
news.title: U.N. Envoy Will Try to Visit Burmese Dissident Held by Junta

news.abstract: The imam at one of Baghdad's largest mosques urged more than a thousand listeners today to wage a jihad, or religious war, against American occupying forces in Iraq.    Speaking at Friday Prayers, Imam Mouaid al-Ubaidi denounced the Americans as invaders and aggressors and implicitly praised recent guerrilla attacks against United States soldiers as self-defense by people who are being ''strangled.''
news.title: As Iraqis' Disaffection Grows, U.S. Offers Them a Greater Political Role

news.abstract: Ismail Abu Shanab and other leaders of militant Islamic group Hamas break off talks with Palestinian Prime Min Mahmoud Abbas on cease-fire with Israel; cite his speech at meeting with Israel demanding end to armed uprising and expressing compassion for Jewish suffering, interviews; Abbas supporters say Hamas seeks to exploit unpopular speech, drafted by Bush administration, to oust help oust him; photo (M)
news.title: HAMAS BREAKS OFF TALKS ON STOPPING ATTACKS ON ISRAEL

news.abstract: American and British intelligence analysts with direct access to evidence dispute claims that trailers found in Iraq in Apr and May were part of biological warfare program, interviews; say they were more likely intended for other purposes; charge evaluation process was damaged by rush to judgment; Central Intelligence Agency reaffirms stand (M)
news.title: Some Analysts Of Iraq Trailers Reject Germ Use

news.abstract: PARIS:—  Ted Matheny, a lawyer based in Paris, travels about one week a month for business, racking up mobile phone charges of about €400 a month.
news.title: New increases expected as vacations begins : Still paying a high price for a 'roaming' cell phone

news.abstract: US tanks rumble through Falluja, Iraq, in display for force intended to reassert control of unruly city; soldiers are trying to root out enemy fighters who have killed three Americans and wounded more than dozen before fading back into narrow streets; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Troops Put On a Show of Military Force in a Center of Hard-Core Resistance

news.abstract: Croatians of Vukovar, where Serbs killed 5,000 people in siege nearly twelve years ago, find it difficult to heed Pope John Paul II's call for forgiveness; photo of pope in Osijek; map (M)
news.title: Forgive, Pope Says, But Croats Find It Hard

news.abstract: Leading Shiite Muslim party, Islamic Revolution in Iraq, says it will not join governing council if members are appointed by US administrator Paul Bremer; US soldier is killed and four others wounded when gunmen open fire near Tikrit; Gen Muhammad Habib al-Mashadani, former deputy commander of national police, is arrested on charges of trying to re-create Baath Party cell within reconstituted police force (M)
news.title: Shiite Muslim Party Warns It May Boycott Iraq Council

news.abstract: Lendu and Hema gunmen battle for control of Congo town of Bunia; photo (S)
news.title: Ethnic Militias in Congo Battle for Control of a Town

news.abstract: Young Indians in Goa, colonized by Portugal five centuries ago, are taking advantage of Portuguese law granting them citizenship to obtain passports that also get them into European Union countries; Portugal gave up colony in 1961 (M)
news.title: Indians Pursue Portuguese Passports as an Entree to Europe

news.abstract: Afghan teenager wounded in suicide car bomb attack on German peacekeepers dies, bringing to five those killed in attack; is lone Afghan casualty, apart from bomber; four German soldiers are killed and 31 wounded; it is worst attack on international peacekeeping force in 18 months it has been deployed in Kabul and surrounding area; photo (M)
news.title: Afghan Youth's Death Raises Kabul Bombing Toll to Five

news.abstract: The chancellor of the exchequer said today that Britons might vote in a referendum next year on joining the euro
news.title: British Finance Official Says Euro Vote Is Possible

news.abstract: The Palestinian prime minister said today that there was no alternative to the new peace plan while Israel began taking down a handful of mostly uninhabited settlements.
news.title: Abbas Answers Critics as Israel Shuts Down a Few Outposts

news.abstract: Pope John Paul II marks his 100th foreign trip with visit to Croatia; visit's muted volume and modest scale, at least by standard of many previous papal journeys, underscore degree to which his infirmities and longevity have begun to lend different shade to his adventures; crowds in Croatian port city of Rijeka respond to him more respectfully than raucously, with softer chants and cheers; overarching atmosphere is more subdued, in line with his diminished energies and less expansive gestures; photo (M)
news.title: For Pope and the Croats, Superstar's Muted Echo

news.abstract: Members of Prime Min Ariel Sharon's Likud Party, attending party convention in Jerusalem, boo and heckle in latest round of criticism he is enduring from traditional right-wing allies in wake of his proposed concessions to Palestinians; they accuse him of surrendering to terror; in Ramallah, Palestinian Prime Min Mahmoud Abbas faces his own barrage of criticism from hard-liners and moderates alike who accuse him of being too conciliatory toward Israel; Sharon is politically strong and Abbas is vulnerable in his new post, but both face mounting internal pressure that threatens latest Middle East peace plan before first steps have been taken to put it into effect; photo (M)
news.title: Sharon and Abbas, Both Under Fire From Hard-Liners

news.abstract: Federal authorities begin draining small pond in municipal park near Frederick, Md, searching for evidence in unsolved anthrax mailings that killed five people and inflicted illness on 17 others in 2001; plastic box that some bioterrorism experts say could have been used to carry anthrax was retrieved from pond last Dec; pond is eight miles from Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases at Fort Detrick, Md; inquiry has become one of largest ever by FBI and postal authorities; they have unearthed thousands of leads, but they have publicly singled out only Dr Steven Hatfill as 'person of interest'; he is germ warfare expert who once worked at Fort Detrick lab and lived in Frederick; has repeatedly said he was not involved in any way with anthrax letters; photo; map (M)
news.title: Hunting Clues, Anthrax Investigators Drain Maryland Pond

news.abstract: Pres Bush says he is 'absolutely convinced' that United States will find proof that Iraq has chemical and biological weapons programs, but he stops short of declaring that Iraq had weapons ready for use rather than just programs to develop them; brushes aside any doubts about primary justification he offered before war for removing Saddam Hussein from power; defends decision to go to war, and again says there are ties between Al Qaeda and Hussein's government; lack of firm evidence that Iraq possessed banned weapons in form that could be used against allied troops or passed to terrorists is becoming foreign policy and political challenge for White House (M)
news.title: Bush Again Vows U.S. Will Find Illicit Weapons

news.abstract: John Sawers, Britain's representative to American administration in Baghdad, says occupying powers intend to run country for foreseeable future, with Iraqis restricted to advisory role; plan he outlines draws sharp criticism from Iraqi political groups that supported American-led invasion and had expected to help govern country, or at least appoint their own consultative council, once Saddam Hussein was deposed; Sawers notes that Iraqis who are beginning to chafe at American and British occupation would also object to transitional government chosen exclusively by former exile groups; says Iraqis who do take part in interim administration must be generally representative of Iraq as a whole; photo (M)
news.title: British Envoy Sees Allies Running Iraq In Near Term

news.abstract: Transportation Security Adm says in report to Congress that stun guns may be permitted on airplanes to protect against hijackers; United Airlines and Mesa Air Group has asked agency to consider allowing their pilots to carry such weapons; agency has not issued final decision (S)
news.title: Stun Guns Closer for Planes

news.abstract: Georgian officials talk with kidnappers of four United Nations military observers monitoring Georgia and Abkhazia cease-fire, but are unable to recover two Germans, Dane and Georgian translator held by captors demanding $3 million in ransom (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Georgia: Talks With Kidnappers

news.abstract: American troops in Afghanistan kill four suspected Taliban members in gun battle on Pakistan border; no US casualties reported (S)
news.title: U.S. Troops in Afghanistan Kill 4 Taliban Suspects Near Border

news.abstract: President Bush condemned the latest deadly bus bombing in Israel today and urged "all the free world" to renounce violence between Israelis and Palestinians.
news.title: Bush Asks Nations to Renounce Mideast Violence

news.abstract: Japan detains two North Korean cargo ships in Japanese ports for safety inspections, day after US encourages allies to pressure North Korea into negotiating end to its nuclear bomb program (S)
news.title: Japan Detains 2 North Korean Ships, Part of Pressure Strategy

news.abstract: Singapore toughens its already strict SARS-prevention regimen (S)
news.title: Singapore Tightens SARS-Control System

news.abstract: BRUSSELS:—  The dangers lurk in the unlikeliest places.
news.title: From farm to fork, risks persist

news.abstract: Large but unwieldy opposition out to end Pres Hugo Chavez's tumultuous rule in Venezuela is adopting new strategy; it is courting country's working class, people in poor neighborhoods who distrust opposition and view it as part of privileged class; Chavez has helped create sharp divide between many of poor and opposition; this has made it difficult for government foes to freely express themselves in hillside slums where he still has strong support, because of threat of violence; opposition has found that rallies backfire in poor areas; their new tact is to go door to door, taking time to explain their position; referendum on Chavez's presidency could take place later this year; photo (M)
news.title: Venezuelan Opposition Courts Working Class

news.abstract: Russian businessman Igor Klimov, recently appointed by government to consolidate air-defense companies, and Sergei Shchitko, official at air-defense company involved in merger, are both shot within few hours of each other in different parts of Moscow; suspected assassinations are part of current wave of killings targeting politicians and businessmen (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Killings Of Defense Executives Linked

news.abstract: Chinese experts survey 101 sites along Great Wall, China's most cherished landmark, and voice alarm at what they find; in western regions, where Wall was largely constructed of mud, erosion has weathered it and sand has buried it in many areas; in eastern portion of Wall, human activities have caused most damage: graffiti on Wall at site near Beijing, and portions of Wall bulldozed in Inner Mongolia to make way for construction; in many locations, Wall has been gussied up with Disney-like creations, in misguided local attempts at 'renovating' ancient Wall to bring tourism into area; Great Wall traverses nine provinces and 100 counties; photo; map (M)
news.title: Vandalism and 'Improvements' Mar Great Wall

news.abstract: On a day of new attacks and counterattacks, there was concern in the Bush administration that the peace plan known as the road map could founder.
news.title: Bush Under Fire in Congress for Criticizing Israel

news.abstract: Egyptian Censorship Director Madkur Thabet bans Matrix Reloaded from Egyptian cinemas because he contends film's violence threatens social peace and content presents controversial view of human creation (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Middle East: Egypt: 'Matrix' Film Banned

news.abstract: Hundreds of Arab families in Iraq's north are being displaced by Kurds, who themselves were driven from area during Iraq's most sweeping ethnic cleansing campaign over 30 years ago; since war, Kurds are returning to their original homes and farmland, and Arabs are migrating back to lands in center, south and west of Iraq; some Arab families have no home or land to go back to; land disputes in north were foreseen by relief organizations long before war (M)
news.title: Kurds and Displaced Arabs Compete for Land

news.abstract: Prince Harry, youngest son of Prince Charles and Diana, late Princess of Wales, completes course of study at Eton and royal family announces his application to Sandhurst Royal Military Academy to begin army career; like his older brother William, he plans to spend year abroad before school; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: A Soldier's Life For Harry

news.abstract: BRITAIN: A Soldier'S Life For Harry; BRITAIN: Blair Shuffles Ministers; BRITAIN: Firefighters Settle Dispute; FRANCE: Strikes Fizzle; CZECH REPUBLIC: Bribery On Jet Deal Alleged;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Bush administration mobilizes to keep its Middle East peace initiative from unraveling; Secretary of State Colin L Powell and other envoys will travel to region to seek mutual concessions from Israel and Palestinians; Powell speaks on telephone to Prime Min Ariel Sharon and Palestinian Prime Min Mahmoud Abbas, urging that efforts be made to get peace talks back on track; John S Wolf, new American envoy to Middle East, is scheduled to leave for Israel on June 13 as part of team to monitor progress on implementing peace plan; Bush administration is frustrated that Arab leaders have not followed through with their pledge to cut off support for Palestinian militant groups responsible for acts of violence against Israelis; photo (M)
news.title: Envoys Hopefully Hit Road On Behalf of Imperiled Map

news.abstract: Israel's Army escalates battle with Hamas militants, blasting Palestinian car with helicopter-fired missiles in Gaza City and killing seven people, including Yasir Taha, Hamas leader, his wife and child; attack comes as Israelis and Palestinians are still burying their dead from carnage day before; in grimly familiar pattern, signs of diplomatic progress have been greeted almost immediately with surge in violence throughout 32 months of fighting; government-owned Israeli Radio says army has been ordered to 'completely wipe out' Hamas movement after suicide bombing of bus in Jerusalem; 17th victim of that bombing dies of wounds; Israel says new Palestinian Prime Min Mahmoud Abbas has proved unable or unwilling to rein in militants since he assumed office six weeks ago; Palestinians say Israeli actions are badly undercutting Abbas, making it impossible for him to resume cease-fire talks with Palestinian militants; he has ruled out using force against them; Hamas says violence is likely to worsen, and it calls on foreigners to leave Israel; White House blames Palestinian extremist for violence; photos; map (L)
news.title: Israeli Assault on Hamas Leaves 7 More Dead

news.abstract: News analysis of long, hard resistance Americans face from Saddam Hussein loyalists; says that while Hussein may not be directing insurgency, nor even be alive, he provides rallying point for former Baathists, many of whom are plotting return to power as part of movement called Return Party (M)
news.title: U.S. Faces a Long Fight With Hussein Partisans

news.abstract: Adel Qazzaz, director general of Iraq's Northern Oil Co, says explosion along major oil pipeline route in north-central Iraq appears to have been act of sabotage; incident comes as State Oil Marketing Organization, which oversees export of Iraqi oil, announces companies that will buy Iraq's first oil exports since war (M)
news.title: Iraqi Pipeline Blast Is Laid To Sabotage

news.abstract: TODI, Italy—  Of all recent art movements, few were execrated by the modernists so virulently as Photorealism. The painters and sculptors of this school, which emerged in the United States in the mid-1960s, produced more or less exact copies of photographs (or in the case of sculptures, often direct body casts), recording seemingly banal city scenes, suburban streets, storefronts, diners, consumer goods, automobiles and motorcycles, with phenomenal adeptness, but with a disconcerting level of emotional detachment.
