news.title: CONTEMPORARY ART:A SPECIAL REPORT : A young artist in Umbria re-examines contours of Photorealism

news.abstract: Czech Republic Television survey shows voters overwhelmingly support membership in European Union with 84% of those asked casting yes ballots for referendum (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: Court Backs Veteran On Gulf Illness

news.abstract: Authorities in Thailand arrest Narong Penanam after seizing large amount of radioactive material he was selling for use in so-called dirty bombs, breaking up plot to sell it to terrorists; material is cesium-137, radioactive byproduct of nuclear power plants commonly found in medical equipment; law enforcement and terrorism experts express alarm that material is available on black market; Penanam, who has no known ties to terrorist groups, is caught in sting operation (M)
news.title: Police in Thailand Seize Radioactive Material

news.abstract: Prime Min Tony Blair's government proposes creation of American-style Supreme Court and independent commission to appoint judges in move to free up Britain's judicial system from political control (M)
news.title: Blair Seeks a Supreme Court Modeled on the U.S. Version

news.abstract: Thousands of American troops backed by tanks, planes and helicopters carry out extensive raids in restive city of Falluja and in at least two other Iraqi cities; military operation is one of largest in Iraq since end of major fighting; no American casualties are reported; dozens of suspected Baath Party members are detained; map; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. FORCES LAUNCH RAIDS IN IRAQ CITIES TO QUELL UPRISINGS

news.abstract: Pentagon officials monitoring attacks on American forces in Iraq say that there are no indications of a centrally organized resistance movement.
news.title: Pentagon Officials Say They See No Organized Iraqi Resistance

news.abstract: More than 2,000 United States marines aboard amphibious assault ship Kearsarge steam toward west coast of Africa to prepare for possible evacuation of American citizens from strife-torn Liberia; more than 500 foreigners are evacuated in week from Monrovia (S)
news.title: Marines Steam to Liberia

news.abstract: European Union delegates struggle to draft its first constitution; 105 delegates who make up Convention on Future of Europe try to codify common ground among long-established states that will give their union more of a logical structure--and perhaps more power--as they expand eastward; draft constitution states that every national of a member state shall be citizen of union; when union expands, that would mean mega-Europe of 450 million citizens, and economy of more than $9 trillion; proposed constitution states that European Union law will have primacy over that of member states; simplifies voting rules and spells out areas like trade policy in which union will have full authority and other areas to be shared with member states, including justice, transportation and economic and social policy; photo of president of European Convention, Valery Giscard de'Estaing of France, and his vice presidents, Jean Luc Dehaene of Belgium and Giuliani Amato of Italy; map (L)
news.title: EUROPE DRAFTING ITS CONSTITUTION

news.abstract: The Israeli leader's tough talk came only hours after an Egyptian delegation failed to win a cease-fire pledge from Palestinian militants.
news.title: Sharon Vows Tough Line After Hamas Rejects Cease-Fire

news.abstract: European Union governments said today that they were ready to use force if necessary to combat the threat of weapons of mass destruction.
news.title: European Union Toughening Stance on Weapons Policy

news.abstract: Official Iran is pitted against the kind of society in which most Iranians want to live.
news.title: Young Iranians Are Chafing Under Aging Clerics' Edicts

news.abstract: Jose Dirceu de Oliveira e Sliva, chief of staff of Pres Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva of Brazil, is generally regarded as second most powerful man in Brazil, acting as political coordinator and gatekeeper of government; power is enhanced by fact that da Silva's keeps his distance from minutiae of government; Dirceu says government's commitment to improve, develop and radicalize Brazilian democracy has not changed, even though it is maintaining policies his party criticized when it was in opposition; remains suspicious of US, but American officials say Dirceu has been coopertaive and pragmatic in dealing with them; photo (M)
news.title: Behind Brazil's Leftist Leader, a Kindred Spirit Thrives

news.abstract: Lahib Naoman, 48-year-old Iraqi lawyer, has paid the price of running afoul of Saddam Hussein, beginning 20 years ago when she defended man accused of stealing videocassette recorder belonging to Hussein's son Uday; has spent 17 years in and out of Baghdad's prison and psychiatric hospitals; now lives in penury in a near empty house; photo (M)
news.title: Hurt in Body and Mind, A Lawyer Battles On

news.abstract: Federal wildlife biologists in United States say polar bears that traverse floating ice between Russian Arctic and Alaska are being shot in rising numbers by poachers on Russian shores; say killing could greatly diminish bear population if it is not slowed; findings are released as US and Russia consider ratifying treaty they signed in 2000 to protect shared population of about 4,000 bears; treaty would allow limited hunting by native populations but would clamp down on poaching under management plan developed by scientists and representatives of native communities; Pres Bush has urged Senate to approve treaty (M)
news.title: Hunt Imperils Polar Bears In Bering Sea, Report Says

news.abstract: Prime Min Ariel Sharon, addressing Israel's Parliament, warns that Middle East diplomacy will stall if 'terror runs rampant,' and pledges to 'hound the terrorists' until Palestinian security forces crack down on them; speech comes only hours after visiting Egyptian delegation fails to win cease-fire pledge from Hamas and other militant Palestinian factions during two days of talks in Gaza Strip; Palestinian Prime Min Mahmoud Abbas arrives in Gaza City for new talks with Hamas, which has rebuffed his previous appeals for truce; Palestinian officials say they are caught between widely divergent demands of Israel and Hamas; each side wants other to agree to truce first; nevertheless, Israeli and Palestinian officials renew security talks; further talks are considered likely on proposal for withdrawing Israeli troops from Palestinian areas in northern Gaza, with Palestinian security forces replacing them; violence remains constant threat, with Hamas refusing to suspend its bombing campaign and with Israeli troops still operating in and around Palestinian cities; Sharon' s speech focuses on security and is directed at his core of right-wing supporters who are deeply skeptical of peacemaking efforts after 32 months of almost daily fighting; he is being criticized by both left and right; photo (M)
news.title: Sharon Vows to 'Hound' Hamas, Which Rejects a Cease-Fire Bid

news.abstract: Iran is urged to sign protocol that would give United Nations nuclear weapons inspectors right to conduct more intrusive examinations of its facilities; both Iran's main trading partner, European Union, and Russia, whose engineers are helping it build civilian nuclear power plant, call on Tehran to provide necessary cooperation; calls come after governing board of International Atomic Energy Agency formally reviews recent report that gives new details about Iranian plans for heavy water research reactor, which could be used in production of plutonium for nuclear weapons; US State Dept responds to developments by calling on board of IAEA to formally urge Iran to sign protocol, which was added to Nuclear Nonproliferation Treaty (M)
news.title: Iran Is Urged To Sign Pact Giving Power To Inspectors

news.abstract: Pres Bush sweeps aside criticism that United States overstated threat posed by Iraq as work of 'revisionist historians' and says there is no doubt that Saddam Hussein posed 'threat to the United States' for past dozen years; speaks to small-business owners in Elizabeth, NJ, dwelling largely on benefits of recently passed tax cuts; makes no mention of so-far fruitless search for Hussein's chemical, nuclear or biological weapons; his speech is seen as harbinger of his approach to early days of his re-election campaign; his decision not to delve into question of unconventional weapons comes 11 days after he addressed American troops in Qatar, insisting then that his concerns about Hussein's weapons were justified; photo (M)
news.title: In Speech, Bush Reiterates Threat Hussein Posed, but Makes No Mention of Weapons Search

news.abstract: Japanese police obtain arrest warrant for Lance Cpl Jose W Torres, United States Marine accused of raping 19-year-old woman on island of Okinawa on May 25; he is now in military custody (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Japan: Warrant For Marine In Rape Case

news.abstract: Palestinian officials say they are nearing cease-fire agreement with three groups, including Hamas, that are responsible for most terrorist attacks against Israel; 7-year-old Israeli girl is killed and 5-year-old sister seriously wounded when Palestinian gunman opens fire on car inside Israel, northeast of Tel Aviv; photo; Mahmoud Zahar of Hamas says it is 'proper time for hudna,' using Arabic word for truce, but not without long list of concessions, including release of prisoners, withdrawal of Israeli forces from much of West Bank and Gaza and end of assassinations of militants (M)
news.title: Palestinians Raise Hope of Cease-Fire Deal With Militants

news.abstract: Human Rights Watch accuses US troops of using excessive force in two April shootings that killed 20 Iraqis and wounded at least 86; soldiers were responding to hostile fire from protesters in Falluja (S)
news.title: Rights Group Says U.S. Soldiers Twice Used Excessive Force

news.abstract: WHO lifts advisory against travel to Taiwan, leaving Beijing as only place travelers are urged to avoid because of SARS risk; Taiwan has had five or fewer new cases every day this month (S)
news.title: As SARS Ebbs, W.H.O. Lifts Its Advisory On Taiwan

news.abstract: Sec Colin L Powell says US has broad support to press North Korea to abandon nuclear weapons program; comments in Cambodia, where Assn of South East Asian Nations and Asian Regional Forum will discuss efforts against regime; US move to interdict shipments of nuclear materials draws new threat of retaliation from North Korea (M)
news.title: Plan to Block North Korean Nuclear Shipments Gains Support

news.abstract: Letter From South America reports that Pres Nestor Kirchner is carrying out inaugural pledge to seek justice for estimated 30,000 people who disappeared during 'dirty war' of military dictatorship between 1976 and 1983; photo of mass grave; Kirchner purges military command, says he will allow extradition of human rights violators wanted in other countries and makes clear he wants Supreme Court to overturn amnesty laws and pardons (M)
news.title: Now the Dirtiest of Wars Won't Be Forgotten

news.abstract: LONDON:—  The David and Victoria Beckham phenomenon, having left Hollywood somewhat underwhelmed, touched down at Narita Airport in Tokyo on Wednesday to the tumult of a thousand shrieking girls, fans of the soccer player.
news.title: Beckham's eye-catching knack for the soft sell

news.abstract: Italian Parliament grants Prime Min Silvio Berlusconi immunity from prosecution while he remains in office, effectively derailing his corruption trial just days before he assumes rotating presidency of European Union; Pres Carlo Azeglio Ciami is expected sign law quickly (M)
news.title: Parliament In Italy Passes Immunity Law For Berlusconi

news.abstract: The secretary of state said that he would press for a transfer of security operations in the northern Gaza Strip to Palestinians.
news.title: Powell to Visit Israel to Ask for Looser Reins in Gaza

news.abstract: Russian court orders parole of Eduard Limonov, writer who came to lead ultranationalist National Bolshevik Party and who was sentenced in April to four years in prison for weapons possession (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Writer-Politician To Be Freed

news.abstract: Happy Sindane becomes national sensation after South African teenager walks into Bronkhorstspruit police station and tells officer that he is white and was kidnapped from his Afrikaner parent as young child and virtually enslaved in black township; police are flooded with callers claiming to be his parents, and court orders DNA tests in hopes of finding resolution; case raises legacy of apartheid and country's obsession with racial makeup, not only as symbol of white fears of being taken over by black majority but also because one focus of DNA testing is to determine whether Happy is of mixed race; map; photos (M)
news.title: 'Lost Boy' Shines Light on Race in South Africa

news.abstract: European leaders broadly endorsed the draft of a first-ever constitution for the European Union at a summit meeting here today.
news.title: Draft of European Union's Constitution Wins General Support

news.abstract: American intelligence analysts now believe that Saddam Hussein is more likely alive than dead, view reinforced in recent weeks by intercepted communications among some of his fugitive supporters; new hunt for Hussein is being led by Task Force 20, secret military organization that includes members of Army's highly specialized Delta Force and Navy's elite counterterrorism squads, with support from Central Intelligence Agency; prevailing belief is that Hussein is still in Iraq; arrest of Abid Hamid Mahmoud al-Tikriti, Hussein's closest confidant, has raised some hope of obtaining more conclusive information; but Mahmoud's success in eluding capture for nearly two months in country occupied by nearly 150,000 troops underscores reality that Iraq still offers many hiding places; chronology of developments since March 20 in trying to determine Hussein's fate; photos (M)
news.title: Hussein Is Probably Alive in Iraq, U.S. Experts Say, Citing Intercepts

news.abstract: Thousands of war munitions dumped by American, British and Soviet military after World War II are leaching toxic chemicals into Baltic Sea as weapon casings corrode; even entire ships full of weapons, most captured from Germany, were scuttled and forgotten; problem is compounded by fisherman who go to risky areas to catch depleted fish stocks, using increasingly aggressive methods, including bottom tackle that snag objects; scientists believe that some poisons dissipate in water, but others can build up in food chain; fishing is now forbidden around four main dumping grounds, which hold estimated 300,000 tons of munitions; in other areas, vessels are required to keep special protective gear and medical kits on board; environmental and citizens' groups are demanding cleanup, but there is wide disagreement on how to approach problem; map; photo (M)
news.title: Discarded War Munitions Leach Poisons Into the Baltic

news.abstract: Shimon Peres is elected as temporary leader of Israel's Labor Party, which suffered its worst electoral defeat earlier in year; party leader Amram Mitzna resigned on May 4, and no clear successor has emerged (S)
news.title: Shimon Peres Is Elected Temporary Leader of Labor Party

news.abstract: Soldier from 804th Medical Brigade is killed south of Baghdad when military ambulance in which he is traveling comes under fire from rocket-propelled grenade; soldier is 13th to die since small-scale, guerrilla-style attacks on American troops in Iraq began in May, several in recent days (M)
news.title: G.I. Dies as Military Ambulance Is Hit by Rocket-Propelled Grenade

news.abstract: Article profiles Akil Dair, 26-year-old part-time college student who lives with his family in Baghdad, Iraq; Dair and other young Iraqi men are being barraged by ideas, ideologies and political concepts they scarcely understand after life of isolation and war under Saddam Hussein; role models they adopt could be crucial to success of American effort to create democratic, friendly Iraq; photos (M)
news.title: Young Iraqis Face a Bewildering World. How They Fare Could Be Vital.

news.abstract: PARIS—  Finding an acceptable apartment in a pleasant neighborhood abroad can be challenging enough for an expat who wants to hit the ground running in a foreign assignment. And while signing a lease may bring a sigh of relief, expats should take extra care to study local real estate customs and read the fine print of their lease if they want to prevent misunderstandings, unforeseen obligations or even the surprise of a sudden eviction.
news.title: Moving in : Reading the fine print of lease can prevent misunderstandings

news.abstract: Japanese encephalitis outbreak in Guangdong Province (China) is confirmed as regional authorities announce 18 deaths and 211 cases of disease; secrecy about outbreak, reminiscent of regional confusion regarding SARS outbreak, has caused Hong Kong officials to be concerned (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: China: Disease Outbreak Confirmed

news.abstract: Abid Hamid Mahmoud al-Tikriti, captured top aide to Saddam Hussein, reportedly tells US interrogators that Hussein and sons Uday and Qusay survived war and that he himself fled to Syria with sons after conflict; news reportedly sparks intense burst of clandestine US military activity aimed at capturing Hussein and his sons; American officials say conviction among loyalists that Hussein is still alive is motivating military resistance against US forces; photo (M)
news.title: CAPTURED OFFICIAL IS SAID TO TELL U.S. HUSSEIN SURVIVED

news.abstract: Italian President Carlo Azeglio Ciampi signs bill giving Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi immunity from prosecution while in office; legislation freezes his current bribery trial and avoids potential fallout from verdict before he becomes European Union president on July 1; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Italy: Law Signed Ending Berlusconi Trial

news.abstract: American administrator L Paul Bremer 3d comes to World Economic Forum in Jordan with message of guarded optimism about Iraq's prospects; asserts that Iraq would soon resume oil exports and begin establishing economy based on private enterprise; seeks to counter image of an Iraq that is sliding into chaos, with rising attacks on American troops and frustration over inability to find Saddam Hussein or unconventional weapons; claims Iraq has already come long way in establishing law and order (M)
news.title: Overseer Says Iraq Economy Is Beginning To Recover

news.abstract: ATHENS, June 22 — Greek law enforcement officials said they found and confiscated 680 tons of explosives tonight from a boat off the country's western coast. The officials described the explosives as suspicious.
news.title: Greek Officials Confiscate Explosives From Boat

news.abstract: Israeli forces killed a leader of Hamas a day after Secretary of State Colin L. Powell tried to conclude a cease-fire agreement with Israeli and Palestinian leaders. Page 4.
news.title: Israelis Kill a Hamas Leader

news.abstract: Israel and the Palestinians continued to try to narrow their differences over the turnover of security throughout the Gaza Strip to the Palestinians.
news.title: Killing of Hamas Chief Shouldn't Stop Peace Efforts, Powell Says

news.abstract: A large and vocal group of Anglicans are protesting their church's decision to name a gay priest, Dr. Jeffrey John, as the new Bishop of Reading.
news.title: Anglicans Deeply Divided Over Appointment of Gay Bishop

news.abstract: Hamas leader Mahmud al-Sahar discusses his organization's strategy of violence, the conditions of a cease-fire, and cooperation with the Palestinian Autonomous Authorit
news.title: 'Drinking the same poison'

news.abstract: Large and vocal group of Anglicans protest their church's decision to name Dr Jeffrey John as new bishop of Reading, Eng; he is first openly homosexual bishop nominated by Church of England; action has stirred deeply divisive reaction that goes well beyond Reading; Dr John issues statement acknowledging that he has been in relationship for 27 years with male partner but avowing that they ceased having sex after church issued 1991 policy paper that permits members of congregation to pursue faithful homosexual relationships but demands celibacy from gay priests; photo (M)
news.title: New Gay Bishop Unsettles Church of England

news.abstract: The talks are on whether and how Palestinian security forces will assume control from Israeli troops for policing the West Bank city of Bethlehem and parts of the Gaza Strip.
news.title: Israelis and Palestinians Seeking Accord on Gaza

news.abstract: With no conclusive evidence found in the five days, the prospect that the former Iraqi leader had been killed was seen as a remote possibility at best.
news.title: U.S. Officials Doubt Hussein Was Killed in Raid Near Syria

news.abstract: King Abdullah II of Jordan, host of World Economic Forum conference, seems to have created his own style in four years since death of his father, King Hussein; in part he has extended his father's courtly manner, but he seems to want to blend dignity of his job with more open manner; some in kingdom fault him harshly for dissolving Parliament and postponing elections for two years; others credit him for holding elections at all in region ruled generally by fiat of one kind of another; photo (M)
news.title: Jordan's King Shows Guests Some Flair

news.abstract: Palestinian officials predict that militant group Hamas will soon agree to halt violence against Israel temporarily, acceding to request by Prime Min Mahmoud Abbas and to international pressure; Marwan Barghouti, rising leader of Yasir Arafat's Fatah movement who is imprisoned by Israel, is instrumental in seeking cease-fire; Israeli and Palestinian security officials report some progress toward determining how Palestinian security forces will assume control from Israeli troops for policing West Bank city of Bethlehem and parts of Gaza Strip; photos (M)
news.title: Temporary Truce by Hamas Expected, Palestinians Say

news.abstract: HONG KONG:—  The World Health Organization on Monday removed Hong Kong from the list of SARS-infected areas, marking the end of a four-month crisis during which the deadly respiratory disease spread around the world.
news.title: WHO lifts Hong Kong from list of SARS areas

news.abstract: US Special Operations forces engage in firefight with several Syrian guards during American attack on convoy suspected of carrying fugitive Iraqi officials near Iraqi border with Syria on June 18; at least one of Iraqi vehicles destroyed in attack is hit by American attack helicopters on Syrian side of border; five Syrian guards are wounded, and three of them remain in American custody for medical treatment; American officials detain as many as 20 Iraqis, but do not provide any details about their identities; US has not yet discussed matter with Syrian government because so much remains unclear, including whether Syrian guards were trying to help or hinder American effort to halt convoy; photos; map (M)
news.title: SYRIANS WOUNDED IN ATTACK BY U.S. ON CONVOY IN IRAQ

news.abstract: Pres Bush removes Ali Saleh Kahlah al-Marri, Qatari student, from criminal justice system and declares him enemy combatant after prosecutors say new evidence links him to another round of terrorist plots by Al Qaeda after Sept 11; Marri is moved from prison in Illinois to military brig in South Carolina, where he can be held indefinitely without access to lawyer unless military decides to bring charges; critics of detention policies say move adds to confusion over using array of military, criminal and civil measures against people considered terrorism suspects; photo (M)
news.title: Bush Declares Student an Enemy Combatant

news.abstract: Series of pipeline explosions, the work of expert saboteurs, hampers efforts to restore oil production in Iraq, which is now only third of prewar levels; looting of equipment slows repair work; photo (M)
news.title: A Rash of Pipeline Fires Is Keeping Workers Busy

news.abstract: US officials say Abid Hamid Mahmoud al-Tikriti, senior lieutanant to Saddam Hussein, obtained Belarussian passports for himself and others, possibly including Hussein's sons, in Syria, where Mahmoud fled after war; say Mahmoud never claimed Hussein fled to Syria, only that he saw him alive after American attack on April 7 that was attempt to kill him; believe Hussein is still in Iraq; Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld and Gen Richard B Myers defend June 18 raid on Iraqi convoy along Syrian border, which was prompted by Mahmoud's account of Iraqi officials' escape into Syria (M)
news.title: Hussein's Top Aide Got Belarussian Passports, U.S. Officials Say

news.abstract: Latest hopes for peace in Bunia, northeastern provincial town in Congo, and Liberia are dealt setbacks; multinational force that was to declare Bunia a gun-free zone wants more time for talks with militia that now controls town; chief rebel group in Liberia says it will boycott peace talks until Pres Charles Taylor steps down, and there are reports of renewed fighting near Monrovia, prompting yet another exodus of terrified civilians from capital; map (M)
news.title: Latest Peace Hopes Thwarted on Africa's Battlefields

news.abstract: Bush administration says it will not comment on arrest by Israel of 130 Palestinians in Hebron until American experts can inquire about who was detained and what evidence lead Israel to make arrests (S)
news.title: U.S. Silent on Israeli Move

news.abstract: Mexican military, fulfilling new freedom of information law, discloses to El Universal Mexico City newspaper that 299 soldiers have been court-martialed since December 2000; 210 of those tried were convicted on variety of charges (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Mexico: Military Breaks Silence

news.abstract: Killing of six British military policemen in southern Iraq and ambush of British paratroopers threaten to raise new questions among Britons about deployment of their troops alongside US forces; adds to political woes confronting Prime Min Tony Blair over his reasons for sending British troops to Iraq in first place; several antiwar members of Parliament urge deployment of United Nations peacekeepers to replace British and American troops; Foreign Sec Jack Straw says dossier of supposed evidence that Iraq possessed illicit weapons, which Blair used to justify Iraqi invasion, has become embarrassment and should never have been published (M)
news.title: Deaths of Military Policemen Raise New Doubts Back Home in Britain

news.abstract: MONTGERON, France:—  The steak at the Reveil Matin in the Paris suburb of Montgeron is tender, the house wine thin but acceptable, the service no worse than the usual inattentive, the bill a bit less than it would be in a more chic and higher-rent restaurant in the capital.
news.title: Worth a (bike) trip, 100 years later

news.abstract: American Embassy in Nairobi (Kenya) reopens after closure for several days amid concerns of terrorist attack; Kenyan and Tanzanian officials find fault with American and British travel warnings to East Africa made during state of alert (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Kenya: Embassy Reopens

news.abstract: Mobile abortion clinic housed on Dutch ship and organized by Women on Waves, women's rights group, is fined $3,000 by Wladyslawowo (Poland) port authorities for failing to follow docking instructions that required ship to tie up away from protesters; boat brings birth control and pregnancy counseling to countries where abortion is illegal; boards women wanting abortions and takes them to international waters to perform procedure (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Poland: Abortion Boat Fined

news.abstract: A new generation of Al Qaeda-trained terrorists as well as veterans of the Islamic extremist group were said to continue to threaten the global community.
news.title: Al Qaeda Remains a Global Threat, U.N. Report Says

news.abstract: Prime Min Tony Blair, responding to killing of six British soldiers in disputed circumstances in southern Iraq, pledges to maintain British military presence there and to send reinforcements if needed; pledge seems designed to head off suggestions by some legislators that Britain should begin contemplating 'exit strategy' (M)
news.title: Blair Says Reinforcements May Go to Iraq

news.abstract: Pres Bush outlines ambitious agenda for advancing peace and prosperity in Africa; pledges $100 million to help countries fight terrorism and makes case for expanded trade as most powerful engine for fighting poverty on continent; speaks to US-Africa Business Summit, group of African leaders, business executives and investors, 11 days before his scheduled first trip as president to sub-Saharan Africa; his speech is striking for its blunt calls for change in nations that have been wracked by violence; he demands that Pres Charles Taylor of Liberia step down to avert further bloodshed in his country; he calls for change of government and 'return to democracy' in Zimbabwe, which is ruled by Robert Mugabe; pledges active role in bringing peace to Sudan, saying he has asked his special envoy to Sudan John C Danforth to travel there to bring end to conflict (M)
news.title: Bush Calls for Changes in Africa To End Wars and Promote Trade

news.abstract: Saudi Arabia arrests senior figure in Al Qaeda who is believed to have played crucial role in planning and carrying out May bombings in Riyadh that killed 34 people, including 8 Americans; senior American and Saudi government officials say they believe same man, Ali Abd al-Rahman al-Faqasi Al-Ghamdi, had been planning further operations against American targets; Ghamdi's name and picture were included among those of 19 men sought in connection with arms caches seized in Riyadh several days before attack; photo (M)
news.title: Saudi Arabia Arrests a Suspect in the Riyadh Bombings

news.abstract: Ferns Diocese in County Wexford, center of Ireland's clerical sex abuse scandal, directs priests to never be alone with single child or adolescent and to use public rooms with windows when meeting with groups of children or teenagers (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Ireland: Rules For Clergy And Children

news.abstract: As a poll showed public disenchantment with the Labor Party, Foreign Secretary Jack Straw said today that he stood by the accuracy of British government intelligence on Iraqi weapons.
news.title: Support for Britain's Labor Party Eroding, Poll Says

news.abstract: Ahmed Jubarah, who helped plant bomb that killed 13 people and wounded more than 60 in Jerusalem in 1975, is released from jail after 27 years in concession by Israel to encourage new peace process; he was longest-serving Palestinian prisoner; he has emerged as symbol of popular Palestinian movement for release of prisoners; he has not expressed any shame or remorse for randomly killing civilians, but he says he longs for peace; says only after Israel agrees to Palestinian state free of settlements can violence end; photo (M)
news.title: Arab Bomber, Freed After 27 Years, Longs for Peace but Has No Regrets

news.abstract: Palestinian leaders reached beyond Hamas and Islamic Jihad today to persuade other, smaller factions to agree to a complete suspension of violence against Israelis.

news.abstract: Protests arise in Pakistan after Pres Pervez Musharraf, after meeting with Pres Bush at Camp David, suggests that Pakistani troops might be sent to Iraq if United States would finance the expedition; several politicians say move would make Pakistan Army nothing more than mercenary force (M)

news.abstract: Secretary of State Colin Powell offers public support for Christian Westermann, department chemical and biological weapons expert who told Congress that he felt pressured to make intelligence reports on Iraq and other matters conform to Bush administration policy (M)

news.abstract: New satellite images show that Amazon rain forest is disappearing at increasing rate--with about 10,000 square miles lost mainly to pasture land, plantations and illegal logging in 12-month period ended last August; scientists and environmentalists say about 20 percent of Amazon has already vanished and that rain forest could be wiped out in 80 years; Brazilian Environment Min Marina Silva promises emergency action but does not offer specific proposals (M)
news.title: Rain Forest Is Losing Ground Faster in Amazon, Photos Show

news.abstract: Bodies of two American soldiers missing in Iraq for 3 days are found, miles apart from their Humvee; military refuses to give any details about how men died or to answer speculation that they might have been abducted; two soldiers are Sgt First Class Gladimir Philippe and Pfc Kevin Ott; they disappeared near town of Balad, 20 miles from Baghdad, in area near strongholds of conservative Sunni Muslims; Army criminal investigators have been assigned to determine what happed at scene, to find out how two heavily armed soldiers and their armored military vehicle could have been taken without report of struggle or of gunfire; photos; map (M)
news.title: Bodies of G.I.'s, Missing 3 Days, Found in Iraq

news.abstract: Population that is both living longer and producing fewer children is beginning to change some of basics of both social and political life in Germany and elsewhere in Europe; many experts see government bids to cut pensions and other social services as harbinger of demographic shift with important implications for European societies as whole; median age is expected to rise from 37.7 to 52.3 in 2050 in Europe, compared with only 35.4 in United States, meaning European economic and military power will decline in world that is largely becoming younger; European population is shrinking as well; Europe seems to face choice of allowing more immigration or accepting less influential role in world affairs; graph of median age and fertility rate; photos (M)
news.title: An Aging Europe May Find Itself on the Sidelines

news.abstract: Midterm elections will be first national vote since Mexico's transition to multiparty rule, with control of Congress and future of Pres Vicente Fox hanging in balance; warring parties are spending heavily in quest for votes, yet polls suggest that half of electorate will sit election out; those who will vote seem set to keep power deeply divided, giving neither Fox nor any party upper hand and all but ensuring three more years of political stagnation until 2006 presidential election; photo (M)

news.title: U.S. Chill Flattens Mood at French Wine Fair

news.abstract: Quebec Premier Jean Charest, vowing change in provincial government, has cut cabinet by one-third, cut taxes on small businesses, slashed spending and promised to cut income taxes by 27 percent over next five years; engineered Liberals' landslide defeat of Parti Quebecois by playing down old debate over sovereignty and promising to cut government sloth (M)

news.abstract: China analysts say conflict between supporters of Pres Hu Jintao and predecessor Jiang Zemin exposes tensions within top leadership and makes it more difficult for new generation to put its stamp on politics; Jiang, 76, retains enormous political muscle by keeping allies in key posts and staying on as chairman of Central Military Commission; Hu, 60, solidifies his stature with strong handling of SARS epidemic, but has to navigate between liberal intellectuals calling bluntly for political change and Jiang allies, who fear instability and reportedly try to reverse trend toward government openness (M)
news.title: Analysts See Tension in China Within the Top Leadership

news.title: China's Leader Gives No Sign of Changes to Come

news.title: Bush Says Attacks on U.S. Forces Won't Deter Him From the Rebuilding of Iraq

news.abstract: China and Russia seek to delay Security Council condemnation of North Korea's nuclear arms program one day after top North Korean general says any sanctions or blockades initiated by United States would be considered 'complete breach' of truce that ended hostilities 50 years ago and would trigger 'merciless retaliatory measures' against South Korean population; North Korean Foreign Min Paek Nam Sun issued similar warning in his letter to Security Council last week, but tone of his letter contrasts sharply with harsh tone of general's follow-up letter; this leads some diplomats to wonder if there is internal North Korean dispute over what mix of conciliatory language and threats should be used with UN and US; one Asian diplomat notes how unusual it is to have Army communicating with UN (M)
news.title: Delay by U.N. On Rebuking North Korea Is Urged

news.abstract: European Parliament approves legislation to require strict labels for food and feed made with genetically altered ingredients; move is hailed by environmentalists but pilloried by American farmers; legislation is intended to better inform wary European consumers; it requires supermarkets to label all food containing more than 0.9 percent of genetically modified organism; it also ensures that such food will be traced from moment of its inception to its arrival in European Union through processing stage and into supermarkets; new law is expected to receive final approval by European Union's 15 member states this fall, and to take effect early next year; Bush administration criticizes bill, saying it would be burdensome for food producers, could prejudice consumers against genetically modified food and become barrier to free trade (M)
news.title: Europe Acts to Require Labeling of Genetically Altered Food

news.abstract: United States Central Command in Iraq says explosion at mosque in Falluja that killed at least six people, including mosque's imam, resulted from presence of bomb-making class inside; American commander says that unless troops are fired on from mosque, he will continue to adhere to policy of not searching them because it might risk further alienating Muslim population already seething at American-led occupation; members of Falluja mosque insist explosion was caused by American missile fired from helicopter or airplane; their version of events gains currency on streets of Falluja and beyond, prompting vows of revenge; neighbors of mosque say they heard no aircraft before explosion but they did hear that explosives were being stored at mosque; photo; map (M)
news.title: U.S. Attributes Explosion at Iraqi Mosque to Bomb-Making Activity

news.abstract: Russian authorities arrest Platon Lebedev, chairman of Menatep, company that owns 61 percent of giant Yukos Oil Co, on charges of embezzling money from state company in 1994; arrest, at hospital where Lebedev was convalescing, is first of major tycoon since Vladimor Gusinsky in 2000, as Pres Vladimir Putin consolidated power; arrest may be blunt message to Yukos chief executive Mikhail B Khodorkovsky to stop involving himself in opposition politics (M)
news.title: Russian Oil Man Arrested; Allies Blame Politics

news.abstract: Pers Bush, enmeshed in internal debate within administration on whether to send US peackeeping troops to Liberia, strongly implices that no soldiers will be deployed until Pres Charles Taylor leaves, interview with African reporters; US military officials meet in Ghana with West African representatives; photo of demonstrators in Monrovia (M)
news.title: Bush Insists Liberian President Go Before Troops Come In

news.abstract: Iraqi National Museum re-opens with display of treasures of Nimrud, found after war in submerged bank vault; Col Matthew Bogdanos says looting reports were greatly exaggerated; says that 12,000 objects stolen were mostly items like pottery shards and individual beads, that 42 display-quality objects were looted and ten have been recovered and that most precious collection of coins and seals were untouched because thieves dropped keys in dark (M)
news.title: Iraq Museum Reopens With Assyrian Treasures

news.abstract: A bipartisan group of senators, returning from Iraq, warned that American troops are stretched thin and face continuing attack.
news.title: After Tour, Senators Warn U.S. Is Spread Thin in Iraq

news.abstract: Suspected terrorist Shadi Mohd Mustafa Abdellah states during his Dusseldorf trial that he was part of four person group planning attacks on Jewish targets in Dusseldorf and on Jewish Museum in Berlin (Germany); Palestinian from Jordan, he trained with Al Qaeda, but contends he was working with Al Tawhid, terrorist group (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: Jewish Museum A Target

news.abstract: Hong Kong chief executive Tung Chee-hwa says he will remove or amend several of most controversial provisions of unpopular internal security bill, but not delay legislative consideration of bill; gambles that he can push through bill despite calls for delay by even one of two pro-government parties; bill calls for long jail sentences for people involved in sedition, secession and treason (M)
news.title: Hong Kong's Chief to Amend Internal Security Legislation

news.abstract: Platon Lebedev, chairman of Menatep, which owns 61% of Yukos, Russia's largest oil company, is arrested and his colleague Mikhail B Khodorkovsky is interrogated about alledged embezzlement; claims charges are false; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Prosecutors Quiz Oil Magnate

news.abstract: Arab satellite channel Al Jazeera broadcasts part of audiotape with voice claiming to be that of toppled Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein urging Iraqis to resist American and British invaders; tape comes as fighting intensifies further in Iraq and day after Bush administration offered $25 million reward for Hussein's capture; voice exhorts Iraqis to protect fighters attacking American and British forces and avoid cooperating with occupation authorities; American officials say troops killed 11 Iraqis that tried to ambush them on road near Balad; map; photo (M)
news.title: A Recorded Voice, Said to Be Hussein's, Calls for Resistance

news.abstract: Turkey protests in unusually harsh language what it calls detention of 11 Turkish soldiers by American forces in Sulaimaniya, northern Iraq, where there are signs Turks want to play more aggressive role; Prime Min Recep Tayyip Erdogan says Americans have released some of soldiers; scores incident; Turkish newspaper reports Americans acted on intelligence reports that Turkish commandos were plotting to assassinate Kurdish governor of nearby Kirkuk; Turkish officials deny claim; Min Abdullah Gul phones Sec Colin L Powell; hundreds of Turkish troops have operated in northern Iraq since mid-1990's, mainly to hunt down Kurdish guerrillas (M)
news.title: Turkey Says U.S. Has Detained Some of Its Soldiers in North Iraq

news.abstract: Two blasts rip through entrances to suburban Moscow rock festial, killing at least 16 people and wounding up to 60 more; Russian government blames female suicide bombers; at least one reportedly is identified as Chechen; blasts are first major terrorist act in Moscow since last Oct; seem to fit growing pattern of suicide bombing attacks on both government and civilian targets in and around Chechnya; map; photos (M)
news.title: Explosions at a Moscow Rock Festival Kill at Least 16

news.abstract: Government and democracy advocates brace for another showdown over internal security bill as Hong Kong chief executive Tung Chee-hwa softens bill but insists legislature pass it quickly; democracy suppporters call changes inadequate and vow to stop bill; China's national legislature urges Hong Kong to approve bill on time; Tung deleted provisions that would have allowed search and seizure without warrant during national security probes and let government ban groups subordinate to groups banned in China on security grounds; photo (M)

news.title: In Africa, Bush to Focus on Threats and Opportunities

news.abstract: Corsicans vote by slim margin to reject referendum intended to enhance their decision-making powers; Pres Jacques Chirac had supported referendum, calling it best way for Corsicans to affirm their attachment to France; few voters seem to understand purpose of exercise or whether outcome would improve their lives; many believe timing of arrest of Corsican nationalist who is most wanted man in France was not accidental, but crass political move intended to garner more positive votes; map (M)
news.title: In Blow to Paris, Corsica Rejects French Restructuring Plan

news.abstract: Three American soldiers are killed in 12-hour period in Baghdad amid growing signs of guerrilla resistance to American forces; deaths represent 26th, 27th and 28th American soldiers to be killed in hostile action since May 1, when Pres Bush said major fighting had ended; in first of latest attacks, American soldier accompanying United States officials visiting Baghdad Univ is fatally shot by unidentified gunman; this raises questions about whether movements of American officials are being tracked by Iraqi insurgents; military officials are describing recent attacks as isolated work of desperate Iraqis connected to toppled government of Saddam Hussein; Gen Richard B Myers, chairman of Joint Chiefs of Staff, says officials will examine whether attacks are becoming better organized; military officials in Baghdad say 7-day effort to root out Iraqi resistance and paramilitary activity in central Iraq has resulted in detention of 282 people and seizure of many weapons; photo; map (M)

news.abstract: Two officials overseeing American-led effort to rebuild Iraq say electricity and drinking water available in Baghdad and some other parts of country remain below prewar levels; assessment runs counter to Pentagon's earlier assurances that goal levels for improving services are almost met; it also reflects damage done by looters and saboteurs since end of major combat two months ago (M)
news.title: Water and Electricity in Baghdad Are Still Below Prewar Levels, Officials Say

news.title: AIDS-Afflicted Villagers Say Chinese Police Attacked Them

news.abstract: Abu Ghraib town council, first to be freely chosen in Iraq since fall of Saddam Hussein, hears litany of complaints about electric power, water, security and the like, and offers usual mix of limited help and impotence in return; Dari Hamis al-Dari, leader chosen by local tribes, says he and constituents are increasingly frustrated; photos; Dari, who has lived in Europe and speaks excellent English, maintained his independence during Hussein rule, shunning material blandishments; welcomes Americans and works closely with military commanders but he is losing faith, saying conditions have never been worse and warning that time is almost up for meeting expectations; Col Jeff Ingram, his partner, says Dari is caught in middle, but blames Iraqis who tear down power lines and rob each other (M)

news.abstract: United Nations court on war crimes in former Yugoslavia has several senior Serbian suspects in custody, but whether these men will link Slobodan Milosevic to crimes such as massacre of thousands of Bosnian Muslims at Srebrenica in 1995 remains unclear; two of four Serbian military officers on trial on charges of taking part in Srebrenica massacre have unexpectedly pleaded guilty and agreed to cooperate with prosecution; that could produce most complete picture yet of who ordered massacre and to what extent Serbia itself was involved; prosecutors learn that Serbia, which has stalled for more than year, has approved handing over large cache of classified documents that might prove vital in trial of Milosevic; prosecutors are trying to prove 66 counts of crimes involving three wars, including charges of genocide; photos (M)

news.abstract: Many Peruvians are unhappy with President Alejandro Toledo and suggest bringing back country's thoroughly disgraced former President Alberto K Fujimori; they recall Fujimori as being strong and decisive, while they see Toledo as weak, disorganized and leading Peru toward economic calamity; Toledo's approval rating has fallen to 11 percent, with majority saying he has failed to deliver on promises of better life; Fujimori has lived in exile in Japan since 2000; if he returns to Peru, he could be tried on charges ranging from embezzlement to treason; photo (M)
