news.abstract: United States calls for international conference in Oct to be attended by dozens of nations--many of which opposed war to oust Saddam Hussein--to raise billions of dollars to restore Iraq's economy; Bush administration is running into now familiar diplomatic problem: potential donor nations uneasy about financing military occupation; some American officials concede there will have to be more participation by other countries in deciding how money is raised and spent; Germany and France, which opposed war, say they are ready now to help rebuild Iraq but they want different structure for international aid; in response to donor concerns, American officials are pressing for creation of another element for occupation bureaucracy, trust fund for donations by other countries; it is not clear whether such a fund will be seen by donors as sufficiently independent; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Seeks Help With Iraq Costs, But Donors Want a Larger Say

news.abstract: Yasir Arafat and Palestinian Prime Min Mahmoud Abbas work out power-sharing agreement that guarantees Arafat continued influence over negotiations with Israel and over Palestinian security forces, and puts to rest threat by Abbas to resign; agreement between Arafat and Abbas said to reflect fact that two need each other: Abbas lacks Arafat's broad domestic support, while Arafat lacks Abbas's credibility with Israel and United States; Prime Min Ariel Sharon visits Prime Min Tony Blair in London in unsuccessful effort to persuade Blair's government to cut all ties to Arafat; Israelis have also failed to persuade other parties to new peace plan--Russia, European Union and United Nations--to adopt American and Israeli policy of isolating Arafat; photo (M)
news.title: Arafat and Abbas Agree On Roles in the Peace Effort

news.abstract: North Korean officials tell Bush administration that they have finished producing enough plutonium to make half-dozen nuclear bombs and that they intend to move ahead quickly to turn material into weapons; American intelligence agencies scramble to determine if this is bluff or if government of Kim Jong Il has really succeeded in producing material undetected; most recent tests suggest nuclear work has accelerated, but results are inconclusive; more test results are expected this week; North Korea's declaration, if true, would pose direct challenge to Pres Bush, who said two months ago that nuclear-armed North Korea 'will not be tolerated'; he decided early this year that it is too risky to take military action against main nuclear reprocessing plant at Yongbyon; now he must decide whether to negotiate with North--under its implicit nuclear threat--or hold fast to his insistence that any talks must include other regional nations, and that nuclear blackmail would be met with increasingly harsh sanctions; Bush is resisting bilateral talks for fear that Asian nations would press US to reach deal similar to one Clinton administration signed--'freeze' on nuclear activity in return for aid (M)
news.title: NORTH KOREA SAYS IT HAS MADE FUEL FOR ATOM BOMBS

news.abstract: KUWAIT: Leadership Shift; IRAN: Journalist Arrested;.
news.title: World Briefing: Middle East

news.abstract: ITALY: Drought Aid Sought; CYPRUS: An Official Yes To The E.U.; POLAND: New Wrapping For Stalin'S Gift;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Economic Observer, China's state news media, reports government is poised to purchase Japan's Shinkansen bullet train to link Beijing and Shanghai; high-speed rail technology will cost estimated $12 billion (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: China: Catching A Fast Train

news.abstract: US military officials say they are committed to bringing home Third Infantry Division's troops, who led capture of Baghdad, by autumn, but possibly not by September date given to Senate by Sec Donald Rumsfeld; Marine units, not usually used to occupy territory, may be assigned to Iraq (M)
news.title: Pentagon Sees Possible Delay In Return of the Third Division

news.abstract: Prime Minister Tony Blair travels to Washington on Thursday on a mission to underline Britain's relationship with the U.S.
news.title: Dispute on Iraq Weapons Clouds Blair's Trip to U.S.

news.abstract: European Union tentatively offers to help finance Iraq reconstruction, despite bruising disagreements with US, provided money is administered by international agency like World Bank or UN; Comr Christopher Patten says money will not be turned over to US-led authorities (M)
news.title: Europe Weighs Helping Out in Iraq, but Under Its Own Terms

news.abstract: NORTH KOREA: New Search For Missing G.I.'S; MYANMAR: Pressure From U.S.; PHILIPPINES: Ruling On Marcos Money; AFGHANISTAN: 5 Killed In Attack;.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: 'Comedic terrorist' Aaron Barschak, who last month crashed Prince William's 21st birthday party at Windsor Castle, will not be charged for his actions, but palace security commander has been removed from his post and some security staff are under investigation; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: Party Crasher Avoids Charges

news.abstract: The episode raised the question of whether the North had precipitated the episode as a dramatic reminder of its military presence.
news.title: Machine-Gun Fire Is Traded at Korean Border

news.abstract: John D Gerhart, specialist in African agriculture and land use for Ford Foundation and president of American University in Cairo until his retirement in 2002, dies at age 59; photo (M)
news.title: John Gerhart, 59, Expert On Agriculture in Africa

news.abstract: Tens of thousands of birds--finger-sized swifts--have been building their nests in Pattani, Thailand, for last three years; residents of Pattani are building alternative homes for them; they hope to sell their nests, which are important ingredient in expensive Asian delicacy, bird's nest soup; photos; map; recipe for bird's nest soup (M)
news.title: Pattani Journal; Snug Hotels for Birds, Who Pay With Their Nests

news.abstract: Italian police report that American military helicopter from base at Sigonella (Sicily) has crashed killing all four crew members; cause is unknown (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Sicily: U.S. Military Craft Crashes

news.abstract: Representatives of countries contributing to fund to support global struggle against AIDS and other diseases meet in Paris but make little progress toward easing cash crisis expected later this year; United Nations Secretary of Health and Human Services Tommy G Thompson says fund needs $3 billion by end of 2004; appropriations are bogged down in Washington and in European Union; governments are being upstaged by private donors; Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation has announced it would pay $100 million into fund immediately (M)
news.title: Global AIDS Fund Finding Few Answers to Its Cash Shortage

news.abstract: Zimbabwe's Council of Churches apologizes for inability to stop political violence and economic collapse in Zimbabwe, which has reached epic proportions since President Robert Mugabe won contested election last year; promises to work harder for government reforms (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Zimbabwe: Churches Regret Inaction

news.abstract: Tepid international support for the U.S. campaign to topple Saddam Hussein has led to larger American deployment in Iraq.
news.title: Lonely at the Top

news.abstract: Central Intelligence Agency and other agencies reportedly block Bush administration plan to deliver sharp new warnings about Syria's efforts to develop unconventional weapons; State Dept Under Sec John R Bolton's appearance before Congress is postponed, reportedly because he planned to say in classified portion of his testimony that Syria's development of chemical and biological weapons has progressed to point that it poses threat to stability in Middle East; government officials say intelligence agencies are being particularly rigorous in scrutinizing testimony that Bolton prepared about Syria because of controversy surrounding Pres Bush's use of disputed intelligence about Iraq's suspected nuclear weapons program (M)
news.title: New Warning Was Put Off On Weapons Syria Plans

news.abstract: Excerpts from Prime Min Tony Blair's speech to joint meeting of Congress (M)
news.title: Blair's Words: 'Our Job Is to Be There With You'

news.abstract: Palestinian leaders claim they have closed headquarters of at least 10 militant groups bent on waging war against Israel; in Syria, two largest militant groups, Hamas and Islamic Jihad, have closed their doors, but it is not apparent that they have ceased activities that prompted American demands in first place; Palestinian leaders say most of senior commanders of groups are still in Syria, or planning to return soon; American officials regard closing of offices in Syria as important test of willingness of Syrian leaders to modify their historic hostility toward Israel; photos (M)
news.title: Shutting Doors in Syria May Not End Militants' Attacks

news.abstract: Foreign Min Joschka Fischer of Germany, leading candidate to become European Union's first foreign minister under its new constitution, says in Washington that strong future Europe must not be developed in rivalry with US, as French government sees it; says 'we must bring all our capabilities together to win the peace' in Iraq and restates German offer of relief effort and economic help in Iraq (M)
news.title: German Official Says Europe Must Be U.S. Friend, Not Rival

news.abstract: White House sets out its most detailed explanation yet of how disputed intelligence about Iraq's weapons program made it into Pres Bush's State of the Union address; say White House changed initial draft of speech to make it more credible by attributing assertion that Iraq had been trying to acquire uranium from Niger to public British intelligence dossier; says change was made after internal White House deliberations about best way to present information and not, as intelligence officials have said, in response to concerns raised by CIA about credibility of intelligence reports; declassifies part of its main prewar intelligence summary on Iraq's weapons programs (M)
news.title: White House Tells How Bush Came to Talk of Iraq Uranium

news.abstract: CONGO: Troubles For New Government; ZIMBABWE: Court To Hear Election Challenge; SOUTH AFRICA: Happy Birthday!;.
news.title: World Briefing: Africa

news.abstract: Mohamed Dia, who grew up in rough Paris suburb, son of parents who immigrated to France from Mali, builds successful hip-hop clothing business and escapes poverty the America way; says there is more racial integration in US than in France and more opportunities for those who strive; plans to expand business to US; photo (M)
news.title: A Hip-Hop Fashion Bridge Across the Atlantic

news.abstract: Dr David Kelly, arms expert at center of dispute about BBC charge that British government doctored its intelligence reports on Iraq's weapons programs to gain public support for going to war, is found dead near his home in Oxfordshire, a suicide, according to his wife; wife, Jan Kelly, says her husband was under enormous stress; Alastair Campbell, aide to Prime Min Tony Blair, has conducted wide-ranging campaign against BBC, alleging that it has let its vaunted standards of impartiality lapse in pursuit of what he has called 'agenda against the war'; Kelly, soft-spoken civil servant, may have unwittingly become caught up in painfully public political storm for which his experience as respected expert on bioterrorism and his personal life as intensely private family man had not prepared him; photo (M)
news.title: British Arms Expert at Center of Dispute on Iraq Data Is Found Dead, His Wife Says

news.abstract: Interview with Palestinian Prime Min Mahmoud Abbas, who faces crucial week of diplomacy, bracketed by meetings with Pres Bush and Israeli Pres Ariel Sharon; in meeting with Sharon, Abbas is expected to demand Israeli pullout from at least two more Palestinian cities, and in meeting with Bush, he will request additional financial aid; Abbas, who remains unpopular among Palestinians, says it is Palestinians' interest to halt violence, respect Israelis as neighbors and pursue state only in West Bank and Gaza; expands on his vision for Palestinian state; photo (M)
news.title: On Eve of Crucial Week of Diplomacy, Abbas Sums Up Vision for a Palestinian State

news.abstract: A noisy political brawl between President Vladimir V. Putin and Mikhail B. Khodorkovsky, the country's richest man, is rewriting the rules of Russian politics.
news.title: Crackdown on Tycoon Shakes Up Moscow

news.abstract: Rebels advance swiftly into Monrovia, Liberia, shelling buildings, firing bullets and sending streams of civilians searching for safety where there is none; fighting continues for control of two bridges leading to city's main commercial artery; injured trickle into makeshift clinics run by international aid groups; rebels are frustrated with Pres Charles Taylor's promises to step aside and Pres Bush's so-far unfulfilled pledge to play active role in bringing stability; Taylor is urging his fighters to defend city and vows to remain until peacekeepers arrive; accuses US of failing to assist him in providing adequate protection for people; American Amb John W Blaney calls on rebels to stop advancing and participate in peace talks in Ghana; angry civilians, who feel they have nothing left to lose, are confronting government militias and demanding peace and end to looting; photo (M)
news.title: Rebels Push Toward the Heart of the Capital in Liberia

news.abstract: Deputy Defense Sec Paul Wolfowitz visits mass gravesite in Hilla, one of 62 such sites that American and allied investigators have discovered in southern Iraq; about 3,000 bodies have been unearthed, but townspeople say thousands more probably decomposed in shallow water table over last decade; Wolfowitz promises group of local Iraqis that occupying forces will lend whatever aid is ncessary to track down killers, but Iraqis say Americans have already squandered opportunities to capture suspected executioners and want them to do more (M)
news.title: Wolfowitz Visits Mass Graveyard of Hussein's Victims and Promises Help in Hunting Killers

news.abstract: Team of International Atomic Energy Agency representatives begins new round of inspections of Iran's nuclear sites (S)
news.title: New U.N. Team Enters Iran

news.abstract: United States is creating new Iraqi civil defense force in next 45 days that is intended to free up thousands of American troops for anti-guerrilla missions and put Iraqi face on occupation's postwar security efforts; goal is to field 7,000 American-trained militiamen to protect supply convoys and replace American troops now guarding power plants and ammunition depots; plan has strong support of new Iraqi Governing Council, and goes well beyond proposal under consideration at Pentagon to hire private contractors to provide security at sites around country; Deputy Defense Sec Paul D Wolfowitz, on visit to Iraq, says recruiting Iraqis for security and intelligence tasks is essential for rebuilding of Iraq to succeed; Gen John P Abizaid, new head of US Central Command, concurs; violence in Iraq continues; in latest incidents, two soldiers are killed and one is wounded in ambush near Mosul, and Iraqi driver for United Nations agency dies when convoy is attacked near Baghdad; American administrator L Paul Bremer 3d claims armed resistance to American-led occupation comes from small number of 'professional killers' drawn from remnants of old regime and poses 'no strategic threat' to Americans; cites signs of progress, including restoration of basic services, economic reforms and establishment of Iraqi Governing Council; photos (L)
news.title: U.S. Is Creating An Iraqi Militia To Relieve G.I.'s

news.abstract: More than 80 members of extended Palestinian family live in two large stone homes inside walled property in Hebron on West Bank; for them, Middle East peace initiative has brought hope, but no real confidence, that some normalcy might return to their constricted lives; Hebron, where 450 Jewish settlers live in few small enclaves among some 150,000 Palestinians, illustrates how complicted it will be to move forward with peace plan when mutual suspicion runs so deep; under previous agreement, Israel is permitted to keep troops in center of Hebron to guard settlers, even if soldiers leave other parts of town; this allows military to maintain strict control over 30,000 Palestinians; Palestinians complain of not being able to move about and of continued curfews; photos; map (M)
news.title: Curfew's Gone, but Troops Still Hem In Hebron Family

news.abstract: Protest erupts in Shiite holy city of Najaf after cleric Moktada al-Sadr claims that American forces have encircled his home, bent on arresting him for his incendiary sermon rejecting American-appointed Governing Council; he is scion of clan of beloved clerics; Lt Col Christopher C Conlin, commanding officer in Najaf, calls matter deliberate misunderstanding; says helicopters heard overhead and extra troops on streets are to provide security for visit by Deputy Defense Sec Paul D Wolfowitz; situation underscores point made by review of Iraq reconstruction effort by panel from Center for Strategic and International Studies, that lack of Iraqis involved in reconstruction at all levels, widespread unemployment and woefully inadequate means of communicating what is happening have combined to fuel ever-higher level of frustation and anger about American presence; photos; map (M)
news.title: In Shiite Holy City of Najaf, A Sudden Anti-U.S. Storm

news.abstract: Family of Britain's 11th Earl of Sandwich has set up sandwich-selling business; Lord Sandwich is one of few hereditary peers who won right to keep their seats in House of Lords after most were evicted by government in 1999; idea for sandwich company was born in 1992 when Lord Sandwich's second son, Orlando Montagu, stumbled on snack bar that called itself Earl of Sandwich and used family as its theme; photo (M)
news.title: London Journal; What's in a Name? In This Case, Fancy Sandwiches

news.abstract: Capitol Hill and Pentagon debate question of whether military needs more troops worldwide; Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld is considering how to assign enough soldiers to fill long-term mission of stabilizing Iraq while simultaneously fulfiling other overseas commitments and providing security against terrorism at home and abroad; of Army's 33 active-duty combat brigades, only three are described as free now for new mission; 21 brigades are now assigned overseas--16 in Iraq; of those not abroad, most are already earmarked as replacement forces for other missions, like one in Afghanistan, or are building their ranks or on emergency standby in case of crisis with North Korea; officials say National Guard and Reserves, which have 201,099 members on active duty, would probably have to shoulder some of burden of any additional missions as well; Marine Corps could be asked to share long-term peacekeeping duties, which traditionally have fallen to Army; on Capitol Hill, Sen James M Inhofe, Republican, and Sen Jack Reedm, Democrat, predict that Congress will support request to expand military's personnel roster, even with growing budget deficit; photo (M)
news.title: OFFICIALS DEBATE WHETHER TO SEEK A BIGGER MILITARY

news.abstract: Bucharest Journal on Romanian movie industry's hopes of luring Hollywood filmmakers from Prague with offers of lower labor costs, inexpensive wood for sets and stunning landscapes; biggest undertaking so far has been Cold Mountain, Civil War epic directed by Anthony Minghella, with everything from artificial snow and blood imported; American producer Michael Flannigan and director Allan A Goldstein comment on their low-budget movie Fire; photos (M)
news.title: Bucharest Journal; On Dracula's Terrain, an Infusion of New Blood

news.abstract: The White House refused today to say when, or if, the United States would send a peacekeeping force to Liberia.
news.title: White House Remains Noncommittal on Troops for Liberia

news.abstract: US marines arrive by helicopter to protect US Embassy in Monrovia and help evacuate foreigners in midst of heavy shelling by rebel forces; hundreds of enraged Liberians lay mutilated bodies by embassy's gates, demanding that US intervene; photos; map; mortar rounds pound neighborhood near embassy, one shell dropping on grounds (M)
news.title: ENRAGED LIBERIANS CALL FOR U.S. HELP AS REBELS ATTACK

news.abstract: Eleven Egyptian men accused of homosexual activity are aquitted, but labeled sinners by court; international human rights groups criticized similar case on March 21 in which homosexuals were sentenced by Egyptian court to three years in prison (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Middle East: Egypt: Court Acquits 11

news.abstract: The United Nations' special representative to Iraq gave firm support to the governing council in Baghdad today.
news.title: Iraq's Governing Council Gains Support at U.N.

news.abstract: US troops, acting on tip from Iraqi, surround house in Mosul and kill Saddam Hussein's sons Uday and Qusay in ferocious shootout after men inside refuse to surrender; photos; map; bodies are flown to Baghdad and identified; Gen Ricardo Sanchez says they were physically recognizable and 'multiple sources' were used to confirm identities; two other bodies taken from house may be Qusay's teenage son Mustapha and Uday's bodyguard; retired Iraqi general living nearby says others may have escaped; Sanchez says $15-million reward for each of sons will be paid, possibly to house's owner who neighbors say was seen sitting calmly in US vehicles near scene; US soldier is killed and second wounded in ambush north of Baghdad; Red Cross reports technician killed near Hilla (M)
news.title: Hussein's 2 Sons Dead in Shootout, U.S. Says

news.abstract: MADRID:—  Two bombs planted in beachfront hotels on Spain's Mediterranean coast exploded Tuesday, wounding 13 people, including foreign students, tourists and police officers.
news.title: Hotel bombings tied to Basque separatists : Two blasts wound 13 in Spain

news.abstract: Jomhouri Eslami, Iranian hard-line newspaper, infers that Iranian-Canadian photojournalist Zahra Kazemi, who died while in custody from brain hemorrhage, purposely slammed her head into wall in effort to frame her captors for maltreatment; hard-line Judge Saeed Mortazavi, who participated in Kazemi's interrogation, has recently been appointed to investigate her death (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Middle East: Iran: Report On Journalist

news.abstract: The U.S. holds irrefutable proof that Saddam Hussein's sons are dead, but the Iraqi public held out today for photographs.
news.title: Iraqis Wait to See U.S. Proof That Hussein Sons Are Dead

news.abstract: HONG KONG:—  A widening music industry scandal has transformed Hong Kong's top of the pops into a Ten Most Wanted list.
news.title: Allegations range from simple bribes to stock swindles : Music scandal rocks Hong Kong

news.abstract: Transvestites go back many centuries in Indonesia; their recognition stands in contrast to relative disapproval of homosexuality; now country's transvestites are trying to create roles for themselves beyond their long tolerated positions as television stars, entertainers and beauticians, moving even into political arena; in keeping with Indonesia's mostly relaxed practice of Islam, imams appear to be tolerant of transvestites; photo; map (M)
news.title: Surabaya Journal; For These Transvestites, Still More Role Changes

news.abstract: Military commanders in Iraq and Pentagon officials in Washington defend decision to storm house in Mosul where Saddam Hussein's sons were hiding rather than try to encircle it and force them to surrender; Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld says sons were 'determined to fight to the death'; Pres Bush says their deaths are clearest sign yet that former regime is gone and will not be coming back; military officials say waiting out two sons posed several risks, including their escape through suspected tunnel to nearby buildings; say prolonged siege could have given guerrillas time to fire on 200 American forces surrounding house; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Defends Move to Storm House Where Hussein Brothers Were Hiding

news.abstract: HONG KONG:—  A widening music industry scandal has transformed Hong Kong's top of the pops into a Ten Most Wanted list.
news.title: Allegations range from simple bribes to stock swindles : Music scandal rocks Hong Kong

news.abstract: Canada announces it is pulling its ambassador out of Iran after Canadian freelance photographer Zahra Kazemi, who died in Iranian custody after blow to head, is buried in her birthplace in southern Iran; Canadian government had demanded that her remains be sent to Canada for autopsy and burial; Kazemi was arrested on June 23 as she took pictures of protests outside prison in Tehran, where many dissidents are jailed; Iranian government first said she suffered stroke, then later admitted she died from brain hemorrhage caused by blow to her head; Canadian Foreign Min Bill Graham warns of other sanctions being considered against Iranl photo (M)
news.title: Canada Recalls Envoy From Iran After Burial of Detained Reporter

news.abstract: British Prime Min Tony Blair gives cautious endorsement to Hong Kong's democracy movement during stopover in former British colony; praises democracy advocates for keeping protests peaceful, and says he believes Chinese leaders are dedicated to Kong Kong's constitutional development and stability; some local democracy advocates are unimpressed by his caution (S)
news.title: Blair Urges Hong Kong to Preserve Stability

news.abstract: Top two American military officers warn of significant dangers facing United States military involvement in Liberia, two days after Secretary of State Colin L Powell calls for speedy deployment of troops to that country; Gen Richard B Myers and Gen Peter Pace, chairman and vice-chairman of Joint Chiefs of Staff, call for clear mission statement and strategy for successful end before any troops are sent; Myers says situation in Liberia does not lend itself to quick fix; Pace says if American troops are sent there, they may have to take military action; generals face insistent questioning from Sen John W Warner, chairman of Armed Services Committee, who calls situation in Liberia 'very tragic' but voices concern about sending American troops into 'volatile situation'; Congressional action is not required for Pres Bush to send in peacekeeping troops, but Warner urges him to define clear national security interests before ordering troops to Liberia; Powell, in closed session with House International Relations Committee, reiterates his support for American role, citing it as moral imperative (M)
news.title: PENTAGON LEADERS WARN OF DANGERS FOR U.S. IN LIBERIA

news.abstract: Argentine court issues arrest warrants for 46 individuals that were part of military dictatorship from 1976 to 1983, at request of Spanish Judge Baltasar Garzon; Argentine President Nestor Kirchner still needs to sign official decree allowing human rights violators to stand trial abroad; General Jorge Videla and Admiral Emilio Massera are among those indicted (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Argentina: Arrests Of Ex-Officers Ordered

news.abstract: Excerpts from report by Congressional intelligence committees on actions of FBI and CIA before and after Sept 11 attacks (L)
news.title: Excerpts From Report on Intelligence Actions and the Sept. 11 Attacks

news.abstract: Vice Pres Dick Cheney, in rare speech in Washington, offers White House's most forceful rebuttal to growing tide of skepticism about justifications for war in Iraq; argues it would have been 'irresponsible in the extreme' to ignore threat from Saddam Hussein's weapons program; his comments reflect effort to recast Iraq war as part of broader campaign against terror, linkage that administration officials say puts Iraq in better political light for them; Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld has made similar comments at recent news conference; Cheney's speech seeks to put administration's critics on defensive, saying safety of Americans was at stake; reads from four sections of recently declassified National Intelligence Estimate on Iraq's weapons programs; that report's conclusions have come under increasing scrutiny; photo (M)
news.title: Cheney Asserts No Responsible Leader Could Have Ignored Danger From Iraq

news.abstract: An Israeli soldier fired a machine gun that killed a 4-year-old Palestinian boy today and wounded two young girls.
news.title: Israeli Soldier's Gunfire Kills Palestinian Child and Wounds 2

news.abstract: Goods from Uday Hussein's extensive estate remain in locked warehouses and storage rooms in main palace, Baghdad, that American-led alliance uses as headquarters; much of collection will be auctioned off in coming months, with proceeds used to repair damage done by Saddam Hussein's violent older son; some items may be retained for museum or documentary record of Saddam Hussein's rule; photo (M)
news.title: Uday's Trove: To Remember or Forget?

news.abstract: Profile of Kurt Christensen, head of Danish Society for a Living Sea, Baltic-wide network of fishermen frustrated by region's dwindling fish stocks and near collapse of cod, ancient staple; group holds European Union's big subsidies have worsened depletion by building oversize fishing fleet; seeks ban on 'brutal fishing methods' like widespread bottom trawling that rips up sea floor; photo (M)
news.title: Fisherman Seeks to Harvest Ailing Baltic, Gently

news.abstract: Still-classified section of joint report by House and Senate intelligence committees reportedly says senior Saudi Arabian officials have funneled hundreds of millions of dollars to charitable groups and other organizations that may have helped finance Sept 11 terrorist attacks; section, which focuses on role played by foreign governments, reportedly centers almost entirely on Saudi Arabia; some members of Congress resent Bush administration's refusal to let committees disclose chapter's contents, holding desire to protect ruling Saudi family prevents American public from learning key facts about attacks; photos (M)
news.title: Classified Section Of Sept. 11 Report Faults Saudi Rulers

news.abstract: Pres Bush meets with Palestinian Prime Min Mahmoud Abbas at White House for first time; signals to both Palestinians and Israelis that he will push them toward tough decisions for peace; Bush suggests he backs Palestinians opposition to Israel's construction of security fence on West Bank, says Abbas must clamp down on Palestinian terrorism and rebuffs calls for Israel to release up to 6,000 prisoners, many accused of terrorism; notes United States recently provided $20 million to Palestinian Authority for economic development; says Secs John W Snow and Donald L Evans will visit region in fall to suggest specific development plans (M)
news.title: Bush, With Palestinian Prime Minister, Urges Compromise

news.abstract: Russian military court convicts Col Yuri D Budanov of murder in Mar 2000 strangling death of Chechen woman Elza Kungayeva, 18, in his quarters; he is highest-ranking officer convicted for what rights group say are routine abuses against civilians in Russia's war against Chechen rebels; was acquitted in first trial on temporary insanity grounds, but Supreme Court threw out verdict; is sentenced to 10 years in prison and stripped of rank and awards; officials announce discovery in village near Moscow of cache of five explosive devices like those used in recent wave of Chechen suicide bombings (M)
news.title: Russian Colonel Guilty of Murder in Death of Chechen Woman

news.abstract: Darko Darko Mrdja, Serbian policeman, pleads guilty in The Hague to taking part in notorious massacre of more than 200 prisoners of war in Bosnia on Aug 21, 1992; Serbian soldiers and police officer separate more than 200 men, mostly Croats and Muslims, from convoy of civilians, took their captives to wooded ravine, told them to kneel on edge of a cliff, and shot them (M)
news.title: In a Startling Plea, a Serbian Policeman Confesses to Atrocities

news.abstract: Mixed-race people in South Africa are still denied status as first-class citizens; one mixed-race South African says that under apartheid, they were not white enough, and that now they are not black enough; many mixed-race people of Cape Flats, where poverty and unemployment help push young men into violent street gangs and where life seems to have gotten harder since apartheid's end, say they feel there is no place for them in new South Africa; photos; map (M)
news.title: For Mixed-Race South Africans, Equity Is Elusive

news.abstract: The move came just hours before Prime Minister Ariel Sharon flew to the U.S., where he could face rare differences with President Bush on Mideast peacemaking.
news.title: Israeli Cabinet Agrees to Free 100 Militants and Lift Roadblocks

news.abstract: This weekend's unrest was only a caricature of the coups and popular putsches that have kept the country on edge for years.
news.title: Brief Standoff Is a Lesson in Philippine History

news.abstract: Cambodia is inching toward democracy, with 6.3 eligible voters set to cast ballots that are expected, by hook or by crook, to produce another five-year term for Prime Min Hun Sen; Hun Sun leaves campaigning to lesser figures, although he will open new schools and meet with admirers; civil society plays increasing role in national affairs; Hun Sen allows remarkably freewheeling press for self-described strongman; photos (M)
news.title: Inching Toward Democracy, Cambodia Again Visits Polls

news.abstract: No one was detained after the attack, the latest in a series of lethal and sophisticated strikes against American soldiers.
news.title: Soldier Killed and 3 Others Wounded in Baghdad Bombing

news.abstract: American soldiers fire on Toyota passenger car in upscale Baghdad neighborhood, killing at least three Iraqis, as American Special Operations team prepares to raid nearby house in what Iraqi policeman later describes as unsuccessful attempt to capture Saddam Hussein; owner of home that is raided claims he has not seen Hussein for more than year; shootings outrage local residents, who say Americans did not offer adequate warnings before firing on car; photo (M)
news.title: 3 Iraqis Killed as G.I.'s Set Up Raid in Hunt for Hussein

news.abstract: Latest brief mutiny in Philippines is mere caricature of coups and popular putsches that have kept country on edge for past 18 years; no shots are fired and no real threats are made by either side; in latest incident, band of 300 junior military officers and troopers barricade themselves inside apartment building in Manila for 18 hours, demanding resignation of president and defense secretary and better equipment for soldiers in field; they later give up and agree to return to barracks, but their passion is real and some of their grievances--corrupotion and mismanagement in military--seem justified; some past coup attempts recalled; photo (M)
news.title: Brief Mutiny Was Pale Shadow of Past Philippine Coups

news.abstract: Residents of village of El Quemado, Mex, are haunted by memories of what happened in Sept, 1972, when soldiers surounded their fields and summoned all male residents and accused them of having helped guerrillas stage ambush that left several soldiers dead; men were tortured and close to 50 of them were convicted of treason and sentenced to jail; 7 of them were never seen again; Pres Vicente Fox had promised to investigate this and other heinous atrocities, but Human Rights Watch has faulted him for not putting his full authority behind that effort; photos; map (M)
news.title: El Quemado Journal; A Mexican Village Mourns Its Abducted Sons

news.abstract: Japanese government officials win bitterly disputed parliamentary vote to send military force to Iraq, then set out to sell skeptical public on sending troops to area where they could find themselves in combat for first time since end of World War II (M)
news.title: Japan Courts a Public Wary Of Sending Its Troops to Iraq

news.abstract: Senators assailed officials today for failing to give projections on the length, cost and troop levels for the postwar effort.
news.title: Senators Assail Bush Aides for Lack of Data on Iraq's Future

news.abstract: Children of Russia's new rich, first generation to come of age after Communism, remember little or nothing of Soviet privations; many live life of royalty, with servants and expensive educations in foreign boarding schools; their parents came into their fortunes during Russia's property grab, few short years in 1990's; downside to instant fortunes amassed during time of economic chaos is that government occasionally threatens to take wealth away, as evidenced by Kremlin's recent attack on Russia's richest man, Mikhail B Khodorkovsky; photo (M)
news.title: Moscow Journal; Young, Russian, and Rich -- for Now at Least

news.abstract: New York-based Human Rights Watch report documents widespread extortion, armed robbery and kidnapping by police and intelligence officials and militias in Afghanistan, and accuses United States of supporting some of worst offenders; blames all countries for not doing enough to intervene and halt abuses; says perpetrators are people who came to power after US-led intervention that overthrew Taliban government in 2001; authors of report predict that warlords and abusive commanders would become more entrenched with time and could threaten success of Pres Hamid Karzai's government; report does not criticize Karzai; some diplomats and government officials contend that his indecisiveness and his policy of appeaseng powerful warlords to keep peace have kept many abusers in power (M)
news.title: Rights Group Reports Abuses by Afghans, Some Backed by U.S.

news.abstract: Magnus Gaefgen is sentenced to life in prison for abduction and murder of 11-year-old Jakob von Metzler, who was heir to one of Frankfurt's (Germany) oldest banking families (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: Bank Heir's Killer Jailed For Life

news.abstract: Bus bombing in Bombay (India) kills 2 people and injures 31 others; local authorities blame terrorist group (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: India: 2 Die In Bombay Bus Bomb

news.abstract: Article on netherworld of black economy in Thailand, where corruption is so thoroughly entwined in public life that, if it were pulled up by roots, society might fall apart; Chuwit Kamolvisit, who owns six industrial-sized massage parlors and is proud to be known as Thailand's sex tycoon, complains loudly that after paying millions in bribes, he is still accused of criminal activities, without protection he has paid for with 'whole trays of Rolex watches'; photo; most Thais, wealthy and poor, have close personal experience of police corruption, and illegal economy is as much as one-third size of mainstream legal economy (M)
news.title: Thai Vice King's Lament: Police Don't Stay Bought

news.abstract: John F Kennedy's Navy-issue boxer shorts are on display in Louis Copeland's Dublin shop window after Irish businessman Paul Allen purchased them online for $5,000; boxers, along with dress shirt of Kennedy's, will be sent to John F Kennedy Library and Museum in Boston; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Ireland: J.F.K.'S Boxers

news.abstract: American soldiers in Iraq conduct dozens of raids and seize more than 175 suspected Saddam Hussein loyalists in his hometown of Tikrit, in what military calls accelerating drive to flush him out of hiding; forces conduct 58 raids in 24 hours, garnering clues to Hussein's whereabouts; hunt coincides with new audiotape, apparently by Hussein, referring to deaths of sons Uday and Qusay; Iraqis seized include Hussein bodyguard Adnan Abdullah Abid al-Musslit and Tikrit security chief Daher Ziana; photo; map; Gen Richard B Myers warns Tikrit-Baghdad area is still 'war zone'; former Baghdad University dean Dr Muhammad Abdullah Falah Alrawi is shot to death in apparent revenge for his close links to Hussein; Iraqi Governing Council announces rotating chairmanship (M)
news.title: Pursuing Hussein, U.S. Captures 175 In Dozens of Raids

news.abstract: German news reports German female tourist has died of heat stroke while being held hostage in Sahara Desert; 13 other European tourists, who were with her and are believed to have been taken by Algerian Islamic militants, are still missing and thought to be held in Mali (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: Kidnapped Tourist Reported Dead

news.abstract: Village of Tolstopaltsevo, which is in wooded outskirts of Moscow and is where Russians go to escape city, is also where authorities have unearthed cache of explosives fashioned into suicide belts, apparently for use by Chechen terrorists; photo; map; undercurrents of tension and increased security patrols since bombing at rock 'n' roll festival described (M)
news.title: Russia Finds No Corner Is Safe From Chechnya's War

news.abstract: Senior North Korean official Kim Ryong Song announces Voice of National Salvation, North Korean propaganda radio station, will stop broadcasting after over 30 years of airing hostile messages targeted to South Korea (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: North Korea: End To Anti-South Broadcasts

news.abstract: British Court of Appeals rules two mothers must permit their daughters to be given controversial three-in-one vaccine for measles, mumps and rubella despite study possibly linking vaccine to autism; cases were brought by fathers of girls; court cites lack of evidence against vaccine and strong evidence supporting benefits of vaccinations (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: Mothers Lose Vaccine Appeal

news.abstract: Protests in Najaf over swearing in of city's first-ever female judge is emblematic of tension between American desire to leave imprint on levers of government in Iraq versus conservative religious establishment determined to fight what it sees as military invasion dragging Western cultural norms in behind its tanks; Lt Col Christopher C Conlin, senior commanding officer in Najaf, is confronted with three fatwas--religious fiats by senior clergy--against appointment of Nidal Nasser Hussein as judge; says he views appointment of judge as civil matter and had not even considered consulting relgious authorities about woman judge; decides to postpone her swearing in; photo (M)
news.title: In Najaf, Justice Can Be Blind but Not Female

news.abstract: The diplomat gave a speech in South Korea today lambasting Kim Jong Il as "a tyrannical dictator" who presides over a country that is a "hellish nightmare."
news.title: U.S. Arms Diplomat Denounces North Korean Leader

news.abstract: Dozens of former prisoners of war and deserters were left behind in Afghanistan from 10-year-long Soviet occupation of country in 1980's; Ukranian government has granted amnesty for all deserters and POW's of Afghan war, and promised apartment, pension and free health care for those who return home; one such former POW, Gennady Anatolevich Tsevma, now known as Nek Muhammad, would love to return home but has balked at doing so out of concern for his Afghani wife and children; photo; map (M)
news.title: A Stranger in Afghanistan, Too Torn to Go Home

news.abstract: French National Assembly mounts exhibit titled 'Mariannes of Today,' with photos of 13 women, eight of them North African Muslim and African immigrants, who have been chosen to reflect country's ideal face, or faces; since French Revolution, 'Marianne' has been idealized embodiment of freedom, supposedly immortal figure that gets new look occasionally; current display is part of government's campaign to make citizens of foreign origin, particularly Muslims, feel French; goal of other groups is to address problems of underclass women of tough, immigrant suburbs; photos (M)
news.title: Paris Journal; Back to Barricades: Liberty, Equality, Sisterhood

news.abstract: Explosion on road near Baghdad airport and shooting attack 50 miles northeast of capital kills two American soldiers and wounds five, ending rare two-day stretch of relative quiet in which no soldiers died; American administrator L Paul Bremer 3d reiterates that national elections could be held in Iraq as soon as one year from now; his military counterpart Lt Gen Ricardo S Sanchez says 'foreign fighters' have traveled to Iraq to fight American troops; suspects they are linked to Al Qaeda; takes pains to distance himself from recent claim by Deputy State Sec Richard Armitage and other American officials that American troops are closing in on Saddam Hussein; in Jordan, two of Hussein's three daughters arrive with their children after King Abdullah issues order admitting them on humanitarian grounds; their husbands were executed by their father in 1996; photo (M)
news.title: 2 G.I.'s Killed and 5 Wounded After Lull in Iraq Attacks

news.abstract: RUSSIA: Moscow Prosecutors Ousted; THE HAGUE: Life Sentence For Bosnian Serb; ITALY: Berlusconi Ally Returns; FRANCE: Riviera Fires Ease;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Israeli Parliament votes to block Palestinians who marry Israelis from becoming Israeli citizens or residents, erecting new legal barrier as Israel finishes first section of new physical barrier against West Bank Palestinians; supporters of bill call it necessary bulwark against infiltration by terrorists, as well as way to preserve Israel's Jewish majority; opponents call it racist measure that threatens to divide thousands of families or force them out of Israel; Israel's 1.2 million Arab citizens are far more likely than Israeli Jews to marry Palestinians; Israel solicits construction bids to build 22 new homes in settlement in Gaza Strip, even though new peace plan calls on Israel to freeze settlement construction; photo (M)
news.title: New Law Raises Obstacles to Israeli-Palestinian Marriages

news.abstract: Claudio Scajola, former Italian Cabinet member and ally of Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi, returns to Cabinet year after his inappropriate remarks forced his resignation (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Italy: Berlusconi Ally Returns

news.abstract: Middle East television stations broadcast new audiotape, apparently recorded by Saddam Hussein, in which almost desperately sounding voice urges Iraqis not to cooperate with American occupiers; US forces are attacked west of Baghdad; photo (S)
news.title: New Tape, Said to Be From Hussein, Urges Iraqis to Resist

news.abstract: Truck loaded with explosives blows up next to military hospital in Mozdok in southern Russia, killing at least 35 people and wounding dozens more; map; authorities blame Chechen separatists; bombing is latest in series of suicide attacks (M)
news.title: Truck Bombing at Russian Military Hospital Kills 35; Officials Blame Chechen Separatists

news.abstract: Sen John Warner, Republican chairman of Armed Services Committee, criticizes Bush administration for preparing plans to send US troops to Liberia without making convincing case to Congress, which is in recess; comments on Senate floor after Pentagon abruptly cancels detailed briefing; charges administration is not adhering to doctrine of spelling out risks and national interest involved; remarks by usually staunch Bush ally come as two of three Navy ships carrying 2,300 marines are set to arrive off Liberian coast (M)
news.title: G.O.P. Senator Criticizes Bush On Liberia Case

news.abstract: Metropolitan Museum's sumptuous exhibit of Mesopotamian antiquities includes Naram-Sin limestone fragment that was unknown until it surfaced in home of New York collector four years ago, illustrating ambiguous, often murky, world in which such objects are traded; debate becomes more pointed with recent looting in Iraq; photos of three objects in Met show, only one of which has clear provenance; museum director Philippe de Montebello says that even objects without clear records may come from legitimate sources, such as longstanding private collections; experts say including such objects abets illicit trade that destroys archaeological sites; unclear history of Naram-Sin fragment, involving collector Jonathan P Rosen, archaeologist Donald P Hansen and Met curator Joan Aruz, explained (M)
news.title: Ancient Art at Met Raises Old Ethical Questions

news.abstract: Rwandan court convicts 105 people for roles in mass killings of 1994 (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Rwanda: 105 Convicted In Ethnic Killings

news.abstract: Charles G Taylor says he will step down as president of Liberia in nine days, but refuses to save whether he will leave country, condition for any American military involvement in peacekeeping there; spokesman says question can be addressed only after lifting of war crimes indictment; West African officials say first of 1,500 Nigerian troops will still arrive on Aug 4; government forces begin their heaviest counterattack in days on rebels attacking Monrovia; photos (M)
news.title: Taylor Ready to Leave Office Aug. 11, but With a Condition

news.abstract: Two American soldiers and their interpreter are killed when homemade bomb explodes under their convoy on outskirts of Baghdad; grenade attack on convoy near Shumayt kills one US soldier and wounds three (S)
news.title: Americans Killed Near Baghdad

news.abstract: US and Japan fail to resolve differences on how to treat American military personnel suspected of serious crimes in Japan (M)
news.title: U.S. and Japan at Odds Over G.I. Prosecutions

news.abstract: Israelis enjoy three-month suspension of violence declared by Palestinian groups, but doubt if respite will last; peace plan is trying to reacquaint both Israelis and Palestinians about benefits of tranquillity to generate popular support for political concessions needed to sustain it; each day without terrorist attack is good for tourism; photos (M)
news.title: Israelis, and Visitors, Revel in a Summer of Calm

news.abstract: Yasir Arafat acts to put some 20 Palestinian militants under detention at his compound at Ramallah on West Bank, but detainees refuse to be sent to jail in Jericho, as demanded by Israel as condition for withdrawal of its troops from Ramallah; standoff reflects division between Arafat and Prime Min Mahmoud Abbas over how to handle negotiations with Israel (M)
news.title: Arafat Orders Militants Jailed, but They Balk

news.abstract: Religious courts run by upstart young clerics spring up in Najaf and Baghdad following disappearance of Saddam Hussein's government, with dockets covering all types of criminal and civil cases that normal courts would hear if they were functioning; Islamic court's decisions, which include permission to kill, could have dubious legality in regular court system, assuming it is restored; many aggrieved Iraqis, feeling they have no other place they can trust for legal rulings, are flocking to these courts; courts have no enforcement power and are not recognized by either American occupation forces or Iraq's other Muslim religious authorities; grand ayatollahs either deliberately ignore courts or say their decisons lack religious significance because no local senior cleric advises them; officials of regular court system, still trying to recover under American tutelage, expect religious courts inevitably to fade; photos (M)
news.title: With Iraqi Courts Gone, Young Clerics Judge

news.abstract: Palestinian officials back away from attempt to arrest Palestinian militants holed up in Yasir Arafat's West Bank compound; decision eases stalemate with militants, who refused to cooperate, but it prompts Israel to accuse governing Palestinian Authority of buckling to terrorists; most militants are members of Al Aksa Martyrs Brigades, violent offshoot of Arafat's mainstraem Fatah faction; Palestinian officials are urging Israel to pull its forces out of Ramallah and other West Bank cities, in compliance with international peace plan; Israel says Palestinian Authority must first comply with its own obligation under plan to begin collecting illegal weapons and take other steps against militants; photo (M)
news.title: Palestinians Allow Militants to Stay in Arafat's Compound

news.abstract: For the past few weeks, US President George W. Bush has been surrounded by a secretive circle of advisors and public relations experts, giving rise to all kinds of conspiracy theories and debates. It's been said that the group's idol is German Jewish philosopher Leo Strauss.
news.title: The Leo-conservatives

news.abstract: Chung Mong Hun, South Korean industrialist who was business driver behind South's policy of reconciliation toward North Korea, dies in fall from headquarters of his family company, Hyundai Asan, an apparent suicide; he faced trial on charges that he secretly passed $100 milion in money from South Korean government to North Korea in 2000, as way to ensure that Kim Jong Il would receive Kim Dae Jung, then president of South Korea; Chung made numerous trips to North to promote business projects with North; returned from his latest trip to North 10 days ago to learn that government prosecutors, operating independently of Pres Roh Moo Hyun, had placed travel ban on him; Chung, through his aides, said money sent to North Korea was payment for business dealings; photo (M)
news.title: Indicted Hyundai Executive Plunges to Death in Seoul

news.abstract: Foraging for food is too treacherous even for most daring Liberian civilians, as fighting between Pres Charles Taylor's loyalists and rebels seeking to overthrow him shower Monrovia with bullets and mortar shells; in country that can easily grow enough rice to feed itself, food supply is dwindling to dire levels, especially in government-held parts of capital; malnutrition in children is climbing; hospitals scramble to feed patients; civilians in Monrovia plug up their windows with cushions and pray for protection from stray bullets; capital has been pounded by rebel group for more than two weeks; it is demanding Taylor's ouster; he has promised to step aside, but has remained barricaded in his Executive Mansion; United Nations, United States government and West African heads of state have promised to help end bloodshed, but peacekeepers have yet to arrive; photos (M)
news.title: Food and Peace Just a Memory In Liberian City

news.abstract: The explosion seriously damaged the lower floors of the 33-floor hotel, killed at least 10 people and injured nearly 150.
news.title: Deadly Car Bombing Shakes Marriott Hotel in Jakarta

news.abstract: Defense Department releases names of three Americans killed in Iraq (S)
news.title: Killed in Iraq

news.abstract: Bush administration is considering reducing loan guarantees for Israel that were approved by Congress this spring in effort to press Israel to halt construction of barrier separating its citizens from Palestinians; any such punitive step would mark change in Pres Bush's longstanding efforts to avoid any kind of confrontation with government of Prime Min Ariel Sharon; Bush administration officials say they are being told by Palestinian leaders that barrier has cut Palestinians off from farms, homes, schools and workplaces; say Palestinians view barrier as de facto border for Israel in West Bank and Gaza Strip, even though future boundary of Israel and Palestinian state is supposed to be negotiated in talks between two sides; religious conservatives in Republican Party, including Rep Tom DeLay, suggest that Bush should not press Israel to adopt peace plan calling for Palestinian state (M)
news.title: U.S. May Reduce Aid Plan to Get Israel to Halt Barrier

news.abstract: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi, in interview with German newspaper Bild, says he has German work ethic; only last month Berlusconi said German member of European Parliament resembled concentration camp guard (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Italy: Herr Berlusconi

news.abstract: The Bush administration is considering a cut in $9 billion in loan guarantees for Israel as a way to press for a halt in construction of a barrier separating Israelis from Palestinians, administration officials said.    Article, Page A3.
news.title: U.S. Pressure on Israel

news.abstract: American civilian working in Iraq for Halliburton subsidiary KBR is killed when he drives mail truck over homemade bomb north of Tikrit; US forces carry out 25 raids and detain 141 people in hunt for Saddam Hussein (S)
news.title: U.S. Civilian Killed in Blast Near Tikrit

news.abstract: KENYA: Suspects Tied To Hotel Bombing; ZAMBIA: More Charges For Ex-Leader;.
news.title: World Briefing: Africa

news.abstract: Recent breakthrough in British investigation of murder of Nigerian child found headless and limbless in Thames River in 2001 brings new scrutiny to growth of child trafficking; riot police arrest 21 people in raids linked to investigation of child's death in apparent ritual sacrifice; children smuggled from Africa have turned up in several British cities (M)
news.title: Arrests in London Killing Linked to Child Trafficking

news.abstract: Tom Kelly, spokesman for Prime Min Tony Blair, issues unusual public apology for likening late weapons scientist David Kelly to Walter Mitty, fictional character who leads humdrum life but dreams of heroic deeds; latest dispute stemming from accuracy of intelligence data erupts day before funeral of Kelly, who apparently committed suicide after testifying at inquiry about reasons for going to war in Iraq (M),
news.title: Blair Aide Apologizes for Comment About Dead Arms Scientist

news.abstract: Pres Bush is expected to approve resumption of anti-drug surveillance flights in Colombia, including forcible grounding or destruction of planes suspected of smuggling narcotics (S)
news.title: U.S. Expected to Resume Patrols Over Colombia for Drug Flights

news.abstract: Arsonist Kim Dae Han, who set fire to South Korean subway train last February in Taegu killing 198 people and injuring 147, is sentenced to life in prison (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: South Korea: Life Term For Subway Arsonist

news.abstract: Iceland plans to reinstitute whaling for scientific research; government policy sets goal of killing 38 whales by end of next month; International Whaling Commission, which has passed resolution against research whaling, sees practice as cover for commercial gain (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Iceland: Whale Hunts To Resume

news.abstract: The bombing of the Jordanian embassy in Baghdad will not disrupt American military operations in Iraq, a high-ranking Pentagon official said today.
news.title: Pentagon Asserts Baghdad Bombing Won't Alter U.S. Tactics

news.abstract: The attack, which also wounded more than 60, was the most violent of several incidents in Baghdad in the past 24 hours.
news.title: At Least 11 Die in Car Bombing at Jordan's Embassy in Baghdad

news.abstract: An accused member of the Islamic militant group Jemaah Islamiyah is the first defendant to be convicted in the Bali case.
news.title: Man Receives Death Sentence for Bali Blasts That Killed 202

news.abstract: American federal agency, Commission on International Religious Freedom, calls off its visit to China to examine religious freedom after Chinese authorities impose what group calls 'unacceptable last-minute conditions' on trip, including pressure not to visit Hong Kong; visit had been subject of diplomatic negotiations for six months (M)
news.title: U.S. Panel on Religious Freedom Drops China Visit, Protesting Curbs

news.abstract: Shanghai Cooperation Organization, made up of China, Russia, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, and Uzbekistan, hold antiterrorism drill involving more than 1,000 troops (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: China: Antiterror Exercises

news.abstract: The involvement of the F.B.I. appeared to underline the concerns of American officials that the attack represents the work of organized terrorists.
news.title: F.B.I. to Lead Inquiry Into Embassy Bomb Attack in Iraq

news.abstract: The spiritual leader of the world's 79 million Anglican Christians will convene a meeting of Church leaders to try to avert a formal schism over the confirmation of a gay bishop.
news.title: Archbishop of Canterbury Acts to Prevent Rift on Gay Bishop

news.abstract: Chinese Vice Foreign Minister Wang Yi visits North Korea to exchange views in advance of next month's six-party meeting scheduled in Beijing; China is seeking to renegotiate mutual defense treaty (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: North Korea: Chinese Envoy Arrives

news.abstract: South African government, bowing to regional and international clamor for more vigorous attack on AIDS epidemic, says it will develop plan to offer drugs to combat HIV virus to infected people through its public health system by Oct 1; announces shift in drug policy after special meeting to assess financial costs of national drug plan and to explore treatment options; about 5 million South Africans, over 11 percent of population, are infected with HIV, including 20 percent of population aged 15 to 49; epidemic poses major threat to nation's future by primarily affecting young sexually active adults and incapacitating tradition extended family system that cares for sick and orphaned relatives; Pres Thabo Mbeki and his top aides have long resisted national drug programs; government is also expected to provide prevention programs; Bush administration lauds plan (M)
news.title: SOUTH AFRICA SAYS IT WILL FIGHT AIDS WITH A DRUG PLAN

news.abstract: Interview with Romano Prodi, who is set to begin final year of his five-year term as European Commission president; he stresses importance of European unity; expresses concern that United States understands neither value of united Europe nor difficulty in securing unity; photo (M)
news.title: A New European Keeps a Wary Eye on America

news.abstract: Three Palestinians, including two suspected gunmen from Islamic militant group Hamas, and Israeli soldier are killed in firefight and ensuing protest during what Israeli Army calls hunt for bomb makers in Nablus, West Bank; Hamas leaders threaten retaliation, but say they remain committed to cease-fire; incidents apparently do not reflect policy switch by either side; Hezbollah guerrillas from Lebanon shell Israeli military posts in occupied areas of Golan Heights, firing across Israel's northern border for first time since Jan; Israel responds using helicopter gunships and artillery; map; photo (M)
news.title: Mideast Calm Is Disrupted By Exchanges on 2 Fronts

news.abstract: Government reports Italy slid into recession for first time in 11 years, with gross domestic product falling 0.1 percent, Apr-June, same decline as in first quarter (S)
news.title: Italy Slides Into Recession

news.abstract: Government officials say Defense Intelligence Agency experts believe that most likely use for two mysterious trailers found in Iraq was to produce hydrogen for weather balloons used in artillery practice, not biological weapons; agency and Central Intelligence Agency officials say agencies still stand by their May 28 report that trailers were for making biological arms; it was not previously known that majority of Defense Intelligence Agency's engineering teams had come to disagree with that report; officials say teams had not completed work at time report was drafted and that their views were not taken into account at that time (M)
news.title: Iraqi Trailers Said To Make Hydrogen, Not Biological Arms

news.abstract: Thousands of deceased Chinese are being exhumed by their descendants and reburied in America, often in places they have never visited in life; descendants fear destruction of their ancestors' graves as cemeteries in China are bulldozed to make way for farms, offices and housing tracts; posthumous emigration reverses tradition that dates to gold rush, when Chinese-American would dig up laborers who had perished in California and ship them back to their ancestral villages; photo (M)
news.title: Displaced Chinese Ancestors Reburied in U.S.

news.abstract: Hutu rebels in Burundi, who for last few years have limited their fighting to rugged rural areas of country, are making bold incursions into heart of capital, Bujumbura; city's predominantly Tutsi residents are suddenly forced to confront fierce ethnic divisions that they thought were resolved by peace accord; photos; map (M)
news.title: Rebels Move Fighting Into Burundi's Capital

news.abstract: Italian drivers start obeying traffic signals and buckling seat belts in response to new point system that provides for revocation of license after certain number of offenses (M)
news.title: Tough New Point System Tames Some Wild Italian Drivers

news.abstract: Israel described its response to the attack as a limited mission against Hezbollah artillery positions.
news.title: Hezbollah Shelling Kills Teenager; Israel Strikes Back

news.abstract: German-language culture and religious traditions that Mennonites brought to Chaco region of Paraguay are threatened by influx of Spanish speakers who are drawn from other parts of Paraguay by healthy farming economy Mennonites have created; Mennonites, who first arrived in 1927, now make up less than half of population of Filadelfia in heart of Chaco; photo of Orlando Penner, Paraguay's first Mennonite senator, who says Mennonites should integrate more with other Paraguayans (M)
news.title: Paraguay Mennonites Find Success a Mixed Blessing

news.abstract: Port city of Yokusuka, Japan, commemorates 150th anniversary of arrival of Commodore Matthew C Perry, who forced Japan to open up to international trade and relations; this led to collapse of regime that had ruled feudal Japan in isolation and peace for more than two centuries, and then to modern Japan's scramble to catch up with West and grab Asian empire; historians say Perry has sunk into obscurity in United States, but he is most widely known foreign historic figure in Japan; photo of re-enactment of his landing (M)
news.title: Yokosuka Journal; Ripples From Perry's Ships Are Still Felt in Japan

news.abstract: Intelligence officers registered concern at the way the prime minister's government represented the threat from Iraq's weapons.
news.title: British Inquiry Opens Into the Suicide of Weapons Expert

news.abstract: Pres Charles G Taylor of Liberia, cornered by fierce, well-armed insurgency, promises to give up his office on Aug 11 and blames United States for his ouster; calls rebels 'surrogate force' of US in internationally televised farewell address; Liberians wonder how soon he will leave country, as rebel enemies have demanded, and whether rebels will cede control of Free Port of Monrovia, strategic prize of unsurpassed value that could either be country's gateway to fresh bloodshed or its portal to peace; Taylor has been offered asylum in Nigeria; White House has made his departure precondition for any direct American engagement in bringing peace to country after 14 years of on-and-off civil war; photos; map (M)
news.title: On Knife Edge, Liberia Awaits Taylor's Move

news.abstract: In its first mission beyond Europe's frontiers, NATO took formal control of Afghanistan's peacekeeping force today.
news.title: NATO Takes Over Peacekeeping Force in Afghanistan

news.abstract: Antitobacco movement is gaining ground in Western Europe; Ireland is expected to become first European country to ban smoking in pubs on Jan 1; move is so bold and contentious in country devoted to pub culture that few in Europe, and even fewer in Ireland, believe it will succeed; Norway and Netherlands have approved prohibitions on smoking in bars and restaurants that will take effect in future; France is close to approving law that would stiffen penalties on selling cigarettes to minors; question remains how vigorously new laws will be enforced; many European countries already have antismoking laws that are widely ignored; photo (M)
news.title: Glen to Glen, No Smoking At the Pub

news.abstract: Japan's Kyodo News reports Taiwan authorities have seized 40 tons of phosphoros pentasulfide, chemical that can be used to manufacture rocket fuel, from North Korean freighter (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Taiwan: Suspect Chemical Taken From North Korean Freighter

news.abstract: Moroccan-born Abdelghani Mzoudi goes on trial in Hamburg (Germany) for his part in Sept 11, 2001 terrorist attacks in New York and Washington; friend of Mohamed Atta, he is charged with 3,066 counts of abetting murder and terrorism; Moroccan Mounir el-Motassadeq, also part of Hamburg cell, is currently serving 15-year sentence for aiding in attacks (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: Second 9/11 Trial

news.abstract: At least 36 people in Qiqihar, China, have taken ill after unearthing mustard gas Chinese officials say was left behind by Japanese troops at end of World War II, straining Japanese-Chinese ties; visit by Japanese Foreign Ministry team to probe accident overshadows separate Japanese delegation sent to mark 25th anniversary of normalization of ties; bitter history is also complicating China's choice of Japanese or European technology for high-speed rail link between Shanghai and Beijing; tens of thousands of Chinese have signed Web-based petitions calling on government not to award $12 billion contract to Japan; leaders from both countries publicly try to play down divisions; map; photo (M)
news.title: Relic of War Adds to Strain In Beijing Ties With Tokyo

news.abstract: The attacks today inflicted the most serious blow yet to the American-led plan to find peace between Palestinians and Israelis.
news.title: 2 Suicide Bombings, One Claimed by Hamas, Kill 2 Israelis

news.abstract: NORTH KOREA: Talks Likely This Month; INDIA: 27 Feared Dead In Copter Crash; HONG KONG: Police Buy Riot Gear; TAIWAN: Suspect Chemical Taken From North Korean Freighter;.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: HOT, HOTTER, HOTTEST; BELGIUM: People Smugglers Sentenced;.

news.abstract: SOUTH KOREA: U.S. Officer Held After Body Found; SOUTH KOREA: U.S. Military Plane Crash Kills 2; NEPAL: Talks With Rebels To Resume; INDONESIA: 15-Year Term Sought For Cleric; CHINA: Mines Closed After Blast;.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: Record temperatures continue across Europe with Swiss canton Grisons reaching 106.7 degrees, hottest day in Switzerland's history; at least 100 heat related deaths in France, and 45 more in other parts of Europe, have been reported (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Hot, Hotter, Hottest

news.abstract: Serbia rejects calls for independence of United Nations-administered Kosovo province; adopts draft document proposing substantial autonomy, within federation of Serbia and Montenegro; says progress toward building multiethnic society in province has been unsatisfactory and marked with ethnic discrimination; Prime Min Zoran Zivkovic says non-Albanians, especially Serbs, face greater security risks there than ethnic-Albanians; Serbia calls for indictment of ethnic Albanians suspected of war crimes (M)
news.title: Proposal for Kosovo Autonomy Offered Instead of Independence

news.abstract: Two Palestinian teenagers blow themselves up in separate suicide bombings, killing two Israelis and inflicting new blow to fragile American-led plan to forge peace between Palestinians and Israeli; attacks jar Israelis after over month of relative calm; Al Aksa Martyrs Brigade claims responsibility for first attack, Rosh Haayin; Hamas claims responsibility for second, near entrance to Ariel, Jewish West Bank settlement; Prime Min Ariel Sharon again calls for Palestinian Authority to crack down on militants; has yet to launch military reprisal; White House spokeswoman echoes Sharon's call to disarm militants; State Sec Colin L Powell pledges attacks will not derail peace efforts; Hamas leaders deny its attack marks end to self-imposed cease-fire; call it retaliation for killing of two Hamas members in Israeli raid in Nablus; Palestinian Authority condemns attacks; blames Israel for violating terms of peace plan; photo (M)
news.title: 2 ISRAELIS KILLED IN SUICIDE ATTACKS BY ARAB BOMBERS

news.abstract: ARGENTINA: Legislators Back Amnesty Repeal; CHILE: General Strike;.
news.title: World Briefing: Americas

news.abstract: Lady Diana Mosley, who embraced fascism and admired Hitler, dies at age 93; was one of England's famous Mitford sisters; photo with her late husband, Sir Oswald Mosely, leader of British Union of Fascists (M)
news.title: Lady Diana Mosley, Fascist Who Dazzled, Is Dead at 93

news.abstract: British troops remain on edge in wake of riots that have shaken Basra, Iraq, for two days; 21 British soldiers are either stabbed or wounded by thrown bricks or rocks during riots; more unrest is feared if fuel supplies and electric service does not improve quickly; American soldier is killed and two others wounded by homemade bomb north of Baghdad; another soldier is killed and one wounded when their vehicle strikes homemade bomb south of Tikrit; photo; maps (M)
news.title: Officials Say Shortages Could Cause More Riots in Basra

news.abstract: GERMANY: Heat Wave Exposes Old Bombs; RUSSIA: North Korea Security Pact Proposed;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Chinese agriculture officials in Beijing are allowing farms to resume selling masked palm civets, species related to mongoose that may have been source of SARS virus; Chinese provinces retain discretion to bar human consumption of animals (S)
news.title: China Allows Sale of Animal Tied to SARS

news.abstract: Two former Montonero guerrilla leaders are arrested for ordering comrades to return from exile between 1976 and 1983 even though they knew they were likely to be captured, tortured and killed; Montonero leader Mario Firmenich is in Spain and may face extradition for his crimes (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Argentina: Leftists Arrested In 'Dirty War' Inquiry

news.abstract: There was an edge of apprehension that the blackout would last into the night on Thursday, but during the day, the mood in Toronto was calm and cooperative.
news.title: Toronto Calmly Copes but Fears the Night

news.abstract: United States military apologizes for incident that deeply angered Iraqi religious leaders, when soldiers in helicopter forced down flag near mosque in overwhelmingly Shiite district of Baghdad; flag episode outraged residents of Sadr City, poor but fervent Shiite neighborhood; large protest followed, leading to death of one Iraqi and wounding of four others by American troops (M)
news.title: U.S. Apologizes for Baghdad Mosque Incident

news.abstract: Bristol (England) government receptionists and security have been directed to eliminate use of dear or love in addressing public; they are instead advised by City Council leader Barbara Janke to use sir or madam; change has raised some controversy (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: No Love, Dears

news.abstract: Defense Dept confirms deaths of three American service members in Iraq (S)
news.title: Names of the Dead

news.abstract: Idi Amin's eight year reign of terror in Uganda encompassed widescale killing, torture and dispossession of multitudes and left the country pauperized.
news.title: Idi Amin, a Brutal Dictator of Uganda, Dies at 80

news.abstract: Tens of Thousands of Liberians burst through barricade that separated warring government and rebel forces in Monrovia after hearing that rebels have withdrawn from area; Monrovians who had been trapped by shelling and gunfire walk freely through city for first time in weeks; all are survivors of series of brutal battles in last three months, culmination of 14 years of fighting led in large part by Pres Charles G Taylor, who has stepped down; many Monrovians applaud arrival of United States marines, whose presence changed political climate overnight; first ship to arrive for more than month carries first relief shipment to Liberia since June; photo (M)
news.title: Liberians Cross Capital's Former Front Line as Aid Arrives

news.abstract: Polisario Front, Western Sahara rebel group fighting 30-year war for independence, announces release of 243 Moroccan prisoners after renewed request by Spanish President Jose Maria Aznar; United Nations Security Council has shown support for referendum on independent Western Sahara (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Morocco: Separatists To Release Prisoners

news.abstract: Malaria epidemic in Burundi from late 2000 to summer of 2001 generated 3 million cases in country of 6.5 million people; about 85 percent of people live in areas at risk of the disease, which preys on those who have not yet built up natural defenses, particularly children; rate of resistance to common malarial drugs is so high in Burundi that they are deemed ineffectual; increasingly, health experts are recommending combination treatment, called artemisinin, that comes from Chinese herb; it has been endorsed by World Health Orgn and United Nations Children's Fund and has been issued by Doctors Without Borders; treatment does nothing to stop spread of disease; first line of defense is keeping mosquito off human skin, no easy task in Africa; photo (M)
news.title: Herb Offers Hope to Africans Ravaged by Malaria

news.abstract: Prof Jagadish Shukla, Indian-American climatologist in Maryland, returns each year to home village of Mirda, in impoverished Uttar Pradesh, where he has used money earney in America to pay for relatives' education, marriages, homes and, in lean times, food; photos; Shukla is also setting aside ten percent of his income for more ambitious projects, such as community college and medical dispensary, that are bringing change to place where clock is still set by sun (M)
news.title: Professor Teaches Change in His Indian Village

news.abstract: Israeli and Palestinian commanders failed to reach an agreement Sunday night over the planned transfer of two West Bank cities to Palestinian control.
news.title: Talks Stall on the Security Transfer of 2 West Bank Cities

news.abstract: David W Chen article on return to father's hometown of Chen Dong in Fujian Province, China, for ceremony honoring his grandparents; photo; map; looks back on twenty generations of Chens who are chronicled in local genealogy, and describes lives of relatives today (M)
news.title: A China Odyssey Sheds Light on a Murky Past, and Hints at the Future

news.abstract: Women are increasingly filling baggy brown uniforms of North Korea's vaunted army, including many drafted for all-female units; analysts including Dr Alexandre Y Mansourov cite flight of population to China, famine and fact that many young men are ducking seven-year draft to try to make money in small businesses (M)
news.title: As North Korean Men Turn to Business, Women Join the Army

news.abstract: Iraqi athletes who bear physical or mental scars inflicted by Uday Hussein when he controlling Olympic Committee are helping rebuild athletic programs; Ahmed al-Samarrai, former coach of national basketball team who fled to Switzerland in 1983, now heads interim sports committee set up by US occupation to clear out old clubs and replace them with democratically elected groups; photo; Samarrai recalls torture and humiliation of training system that began in primary school (M)
news.title: Iraqi Athletes Scour Field of Nightmares
