news.title: Soros Raided in Moscow in Property Dispute

news.abstract: With the Army stretched thin by duties in Iraq and Afghanistan, some of the Old Guards troops were recently assigned to a new and unexpected mission.
news.title: Sending the Guard

news.abstract: Pres Vladimir V Putin, in heated news conference, emphasizes that arrest of Mikhail B Khodorkovsky, who owns giant Yukos Oil company, does not mean Russia would reverse its policies of private ownership; analysts and investors have been debating whether arrest signals broad crackdown or even rollback in privatization of state property in 1990's; Putin calls Khodorkovsky case 'isolated criminal matter'; notes high-ranking officials in Interior Ministry were arrested too; says aim is to instill law and order and fight corruption; Russian expert Prof Michael McFaul says targets of campaign are hustling entrepreneurs who seized much of Russia's natural resources during last decade; Khodorkovsky has angered Kremlin with his public activities, financing opposition parties and charitable foundations as well as academic institutions (M)
news.title: Putin Says Oilman's Arrest Is No Threat to Private Enterprise

news.abstract: SINGAPORE:—  Though his political nemesis has stepped aside to await history's judgment, Malaysia's former deputy prime minister, Anwar Ibrahim, remains in a tiny prison cell, awaiting his own shot at vindication.
news.title: Anwar Ibrahim's lawyers press his case : With Mahathir retired, ex-deputy may go free

news.abstract: Fernando Londono resigns as interior and justice minister of Colombia after making remarks disavowed by Pres Alvaro Uribe; Londono, with reputation for being outspoken and contentious, prompted nationwide consternation when he told Conservative Party congressmen that Uribe might quit and call early elections if they did not support his fiscal reforms (M)
news.title: Outspoken Minister Resigns in Clash With Colombia's President

news.abstract: Mideast commentators largely dismiss Pres Bush's speech calling for more democracy in region, viewing it as more for US domestic consumption (S)
news.title: Mideast View: Bush Spoke More to U.S. Than to Us

news.abstract: Six American soldiers are killed in Tikrit when Black Hawk helicopter crashes and burns in reeds along Tigris River, after reportedly exploding in midair; photos; Pentagon suspects Iraqi grenade attack; third such loss in two weeks poses problem for commanders who rely on relatively ungainly helicopters to transport troops and materiel across Iraq; 16 deaths in Chinook crash in Falluja is single deadliest attack on US forces since invasion; Black Hawk was ferrying troops from Mosul; second Black Hawk lands unscathed (M)
news.title: 6 AMERICANS DIE IN COPTER CRASH IN HUSSEIN'S CITY

news.abstract: Turkey, with quiet US agreement, withdraws offer to deploy troops to Iraq, ending Bush administration's almost entirely futile effort to bring in large foreign contingents; Iraq was once part of Ottoman Empire and suffered under Turkish rule; Kurds in north were particularly opposed (S)
news.title: With a U.S. Nod, Turkey Says It Won't Send Force to Iraq

news.abstract: CONGO REPUBLIC: Ebola Outbreak Suspected; ETHIOPIA: Rains Reduce Food Needs;.
news.title: World Briefing: Africa

news.abstract: Mauritania presidential election pits staunch American ally, Maaouya Ould Sid Ahmed Taya, against five opponents, including Muhammad Khouna Ould Haidalla, former president drawing support from Arab nationalists, Islamists and Baath Party loyalists; Taya government foiled recent Islamist coup; impoverished Islamic republic straddles Arab and black Africa (M)
news.title: Mauritania's Election Pits Staunch U.S. Ally Against 5 Opponents

news.abstract: CIA tells Congress that it now believes that North Korea has mastered technology of turning its nuclear fuel into functioning weapons, without having to prove their effectiveness through nuclear tests (M)
news.title: North Korea's Bomb: Untested but Ready, C.I.A. Concludes

news.abstract: The casualty toll leaped to 17 dead and 122 wounded in the attack in the Saudi capital that officials attributed to Al Qaeda.
news.title: Al Qaeda Blamed in Deadly Attack on Saudi Homes

news.title: Release of Berkeley Professor Is Delayed by Irans Judiciary

news.abstract: Sunday is Election Day, and a once reviled and now revived old dictator stands a chance of regaining power.
news.title: A Former Rulers Candidacy Revives Fears in Guatemala

news.abstract: Grief of families of 16 American soldiers killed in missile attack on their helicopter on Nov 2 is all the greater for some families because soldiers were on their way home after six months in Iraq; others are comforted by idea that soldiers' final hours were given over to cheerful anticipation of homecoming, not survival in combat; photo (M)
news.title: Lucky Break for Soldiers Heading Home From Iraq Turns to Heartbreak for Families

news.abstract: Bush administration wants to block group of American troops who were tortured in Iraqi prisons during Persian Gulf war in 1991 from collecting any of hundreds of millions of dollars in frozen Iraqi assets they won last summer in federal court ruling against government of Saddam Hussein; administration lawyers argue that frozen Iraqi assets in US banks are needed for Iraqi reconstruction and that judgment won by 17 former American prisoners should be overturned; administration is winning its court challenge so far but is not eager to publicize that fact; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Moves to Block Money For Troops Held in '91 War

news.abstract: For the past two weeks German soldiers have been securing northeastern Afghanistan, one of the biggest opium-growing areas in the world. But there they are safe only so long as they dont get in the way of the local chieftains and their booming drug trade. Orders to the troops are: Look the other way.
news.title: Poppies, Rocks, Shards of Trouble

news.abstract: In the nuclear poker game with the West, a third faction is exerting its influence in the power struggle between the right and the reformers: the pragmatic conservatives.
news.title: Fresh Blood in the Theocracy

news.abstract: American forces opened an assault against suspected Taliban forces in two northeastern provinces over the weekend.
news.title: U.S. Forces in Airborne Assault on Rebels in 2 Afghan Areas

news.abstract: Bush administration officials are shrugging off what some acknowledge to be series of mistakes in relations with Turkey since before war in Iraq; last Feb, Turkey rejected American appeals to allow American soldiers to go through Turkish territory to fight in northern Iraq, just few months after Deputy Defense Sec Paul D Wolfowitz claimed Turkish assent was 'assured'; supporters of Wolfowitz and supporters of Secretary of State Colin Powell blamed each other; now those recriminations are playing out again as Turkey decides not to send troops to help patrol Iraq (M)
news.title: U.S. Aides Acknowledge String of Missteps With Turkey

news.abstract: Israeli Health Ministry announces three babies have died and at least 17 more are seriously ill after receiving non-dairy baby formula made by German firm Humana; product did not contain needed vitamin B1, which was listed on label; product has been pulled from shelves and police have opened criminal investigation; company chief Rolf Janshen maintains product tested at plant contains B1 (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Middle East: Israel: Inquiry Into Baby Formula Deaths

news.abstract: Marking Veterans Day, President Bush said the people serving in Afghanistan and Iraq today are helping "democracy, peace and justice rise in a violent and troubled region."
news.title: Bush Links Efforts in Iraq and Afghanistan to U.S. Security

news.abstract: Israeli officials questioned the report and said the government was still assessing how many Palestinians would be affected.
news.title: Barrier Route Would Give Israel 15% of West Bank, U.N. Says

news.abstract: Hassan Rowhani, leader of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, visiting Russia, says Iran has halted its uranium-enrichment program and will sign protocol that will be safeguard against its development of nuclear arms; says Iran will agree to more intrusive International Atomic Energy Agency inspections on short notice; Russian Pres Vladimir V Putin, after meeting with Rowhani, says he sees no obstacles to cooperation on nuclear power plant Russians are building in Bushehr (S)
news.title: Russia Ready to Aid Iran With A-Plant

news.abstract: A top U.S. military official said today that Iraqis taking part in security jobs now outnumber American troops.
news.title: Iraqi Security Forces Outnumber American Troops, U.S. Says

news.abstract: Dany Ibrahim and Houry Haytayan, Lebanese couple living in Saudi Arabia, recall neighbor, also expecting first child, who was killed in terrorist bombing that destroyed their homes in Riyadh; photo; Saudi official reports arrest of some suspects; London-based Arabic newspaper publishes message from Al Qaeda operative claiming responsibility; threat of new attack keeps US Embassy closed (M)
news.title: Survivors of Riyadh Bombing Pick Up Pieces of Their Lives

news.abstract: German Amb Gunter Pleuger, who led UN Security Council mission to Afghanistan, reports that terrorism, drug-related crime and factional fighting threaten to reverse advances in rebuilding and efforts to form democratic government; comments follow car bombing outside UN office in Kandahar; Pleuger says Taliban, Al Qaeda and warlord Gulbuddin Hekmatyar pose 'significant threat' to national security forces (M)
news.title: Afghans' Political Prognosis Is Still Hazy, U.N. Panel Says

news.abstract: The commander of Colombias armed forces is resigning, joining three cabinet ministers who have stepped down in a shake-up marring President Álvaro Uribes administration.
news.title: Commander of Colombias Armed Forces Steps Down

news.abstract: Senate, 89-4, joins House in endorsing diplomatic and economic sanctions against Syria, unless government halts flow of fighters and weapons into Iraq (S)
news.title: Senate Follows House and Votes to Impose Sanctions Against Syria

news.abstract: Kenya overturns 1950's colonial-era legislation labeling members of Mau Mau movement as terrorists; Vice President Moody Awori praises group as brave in their defense of freedom (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Kenya: Mau Mau Group Recognized

news.abstract: Iraqi political leaders have decided a plan to write a new constitution would be too divisive now, and propose instead that they immediately assume the powers of a provisional government.
news.title: Iraqi Leaders Seek Power Before Drafting a Charter

news.abstract: Bush administration moves up its timetable for self-government in Iraq, concluding that increasing attacks on American and other foreign forces lend urgency to need for Iraqi self-rule by mid-2004; administration will try to hold elections in first half of next year and turn civilian authority over to temporary government before new constitution is written; new plan is intended to change political climate in Iraq and reduce anger toward occupying forces that fosters support for violence, by demonstrating to Iraqis that US is moving more quickly to establish self-rule; it is not clear whether those behind guerrilla attacks would regard changed political situation as significant if large numbers of American forces remain in Iraq; American administrator L Paul Bremer 3d, in Washington for high-level talks, heads back to Iraq to begin consultations about new American plan with Iraqi leaders, who have grown increasingly impatient with American-led occupation; members of Iraqi Governing Council say they will reject any plan to write new constitution in coming months because that would be too divisive; say they will propose instead that they immediately assume powers of provisional government (M)
news.title: U.S. Moves to Speed Up Iraqi Vote and Shift of Power

news.abstract: Iraqi political leaders reject plan to write new constitution in coming months, saying it would be too divisive now; they will propose instead that they immediately assume powers of provisional government; say they will work on drafting 'basic law' in hope that they can win international recognition for Iraqi government that would take over considerable authority from American administrator L Paul Bremer 3d and meet conditions laid down by United Nations Security Council last month; their push to establish provisional government reflects frustration with American-led organization overseeing Iraq (M)
news.title: Iraqi Leaders Seek Power Before Drafting a Charter

news.abstract: Car or truck bomb explodes in courtyard of Italian paramilitary police headquarters in Nasiriya, Iraq, killing 17 Italians and at least 9 Iraqis and wounding more than 105 others; it is most lethal single attack in series of attacks on Americans and other foreigners and Iraqis who support them since Saddam Hussein was swept from power in Apr; buildings were only lightly protected; hours after latest blast, American forces launch pair of ferocious strikes against suspected loyalists of Saddam Hussein's government in Baghdad, signaling new and more aggressive strategy; in Rome, Italian Defense Min Antonio Martino blames loyalists of Hussein for attack but presents no evidence to support his claim; Italian Prime Min Silvio Berlusconi says Italy would not be shaken from its commitment to Iraq and United States; photos of attack in Nasiriya, and of previous major bombings against foreign targets in Iraq (M)
news.title: At Least 26 Killed in a Bombing Of an Italian Compound in Iraq

news.abstract: Pres Mohammad Khatami says recent report on Iran's nuclear programs by International Atomic Energy Agency clears Iran of suspicions that it is developing nuclear weapons; adds that Tehran might end its voluntary cooperation if agency's next report, due Nov 20, bends to political pressures; IAEA report states that Iran's nuclear program goes back 18 years, much earlier than what Tehran claims; it also says Iran has produced small amounts of material, including plutonium, that could be made into weapons; report concludes that because of Iran's past pattern of concealment it would take some time before it could determine if its nuclear program is intended exclusively for peaceful purposes; in Washington, deputy undersecretary of state John R Bolton calls agency's finding that there is no immediate evidence Iran has nuclear weapons program 'impossible to believe' (M)
news.title: Iran's Leader Says U.N. Report Removes Suspicions of Weapons

news.abstract: It was the latest in a series of statements by officials and soldiers questioning Israels policy toward the Palestinians.
news.title: 4 Israeli Intelligence Experts Call for Political Solution

news.abstract: Bush administration decision to speed transfer of sovereignty to Iraqis and replace American troops with Iraqis draws warnings from Congress and policy experts against pulling out too early and allowing election-year politics dictate policy; Republican Sens Lindsey Graham and John McCain are among those expressing doubts (M)
news.title: In U.S., Fears Are Voiced Of a Too-Rapid Iraq Exit

news.abstract: GERMANY: Qaeda Suspect May Be Handed Over To U.S.; RUSSIA: Army Diet Found Lacking; SERBIA: Elections Called;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: List of Americans newly confirmed dead in Iraqï
news.title: Killed in Iraq

news.abstract: American commandersin Iraq say their well-publicized offensive against Iraqi insurgents is meant to send rebels 'a message'; at site of one strike in Baghdad, local Iraqis wonder what message is; owner of factory that was bombed says Americans warned guards to leave building before attack; American commanders say they were certain building had been used to fire mortars at American soldiers; commanders concede their primary aim was to impress guerrillas as much as to kill them; photo (M)
news.title: Air Raid Sends Iraqis Message, But What Is It?

news.abstract: PARIS:—  A bitter political fight has broken out at the pinnacle of the French literary world over whether Valéry Giscard d'Estaing, the former French president, is an acceptable choice for the Académie Française.
news.title: A political brawl rages at Académie Française

news.abstract: Georgian Pres Eduard A Shevardnadze calls for calm as thousands of protesters fill streets, surrounding presidential compound in Tiblisi and calling for his resignation; warns protests could spark civil war and rebuffs demands that he resign; protests began over manipulated parliamentary election on Nov 2 and have swelled into cry of anger over decade of mismanagement, during which country has slid into poverty and corruption; opposition leader Mikhail Saakashvili calls for campaign of civil disobedience, urging demonstrators to remain peaceful; map; photos (M)
news.title: President of Georgia Pleads For Calm as Protests Grow

news.abstract: German Environmental Ministry announces closure of first of nation's 19 nuclear power plants; all of plants are scheduled to be phased out over next two decades; 32-year-old plant in Stade is off-line and dismantling process is due to begin in 2005; France will reprocess spent nuclear fuel rods from facility (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: First Nuclear Plant Shut

news.abstract: Brig Gen Ahmed Ibrahim, Iraq's deputy interior minister and boss of national police, along with Baghdad police chief Hassan al-Obeidi, asks residents of Baghdad to help fight crime; say merchants should let them know if they see anything suspicious; very visible raids and patrols are being conducted to help foster sense of safety; photos (M)
news.title: Joy, and Jeers, As New Police Patrol Baghdad

news.abstract: Private schools are springing up in India, capitalizing on parental dismay over poor quality of government schools; quality is uneven, but schools are considered best choice and instruct in English; poor parents seek out private schools, certain that if they provide right education, children will rise above their circumstances; some say such expenditures by poor represent disgraceful abdication by state, one that creates class system segregating those with private education from those without and say such education should be free; some predict that within 10 to 15 years, government schooling will be eliminated; Indian law calls for free compulsory education for children up to 14, but does not address quality of government schools, which may lack power, latrines and even teachers, and do not teach in English, language considered vital for good future employment; photos (L)
news.title: India's Poor Bet Precious Sums on Private Schools

news.abstract: Officials in Mainz, Germany, are scrambling to avert what they fear could be economic blow to region as United States rethinks deployment of nearly 63,000 soldiers and their families in Rhineland-Palatinate, state of which Mainz is capital; bases put estimated $1.4 billion annually into economy and generate 27,000 jobs; with talk of base closings, delegation from Mainz travels to Pentagon to make pitch for troops to stay; such appeals are unlikely to carry much weight in light of Defense Sec Donald Rumsfeld's call for more agility and better strategic planning but move is not thought to be imminent, as resources are focused on Iraq; map (M)
news.title: German City Tries to Persuade Pentagon to Keep Bases Open

news.abstract: Profile of Tariq Ramadan, Swiss-born philosophy professor who touched off controversy last month when he criticized French Jewish intellectuals for supporting American-led war in Iraq; to Muslim followers in France, where he is attending conference, he is spiritual guide; to experts on Islam, he is respectable scholar who promotes moderate version of Islam from his headquarters in Geneva and in his lectures around world; but to some French intellectuals, he is dangerous demagogue whose words have multiple meanings and are laced with anger; Ramadan says he is misunderstood and denies being anti-Semitic, attributing campaign against him to his popularity; photo (M)
news.title: A Muslim Scholar Raises Hackles in France

news.abstract: Serbia will try to elect president for third time in about 14 months; post has been vacant for year but two previous elections were declared void because required minimum of electorate did not vote; six candidates are running, with Dragoljub Micunovic favored to win; coalition government has effectively collapsed and Parliament was recently dissolved, with new elections scheduled for Dec 28; photo (M)
news.title: Serbia Will Try, for a Third Time, to Elect a President

news.abstract: Defense Sec Donald Rumsfeld says it is urgent to resolve festering issue of defining legal rights for American military personnel in Japan suspected of violent crimes, especially rape and murder; talks on issue were disbanded in August; US wants guarantees that its troops will be protected by legal rights similar to those they would receive at home, but Japan balks at giving Americans more legal privileges than its own citizens (M)
news.title: Rumsfeld Presses Japan on U.S. Suspects' Rights

news.abstract: President Néstor Kirchner seems to be meeting stiff resistance as he tries to take on the countrys corrupt police force.
news.title: Argentine Moves Against Police Corruption

news.abstract: One more body was pulled from the rubble left by the attacks on two synagogues, raising the death toll to 24 people.
news.title: Turkish Police Expect to Identify 2 Suicide Bombers

news.abstract: During the Iraq war, Jessica Lynch became a symbol of a glorious military campaign. In her recently published book, she is portrayed as a country girl who naively stumbled into a foreign war. Now, once again, she is a symbol for Americas state of mind.
news.title: A real innocent

news.abstract: Elections in Catalonia leave minor nationalist party, Republican Left, holding key to control of regional parliament (S)
news.title: Catalan Voters Lean Left

news.abstract: The announcement came as Ariel Sharon, said that he might meet the Palestinian prime minister "in the next few days."
news.title: Palestinian Sides Agree to Cease-Fire Talks

news.abstract: Two Yemenis accused of funneling money to Al Qaeda been extradited to the U.S. from Germany to face criminal charges.
news.title: 2 Yemenis Tied to Al Qaeda Extradited by Germany to U.S.

news.abstract: Pres Bush says emphatically that United States will not leave Iraq even though White House has decided to speed transfer of American civilian authority to new government in Baghdad; comments are his most explicit to date about keeping American troops in Iraq, but he does not say how long they will stay, or how many will remain (S)
news.title: Bush Insists That U.S. Troops Will Stay in Iraq

news.abstract: Mexicos ambassador to the U.N. has been dismissed after saying the U.S. regards Mexico as a second-class country.
news.title: Mexicos Envoy to U.N. Is Fired After Criticizing U.S. Policy

news.abstract: Police and paramilitary squads in Zimbabwe are said to be seizing foreign money from tourists and moneychangers in effort to allay acute shortage of hard currency in country; reports in government-controlled press say foreign currency is being collected to buy gasoline for farm vehicles, but unidentified Zimbabwean claims government is buying fuel for its military as precaution against civil unrest (S)
news.title: We Welcome You To Lush Zimbabwe! Your Wallet, Please!

news.abstract: NAPLES—  Slow Food, one of the world's largest and most avant-garde alliances of food lovers, gathered more than 600 protesters of fast food from 36 countries on a recent weekend in Naples to assail blandness and to extol "eco-gastronomy," authentic food traditions and third world peasants.
news.title: Diversity at the table / A fight against blandness: The Brillat-Savarins of slow food: They're eating well and doing right

news.abstract: Turkey said today that the bombers who killed at least 25 people on Saturday were Turkish citizens with links to Al Qaeda.
news.title: Turkey Links Synagogue Bombers to Al Qaeda

news.abstract: Russian Orthodox Church Outside of Russia is holding first-ever talks in Russia to explore reuniting New York based group with Moscow Patriarchate (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Breakaway Church In Talks

news.abstract: Turkish officials reveal guidelines for Kurdish-language media, as part of Parliament's expanded rights program designed, in part, to satisfy European Union's list of reforms necessary for membership in group (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Turkey: Go-Ahead For Kurdish Broadcasts

news.abstract: United Nations Secretary General Kofi Annan begins yearly fund raising appeal, citing need for $3 billion in aid for 2004 to help address 21 of world's most serious crises; 2003 appeal has received just 66% of needed funds (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Annan Plea For Africa

news.abstract: Ahmed Qurei traveled to the Gaza Strip today in a bid to persuade Palestinian factions to halt attacks against Israel.
news.title: Palestinian Premier Starts Cease-Fire Bid

news.abstract: Bush administration officials say resurgence in Taliban activity and cross-border operation pose new threat to eastern and southern Afghanistan and new diplomatic challenge in American dealings with Pakistan; are hopeful that in time, American military operations will push Taliban back and that increase in economic assistance will pull people away from Taliban; say Pakistan has increased its military and security presence in Pakistani provinces bordering Afghanistan but much more is needed to prevent Taliban from using Pakistani territory as sanctuary and arms supply base (M)
news.title: Resurgent Taliban Threatens Afghan Stability, U.S. Says

news.abstract: Feeling among many Britons is that part of 'special relationship' between Britain and US based on shared language, history, culture and economy remains solid and enduring, but that political and diplomatic costs have become too high; Prime Min Tony Blair is gaining little at home from being pictured at Bush's side; Bush's presence serves to point up what divides two allies as well as what unites them; adding to British frustration is that there are no indications that Bush's visit will answer question about whether Blair's loyalty gains Britain any added consideration in Washington; photo (M)
news.title: Of Blair and Bush, and the Ties That Bind

news.abstract: Israel rejects criticism of barrier it is building in West Bank, in Pres Bush's speech in London; says says construction would proceed as planned (S)
news.title: Barrier to Stay, Israel Declares

news.abstract: Queen Elizabeth's state banquet for Pres Bush and wife Laura described (S)
news.title: For Bushes, French Wine And U.S. Tunes

news.abstract: PARIS:—  With his condemnation of the rise of a new anti-Semitism in France, and his promises to combat it, President Jacques Chirac has conceded that his country has a troubled place among the European nations where anti-Jewish outbursts and attacks have become an undeniable and embarrassing pattern.
news.title: Chirac's anti-Semitism fight

news.abstract: Weekly Standard, journal with close ties to Bush administration hawks, reports on highly classified Oct 27 memo from Douglas J Feith, under secretary of defense, to Senate intelligence committee, listing 50 points of raw intelligence that, according to Feith, points to operational link between Iraq and Al Qaeda; conservatives are seizing on report as evidence that Iraq did indeed pose real danger to US; government officials with knowledge of intelligence on Iraq say reports cited by Feith are authentic, but they are not new and some are not credible (M)
news.title: More Proof of Iraq-Qaeda Link, or Not?

news.abstract: Foreign governments warned of more attacks and groups apparently linked to Al Qaeda claimed responsibility.
news.title: Turkey Arrests Suspects in 2 Bomb Attacks in Istanbul

news.abstract: The envoy, Adolfo Aguilar Zinser, said the Bush administration had prodded the administration of Mexican President Vicente Fox to remove him.
news.title: Mexicos Ambassador to the U.N. Resigns

news.abstract: Election Commission of Georgia announces that supporters of Pres Eduard A Shevardnadze have won disputed parliamentary election, confirming result that has already sent thousands of protesters into streets; opposition leaders renew calls for unpopular president to step down(S)
news.title: Officials in Georgia Declare Shevardnadze Ballot Winner

news.abstract: Bettina Goislard, 29-year-old French refugee worker killed by suspected Taliban gunman, is buried in British Cemetery in Kabul, in accordance with her wishes to be buried in Afghanistan (S)
news.title: Slain Frenchwoman Buried in Afghanistan

news.abstract: Kurilovo Journal on young Russian soldier, Yevgeny Rodionov, whose death in Chechnya has made him national hero and unofficial saint, focus of minor cult; Rodionov is said to have been killed by Muslim rebels seven years ago, at age 19, because he refused to renounce his religion or remove cross around his neck; photos of his mother and icons of her son; map (M)
news.title: Kurilovo Journal; From Village Boy to Soldier, Martyr and, Many Say, Saint

news.abstract: Min Nicolas Sarkozy breaks France's cardinal rule against flaunting ambition and admits on television that he thinks about running for president; is by far nation's most popular minister, with approval rating far higher than Pres Jacques Chirac's; Prime Min Jean-Pierre Raffarin has steadily dropped in polls, fueling speculation that he may be replaced, perhaps by Sarkozy; Sarkozy, during broadcast, also says he favors moves to help raise Muslims out of poor suburban ghettos and give them place in French society; photo (M)
news.title: French Official Looks in His Mirror and Sees Future President

news.abstract: Iraqi insurgents use homemade multiple rocketlaunchers on donkey carts disguised as hay wagons to carry out what American officers call 'spectacular' strikes against heavily fortified targets, Baghdad; get close to heavily defended sites, including two hotels and Oil Ministry; critically wound American civilian in hotel attack; donkey cart is spotted and disarmed before it could detonate near Italian and Turkish embassies and Kurdish political party headquarters; another is disarmed near American military camp; attacks seem intended to have maximum psychological impact on city's increasingly fearful residents; photos (M)
news.title: Insurgents Use Rockets on Donkey Carts to Hit Sites in Iraqi Capital
Expat adviser : Dual options for health insurance

news.abstract: Indian Supreme Court suspends trial of 10 people accused of involvement in last year's Hindu-Muslim rioting that killed at least 1,000 Muslims; gives local Gujarat State court two weeks to justify why cases were not transferred out of region; trials have been criticized as unjust (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: India: Court Halts Riot Trial

news.abstract: American officials in Southeast Asia are bracing for new terrorist attacks as they gather new data on Jemaah Islamiyah, Indonesia-based radical Islamic group; they and Asian officials say group remains intact and is growing stronger despite arrests of some top leaders, interviews; say money and arms have flowed to group through Philippines, center for training and money laundering; see attacks most likely in Indonesia and Philippines, with Malaysia and Thailand lesser targets; cite new data gathered from interrogation of Taufik Rifki, group official seized in Oct in Mindanao, Philippines; photo (M)
news.title: Officials Fear New Attacks by Militants in Southeast Asia

news.abstract: Iraqi political leaders say they picked Rend Rahim Francke, Iraqi-American activist, as country's diplomatic representative in Washington; Iraq Foundation, which she helped create, has spent decade devising visions of democratic rule for Iraq and lobbying for war crimes trial of Saddam Hussein; she says her new job will be informal ambassadorship; her appointment reflects accelerating political developments in Iraq in past week since Bush administration said it would turn over control of nation to provisional government by June; Francke, who has not lived in Iraq full time since 1970's, became US citizen in 1987 but considers herself Iraqi citizen as well; photo (M)
news.title: Iraq Picks American as Ambassador to U.S.

news.abstract: People of small Iraqi village of Kifl, all Shiites repressed under Saddam Hussein's rule--relish their new freedom but complain that their expectations of aid and compensation, democracy and security, remain unmet; beneath outward peace runs undercurrent of need and grievance and simmering resentment that has not boiled over but easily could; village is still recovering from damage of major battle that took place eight months ago, as American forces advanced on Baghdad; 11 people from Kifl died, and more than dozen homes were destroyed; Kifl has recovered more quickly than many places in Iraq, in large part because it has not experienced continuing resistance that has brought new destruction elsewhere and hampered efforts to rebuild; there was no frenzied looting in Kifl, which has little of value; election was recently held to create administrative council with 20 seats; in Kifl, as in other parts of Iraq, freedom and democracy seem beside the point to people with little money in their pockets; photos; map (L)
news.title: Iraqi Town Relishes Freedom, But Resentment Runs Beneath

news.abstract: President Eduard A. Shevardnadze resigned today in the face of huge public protests over the corruption and economic collapse that have marked his 12-year rule.
news.title: Bowing to Opposition, Leader of Georgia Steps Down

news.abstract: American soldiers have been unable to snuff out continuing chaos and violence in Iraq; in Baghdad, missile hits civilian airplane, forcing it to make emergency landing; also in Baghdad, top Iraqi politician Abdel Aziz al-Hakim is attacked by mortar shell at mosque but he is not hurt; in Khan Bani Saad, north of Baghdad, suicide attackers explode huge bombs at police station, killing at least 14 people; continuing attacks on civilian flights that operate in Iraq may delay opening airport to civilian traffic, one of major markers for stability in country; photos (M)
news.title: Bombers Kill 14 in Iraq; Missile Hits Civilian Plane

news.abstract: Archaeologists unveil once huge network of narrow dark trenches in potato field in Ypres, Belgium, providing grim testimony to way millions of terrified young soldiers struggled to hold on to life in World War I; trenches have yielded partial remains and wartime artifacts of seven soldiers, including brass regimental badge and uniform fragments almost certainly belonging to 21-year-old British lance corporal killed in Battle of Passendale in 1917; Belgian archaeologists and British historians are engaged in race against time; their excavation work must end next year to make way for highway project; photos; map (M)
news.title: A Battlefield In Belgium Lifts a Curtain On the Past

news.abstract: Three American soldiers were killed in Iraq, military officials said, including two who came under attack in the northern city of Mosul. In Baquba, north of Baghdad, where at least five people were killed in a suicide bombing on Saturday, a soldier from the Fourth Infantry Division was killed by a roadside bomb.    Article, Page A10.
news.title: New Attacks in Iraq

news.abstract: Fatal clashes with shadowy enemy continue for American soldiers stationed in Afghanistan; guerrilla attacks have killed five American and four Afghan soldiers along border with Pakistan in last eight weeks; in series of strikes, pro-Taliban fighters launch missiles, plant mines and mount fierce ambushes against American forces within miles of Pakistan border, and then are seen retreating toward Pakistan; American officer notes difficulty for Pakistan of sealing off such mountainous terrain; battlefield is swath of dozens of miles of arid plateau in eastern Afghanistan, lined by hills and mountains to east and west; photos; map (M)
news.title: The Other Conflict Continues to Take a G.I. Toll

news.abstract: Georgia, the birthplace of Stalin, endured centuries of foreign domination. The Red Army forcibly made it a republic in 1921.
news.title: A Troubled Past

news.abstract: VIENNA—  Two years ago, I was hurrying through Vienna's cheerful, kitschy Christkindl Markt looking for something worth buying when I noticed a little wooden stall right under the giant Christmas tree in front of the Rathaus. The storefront was full of tiny wooden figures, angels, saints and crèche figurines. When I asked the price, I was startled by how expensive they were — until I took another look at the detailed, expressive faces, the soft, glowing colors.
news.title: Building a crèche set, one figurine at a time

news.abstract: PARIS—  Gastronomically, the holiday season suggests luxury, and France's traditional lineup of end-of-year splurges include silken foie gras, earthy black truffles, bittersweet chocolates and ethereal caviar. Of the four, caviar is without doubt the priciest, the most exotic, the rarest and one of the most difficult for the average consumer to evaluate. Yet few gastronomic joys can compete with the intense, momentary pleasure of the sparkling, silken, mouth-popping eggs of the rare sturgeon from the Caspian Sea.
news.title: Caviar: knowing your sevruga from beluga

news.abstract: Profile of Gen A M Hendropriyono, head of Indonesia's intelligence agency; Hendro, as he is known, alerted Indonesian leaders after Sept 11 that country was likely terrorist target, but says they ignored him and even denounced him as tool of Americans; says he feels vindicated now that political colleagues can no longer deny that terrorism is problem; has become important component of American campaign against terror and has helped Indonesia arrest scores of militants from Jemaah Islamiyah; photo (M)

news.abstract: Pres Bush says he expects Halliburton to repay $61 million if subsidiary Kellogg, Brown & Root is found to have overcharged Pentagon on contract to deliver fuel to Iraq; Halliburton charged government $2.27 a gallon for 56.6 million gallons of gas from Kuwait, price that was $1.09 more than another contractor; issue has become lightning rod because of Vice Pres Dick Cheney's connection to Halliburton; Democrats are charging Halliburton's role in Iraq reflects administration's willingness to do favors for friendly corporate interests; Bush also defends his choice of James A Baker III as envoy for talks with other nations about forgiving Iraq's debts; Baker's law firm Baker Botts, and investment firm Carlyle Group, where he is investment counselor, have business interests in Middle East (M)

news.abstract: Representatives of Iranian opposition group People's Mujahedeen, or Mujahedeen Khalq, appeal to Pentagon to overrule order by Iraqi Governing Council that would expel its members from Iraq by end of year, possibly to Iran; group maintained armed camps in Iraq under Saddam Hussein and is listed by US as terrorist organization, but has strong supporters in Pentagon who see it as pressure point on Iranian government; Iran has been trying to persuade Bush administration to hand over group and may move to expel members of Al Qaeda that it has in custody, although Bush administration rejects such exchange; none of group's members have been detained by US and they have been permitted to keep small weapons (M)

news.abstract: Maj Gen Raymond T Odierno, who commands operations in Saddam Hussein's home city of Tikrit, says American forces have dealt damaging blow to insurgency in pivotal region in past month by choking off much of guerrillas' financing and arms supplies; acknowledges that there are still challenges from suicide bombings; says Americans have captured several important insurgent financiers and seized money stashed across region to pay for weapons and attacks, including nearly $2 million in American currency in Samarra; photo (M)

news.title: Sharon's New Offer: A Compromise, a Threat or Both?

news.abstract: Explosion rocks natural gas field in Chongqing in southwestern China, killing at least 191 people as poisonous fumes spread into surrounding communities; high death toll and long lag in reporting accurate information raise possibility that accident resulted from poor safety procedures or faulty rescue operations, which are endemic in China's fast-growing economy; accident occurred when drillers apparently punctured highly pressurized store of natural gas and hydrogen sulfide, which can be lethal when inhaled; natural gas is high priority industry for China because of its energy needs, and also because authorities are eager to replace coal-burning furnaces with cleaner natural gas generators to fight air pollution which has reached hazardous levels in many major Chinese cities; photos; map (M)

news.title: Putin and His Political Allies Extend Power in Parliament

news.abstract: Top United Nations nuclear inspector Dr Mohamed ElBaradei says Libya's nuclear program is years away from producing nuclear weapons and that important pieces of equipment are now largely dismantled and stored in boxes; comments after visiting four previously undeclared sites in Libya where scientists had been working to perfect enrichment of uranium; he expresses surprise that Libya had acquired great deal of high-technology equipment needed to enrich uranium through black-market transactions that have yet to be disclosed; says existence of shadowy network of middlemen who circumvent national export controls proves that those controls are not working; ElBaradei, head of International Atomic Energy Agency, meets with Col Muammar el-Qaddafi; Libyan leader reiterates his pledge to rid country of illicit weapons; he has also pledged to begin immediate compliance with Nuclear Nonproliferation Treaty, especially by submitting to unannounced inspections of any site; photo (M)
news.title: LIBYA'S ATOM BID IN EARLY PHASES

news.abstract: Though authorities said the cause of the blast remained unclear, one witness said he saw a car swing into an alley next to the restaurant just before the explosion.
news.title: Blast Kills 5 at Restaurant as Rash of Bombings Hit Iraq

news.abstract: Lithuanian Constitutional Court rules that President Rolandas Paksas violated three articles of Constitution when he granted citizenship to Yuri Borisov, Russian arms dealer, thought to have ties to organized crime; Parliament has begun impeachment proceedings against Paksas (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Lithuania: Court Says President Violated Constitution

news.abstract: Philippines will deport Michael Ray and Jamil Daoud Mujahid, American brothers suspected of terrorist links; photo; Stubbs worked for Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory until 2000; Filipino authorities say Mujahid, convert to Islam, met with members of extremist groups Abu Sayyaf and Moro Islamic Liberation Front (M)
news.title: Philippines to Deport U.S. Brothers Held in Terror Inquiry

news.abstract: Letter from Europe on Russia's traditional ambivalence about being part of West, at time when European Union's plan to envelop former Soviet satellites leaves Russia on other side of elite club of democratic states; Russian consumers with money to spend delight in Western Europe's glitter, but money and goods have turned Moscow and other cities into oases of consumption in country still beset by poverty; photo; Pres Vladimir Putin's increasingly authoritarian, and popular, rule also reflects disenchantment with decade of democratic experiment; Putin himself says it will be up to new generation to see how relationship with European Union develops (M)
news.title: Russia and the Rich Western Neighbors: A Cold Peace

news.abstract: Israel reports that number of Jewish settlers in West Bank and Gaza increased 16 percent in last three years, to 236,381, about double number in 1993 when Oslo Accords were signed; Israeli helicopter fies missiles at car carrying senior Hamas figures and soldiers at Gaza checkpoint kill Palestinian suspected of planting bomb (S)
news.title: Israel Says Settlement Population Has Doubled Since '93
